PNLE1.question: Which is the primary goal of community health nursing?

choices.A: To support and supplement the efforts of the medical profession in the promotion of health and prevention of illness
choices.B: To enhance the capacity of individuals, families and communities to cope with their health needs
choices.C: To increase the productivity of the people by providing them with services that will increase their level of health
choices.D: To contribute to national development through promotion of family welfare, focusing particularly on mothers and children.

PNLE1.rationale: To enhance the capacity of individuals, families and communities to cope with their health needs

PNLE1.question: CHN is a community-based practice. Which best explains this statement?

choices.A: The service is provided in the natural environment of people.
choices.B: The nurse has to conduct community diagnosis to determine nursing needs and problems.
choices.C: The services are based on the available resources within the community.
choices.D: Priority setting is based on the magnitude of the health problems identified.

PNLE1.rationale: The nurse has to conduct community diagnosis to determine nursing needs and problems.

PNLE1.question: Population-focused nursing practice requires which of the following processes?
PNLE1.rationale: Community diagnosis. Population-focused nursing care means providing care based on the greater need of the majority of the population. The greater need is identified through community diagnosis.

PNLE1.question: R.A. 1054 is also known as the Occupational Health Act. Aside from number of employees, what other factor must be considered in determining the occupational health privileges to which the workers will be entitled?

choices.A: Type of occupation: agricultural, commercial, industrial
choices.B: Location of the workplace in relation to health facilities
choices.C: lassification of the business enterprise based on net profit
choices.D: Sex and age composition of employees

PNLE1.rationale: Location of the workplace in relation to health facilities. Based on R.A. 1054, an occupational nurse must be employed when there are 30 to 100 employees and the workplace is more than 1 km. away from the nearest health center.

PNLE1.question: A business firm must employ an occupational health nurse when it has at least how many employees?
PNLE1.rationale: 101. Again, this is based on R.A. 1054.

PNLE1.question: When the occupational health nurse employs ergonomic principles, she is performing which of her roles?
PNLE1.rationale: Environmental manager. Ergonomics is improving efficiency of workers by improving the worker’s environment through appropriately designed furniture, for example.

PNLE1.question: A garment factory does not have an occupational nurse. Who shall provide the occupational health needs of the factory workers?

choices.A: Occupational health nurse at the Provincial Health Office
choices.C: Public health nurse of the RHU of their municipality
choices.D: Rural sanitary inspector of the RHU of their municipality

PNLE1.rationale: Public health nurse of the RHU of their municipality. You’re right! This question is based on R.A.1054.

PNLE1.question: “Public health services are given free of charge.” Is this statement true or false?

choices.A: The statement is true; it is the responsibility of government to provide basic services.
choices.B: The statement is false; people pay indirectly for public health services.
choices.C: The statement may be true or false, depending on the specific service required.
choices.D: The statement may be true or false, depending on policies of the government concerned.

PNLE1.rationale: The statement is false; people pay indirectly for public health services. Community health services, including public health services, are pre-paid services, though taxation, for example.

PNLE1.question: According to C.E.Winslow, which of the following is the goal of Public Health?

choices.A: For people to attain their birthrights of health and longevity
choices.B: For promotion of health and prevention of disease
choices.C: For people to have access to basic health services
choices.D: For people to be organized in their health efforts

PNLE1.rationale: For people to attain their birthrights of health and longevity. According to Winslow, all public health efforts are for people to realize their birthrights of health and longevity.

PNLE1.question: We say that a Filipino has attained longevity when he is able to reach the average lifespan of Filipinos. What other statistic may be used to determine attainment of longevity?
PNLE1.rationale: Swaroop’s index. Swaroop’s index is the percentage of the deaths aged 50 years or older. Its inverse represents the percentage of untimely deaths (those who died younger than 50 years).

PNLE1.question: Which of the following is the most prominent feature of public health nursing?

choices.A: It involves providing home care to sick people who are not confined in the hospital.
choices.B: Services are provided free of charge to people within the catchment area.
choices.C: The public health nurse functions as part of a team providing a public health nursing services.
choices.D: Public health nursing focuses on preventive, not curative, services.

PNLE1.rationale: Public health nursing focuses on preventive, not curative, services.The catchment area in PHN consists of a residential community, many of whom are well individuals who have greater need for preventive rather than curative services.

PNLE1.question: According to Margaret Shetland, the philosophy of public health nursing is based on which of the following?

choices.B: The mandate of the state to protect the birthrights of its citizens
choices.C: Public health nursing as a specialized field of nursing
choices.D: The worth and dignity of man

PNLE1.rationale: The worth and dignity of man. This is a direct quote from Dr. Margaret Shetland’s statements on Public Health Nursing.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following is the mission of the Department of Health?

choices.B: Ensure the accessibility and quality of health care
choices.C: Improve the general health status of the population
choices.D: Health in the hands of the Filipino people by the year 2020

PNLE1.rationale: Ensure the accessibility and quality of health care

PNLE1.question: Region IV Hospital is classified as what level of facility?
PNLE1.rationale: Tertiary. Regional hospitals are tertiary facilities because they serve as training hospitals for the region.

PNLE1.question: Which is true of primary facilities?

choices.B: Their services are provided on an out-patient basis.
choices.C: They are training facilities for health professionals.
choices.D: community hospital is an example of this level of health facilities.

PNLE1.rationale: Their services are provided on an out-patient basis. Primary facilities government and non-government facilities that provide basic out-patient services.

PNLE1.question: Which is an example of the school nurse’s health care provider functions?

choices.A: Requesting for BCG from the RHU for school entrant immunization
choices.B: onducting random classroom inspection during a measles epidemic
choices.C: Taking remedial action on an accident hazard in the school playground
choices.D: Observing places in the school where pupils spend their free time

PNLE1.rationale: Conducting random classroom inspection during a measles epidemic. Random classroom inspection is assessment of pupils/students and teachers for signs of a health problem prevalent in the community.

PNLE1.question: When the nurse determines whether resources were maximized in implementing Ligtas Tigdas, she is evaluating
PNLE1.rationale: Efficiency. Efficiency is determining whether the goals were attained at the least possible cost.

PNLE1.question: You are a new B.S.N. graduate. You want to become a Public Health Nurse. Where will you apply?
PNLE1.rationale: Rural Health Unit. R.A. 7160 devolved basic health services to local government units (LGU’s ). The public health nurse is an employee of the LGU.

PNLE1.question: R.A. 7160 mandates devolution of basic services from the national government to local government units. Which of the following is the major goal of devolution?

choices.B: To allow greater autonomy to local government units
choices.C: To empower the people and promote their self-reliance
choices.D: To make basic services more accessible to the people

PNLE1.rationale: To empower the people and promote their self-reliance. People empowerment is the basic motivation behind devolution of basic services to LGU’s.

PNLE1.question: Who is the Chairman of the Municipal Health Board?
PNLE1.rationale: Mayor. The local executive serves as the chairman of the Municipal Health Board.

PNLE1.question: Which level of health facility is the usual point of entry of a client into the health care delivery system?
PNLE1.rationale: Primary. The entry of a person into the health care delivery system is usually through a consultation in out-patient services.

PNLE1.question: The public health nurse is the supervisor of rural health midwives. Which of the following is a supervisory function of the public health nurse?

choices.A: Referring cases or patients to the midwife
choices.B: Providing technical guidance to the midwife
choices.C: Providing nursing care to cases referred by the midwife
choices.D: Formulating and implementing training programs for midwives

PNLE1.rationale: Providing technical guidance to the midwife. The nurse provides technical guidance to the midwife in the care of clients, particularly in the implementation of management guidelines, as in Integrated Management of Childhood Illness.

PNLE1.question: One of the participants in a hilot training class asked you to whom she should refer a patient in labor who develops a complication. You will answer, to the
PNLE1.rationale: Municipal Health Officer. A public health nurse and rural health midwife can provide care during normal childbirth. A physician should attend to a woman with a complication during labor.

PNLE1.question: You are the public health nurse in a municipality with a total population of about 20,000. There are 3 rural health midwives among the RHU personnel. How many more midwife items will the RHU need?

choices.D: The RHU does not need any more midwife item.

PNLE1.rationale: 1. Each rural health midwife is given a population assignment of about 5,000.

PNLE1.question: If the RHU needs additional midwife items, you will submit the request for additional midwife items for approval to the
PNLE1.rationale: Municipal Health Board. As mandated by R.A. 7160, basic health services have been devolved from the national government to local government units.

PNLE1.question: As an epidemiologist, the nurse is responsible for reporting cases of notifiable diseases. What law mandates reporting of cases of notifiable diseases?
PNLE1.rationale: Act 3573. Act 3573, the Law on Reporting of Communicable Diseases, enacted in 1929, mandated the reporting of diseases listed in the law to the nearest health station.

PNLE1.question: According to Freeman and Heinrich, community health nursing is a developmental service. Which of the following best illustrates this statement?

choices.A: The community health nurse continuously develops himself personally and professionally.
choices.B: Health education and community organizing are necessary in providing community health services.
choices.C: ommunity health nursing is intended primarily for health promotion and prevention and treatment of disease.
choices.D: The goal of community health nursing is to provide nursing services to people in their own places of residence.

PNLE1.rationale: Health education and community organizing are necessary in providing community health services. The community health nurse develops the health capability of people through health education and community organizing activities.

PNLE1.question: Which disease was declared through Presidential Proclamation No. 4 as a target for eradication in the Philippines?
PNLE1.rationale: Measles. Presidential Proclamation No. 4 is on the Ligtas Tigdas Program.

PNLE1.question: The public health nurse is responsible for presenting the municipal health statistics using graphs and tables. To compare the frequency of the leading causes of mortality in the municipality, which graph will you prepare?
PNLE1.rationale: Bar. A bar graph is used to present comparison of values, a line graph for trends over time or age, a pie graph for population composition or distribution, and a scatter diagram for correlation of two variables.

PNLE1.question: Which step in community organizing involves training of potential leaders in the community?
PNLE1.rationale: Core group formation. In core group formation, the nurse is able to transfer the technology of community organizing to the potential or informal community leaders through a training program.

PNLE2.question: In which step are plans formulated for solving community problems?
PNLE2.rationale: Community organization. Community organization is the step when community assemblies take place. During the community assembly, the people may opt to formalize the community organization and make plans for community action to resolve a community health problem.

PNLE2.question: The public health nurse takes an active role in community participation. What is the primary goal of community organizing?

choices.A: To educate the people regarding community health problems
choices.B: To mobilize the people to resolve community health problems
choices.C: To maximize the community’s resources in dealing with health problems
choices.D: To maximize the community’s resources in dealing with health problems

PNLE2.rationale: To maximize the community’s resources in dealing with health problems. Community organizing is a developmental service, with the goal of developing the people’s self-reliance in dealing with community health problems. A, B and C are objectives of contributory objectives to this goal.

PNLE2.question: An indicator of success in community organizing is when people are able to

choices.A: Participate in community activities for the solution of a community problem
choices.B: Implement activities for the solution of the community problem
choices.C: Plan activities for the solution of the community problem
choices.D: Identify the health problem as a common concern

PNLE2.rationale: Participate in community activities for the solution of a community problem. Participation in community activities in resolving a community problem may be in any of the processes mentioned in the other choices.

PNLE2.question: Tertiary prevention is needed in which stage of the natural history of disease?
PNLE2.rationale: Terminal. Tertiary prevention involves rehabilitation, prevention of permanent disability and disability limitation appropriate for convalescents, the disabled, complicated cases and the terminally ill (those in the terminal stage of a disease)

PNLE2.question: Isolation of a child with measles belongs to what level of prevention?
PNLE2.rationale: Primary. The purpose of isolating a client with a communicable disease is to protect those who are not sick (specific disease prevention).

PNLE2.question: On the other hand, Operation Timbang is _____ prevention.
PNLE2.rationale: Secondary. Operation Timbang is done to identify members of the susceptible population who are malnourished. Its purpose is early diagnosis and, subsequently, prompt treatment.

PNLE2.question: Which type of family-nurse contact will provide you with the best opportunity to observe family dynamics?
PNLE2.rationale: Home visit. Dynamics of family relationships can best be observed in the family’s natural environment, which is the home.

PNLE2.question: The typology of family nursing problems is used in the statement of nursing diagnosis in the care of families. The youngest child of the de los Reyes family has been diagnosed as mentally retarded. This is classified as a:
PNLE2.rationale: Health deficit. Failure of a family member to develop according to what is expected, as in mental retardation, is a health deficit.

PNLE2.question: The de los Reyes couple have a 6-year old child entering school for the first time. The de los Reyes family has a:
PNLE2.rationale: Foreseeable crisis. Entry of the 6-year old into school is an anticipated period of unusual demand on the family.

PNLE2.question: Which of the following is an advantage of a home visit?

choices.A: It allows the nurse to provide nursing care to a greater number of people.
choices.B: It provides an opportunity to do first hand appraisal of the home situation.
choices.C: It allows sharing of experiences among people with similar health problems.
choices.D: It develops the family’s initiative in providing for health needs of its members.

PNLE2.rationale: It provides an opportunity to do first hand appraisal of the home situation.. Choice A is not correct since a home visit requires that the nurse spend so much time with the family. Choice C is an advantage of a group conference, while choice D is true of a clinic consultation.

PNLE2.question: Which is CONTRARY to the principles in planning a home visit?

choices.A: home visit should have a purpose or objective.
choices.B: The plan should revolve around family health needs.
choices.C: home visit should be conducted in the manner prescribed by the RHU.
choices.D: Planning of continuing care should involve a responsible family member.

PNLE2.rationale: A home visit should be conducted in the manner prescribed by the RHU.The home visit plan should be flexible and practical, depending on factors, such as the family’s needs and the resources available to the nurse and the family.

PNLE2.question: The PHN bag is an important tool in providing nursing care during a home visit. The most important principle of bag technique states that it

choices.B: Should minimize if not totally prevent the spread of infection.
choices.C: Should not overshadow concern for the patient and his family.
choices.D: May be done in a variety of ways depending on the home situation, etc.

PNLE2.rationale: Should minimize if not totally prevent the spread of infection. Bag technique is performed before and after handling a client in the home to prevent transmission of infection to and from the client.

PNLE2.question: To maintain the cleanliness of the bag and its contents, which of the following must the nurse do?

choices.A: Wash his/her hands before and after providing nursing care to the family members.
choices.B: In the care of family members, as much as possible, use only articles taken from the bag.
choices.C: Put on an apron to protect her uniform and fold it with the right side out before putting it back into the bag.
choices.D: t the end of the visit, fold the lining on which the bag was placed, ensuring that the contaminated side is on the outside.

PNLE2.rationale: Wash his/her hands before and after providing nursing care to the family members. Choice B goes against the idea of utilizing the family’s resources, which is encouraged in CHN. Choices C and D goes against the principle of asepsis of confining the contaminated surface of objects.

PNLE2.question: The public health nurse conducts a study on the factors contributing to the high mortality rate due to heart disease in the municipality where she works. Which branch of epidemiology does the nurse practice in this situation?
PNLE2.rationale: Analytical. Analytical epidemiology is the study of factors or determinants affecting the patterns of occurrence and distribution of disease in a community.

PNLE2.question: Which of the following is a function of epidemiology?

choices.A: Identifying the disease condition based on manifestations presented by a client
choices.B: etermining factors that contributed to the occurrence of pneumonia in a 3 year old
choices.C: etermining the efficacy of the antibiotic used in the treatment of the 3 year old client with pneumonia
choices.D: Evaluating the effectiveness of the implementation of the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness

PNLE2.rationale: Evaluating the effectiveness of the implementation of the Integrated Management of Childhood Illness. Epidemiology is used in the assessment of a community or evaluation of interventions in community health practice.

PNLE2.question: Which of the following is an epidemiologic function of the nurse during an epidemic?

choices.A: onducting assessment of suspected cases to detect the communicable disease
choices.B: Monitoring the condition of the cases affected by the communicable disease
choices.C: Participating in the investigation to determine the source of the epidemic
choices.D: Teaching the community on preventive measures against the disease

PNLE2.rationale: Participating in the investigation to determine the source of the epidemic. Epidemiology is the study of patterns of occurrence and distribution of disease in the community, as well as the factors that affect disease patterns. The purpose of an epidemiologic investigation is to identify the source of an epidemic, i.e., what brought about the epidemic.

PNLE2.question: The primary purpose of conducting an epidemiologic investigation is to

choices.A: elineate the etiology of the epidemic
choices.B: Encourage cooperation and support of the community
choices.C: Identify groups who are at risk of contracting the disease
choices.D: Identify geographical location of cases of the disease in the community

PNLE2.rationale: Delineate the etiology of the epidemic. Delineating the etiology of an epidemic is identifying its source.

PNLE2.question: Which is a characteristic of person-to-person propagated epidemics?

choices.A: There are more cases of the disease than expected.
choices.B: The disease must necessarily be transmitted through a vector.
choices.C: The spread of the disease can be attributed to a common vehicle.
choices.D: There is a gradual build up of cases before the epidemic becomes easily noticeable.

PNLE2.rationale: There is a gradual build up of cases before the epidemic becomes easily noticeable. A gradual or insidious onset of the epidemic is usually observable in person-to-person propagated epidemics.

PNLE2.question: In the investigation of an epidemic, you compare the present frequency of the disease with the usual frequency at this time of the year in this community. This is done during which stage of the investigation?
PNLE2.rationale: Establishing the epidemic. Establishing the epidemic is determining whether there is an epidemic or not. This is done by comparing the present number of cases with the usual number of cases of the disease at the same time of the year, as well as establishing the relatedness of the cases of the disease.

PNLE2.question: The number of cases of Dengue fever usually increases towards the end of the rainy season. This pattern of occurrence of Dengue fever is best described as
PNLE2.rationale: Cyclical variation. A cyclical variation is a periodic fluctuation in the number of cases of a disease in the community.

PNLE2.question: In the year 1980, the World Health Organization declared the Philippines, together with some other countries in the Western Pacific Region, “free” of which disease?
PNLE2.rationale: Small pox. The last documented case of Small pox was in 1977 at Somalia.

PNLE2.question: In the census of the Philippines in 1995, there were about 35,299,000 males and about 34,968,000 females. What is the sex ratio?
PNLE2.rationale: 100.94:100. Sex ratio is the number of males for every 100 females in the population.
Health programs are sustained according to the level of development of the community. Primary health care is essential health care that can be sustained in all stages of development of the community.

PNLE2.question: Primary health care is a total approach to community development. Which of the following is an indicator of success in the use of the primary health care approach?

choices.A: Health services are provided free of charge to individuals and families.
choices.B: Local officials are empowered as the major decision makers in matters of health.
choices.C: Health workers are able to provide care based on identified health needs of the people.
choices.D: Health programs are sustained according to the level of development of the community.

PNLE2.rationale: Yin. Yang is the male dominating, positive and masculine force.

PNLE2.question: Sputum examination is the major screening tool for pulmonary tuberculosis. Clients would sometimes get false negative results in this exam. This means that the test is not perfect in terms of which characteristic of a diagnostic examination?
PNLE2.rationale: Letter of Instruction No. 949. Letter of Instruction 949 was issued by then President Ferdinand Marcos, directing the formerly called Ministry of Health, now the Department of Health, to utilize Primary Health Care approach in planning and implementing health programs.

PNLE2.question: Use of appropriate technology requires knowledge of indigenous technology. Which medicinal herb is given for fever, headache and cough?
PNLE2.rationale: Cooperation between the PHN and public school teacher. Intersectoral linkages refer to working relationships between the health sector and other sectors involved in community development.

PNLE2.question: What law created the Philippine Institute of Traditional and Alternative Health Care?

PNLE3.question: Estimate the number of pregnant women who will be given tetanus toxoid during an immunization outreach activity in a barangay with a population of about 1,500.
PNLE3.rationale: 265. To estimate the number of pregnant women, multiply the total population by 3.5%.

PNLE3.question: To describe the sex composition of the population, which demographic tool may be used?

choices.D: ny of these may be used.

PNLE3.rationale: Any of these may be used. Sex ratio and sex proportion are used to determine the sex composition of a population. A population pyramid is used to present the composition of a population by age and sex.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following is a natality rate?
PNLE3.rationale: Crude birth rate. Natality means birth. A natality rate is a birth rate.

PNLE3.question: You are computing the crude death rate of your municipality, with a total population of about 18,000, for last year. There were 94 deaths. Among those who died, 20 died because of diseases of the heart and 32 were aged 50 years or older. What is the crude death rate?
PNLE3.rationale: 5.2/1,000. To compute crude death rate divide total number of deaths (94) by total population (18,000) and multiply by 1,000.

PNLE3.question: Which statistic can give the most accurate reflection of the health status of a community?
PNLE3.rationale: Survey. A survey, also called sample survey, is data gathering about a sample of the population.

PNLE3.question: In the past year, Barangay A had an average population of 1655. 46 babies were born in that year, 2 of whom died less than 4 weeks after they were born. There were 4 recorded stillbirths. What is the neonatal mortality rate?

PNLE3.question: Which statistic best reflects the nutritional status of a population?
PNLE3.rationale: Magnitude of the health problem. Magnitude of the problem refers to the percentage of the population affected by a health problem. The other choices are criteria considered in both family and community health care.

PNLE3.question: The Field Health Services and Information System (FHSIS) is the recording and reporting system in public health care in the Philippines. The Monthly Field Health Service Activity Report is a form used in which of the components of the FHSIS?

choices.D: Encouragement of couples to take family planning as a joint responsibility

PNLE3.rationale: 6 months. After 6 months, the baby’s nutrient needs, especially the baby’s iron requirement, can no longer be provided by mother’s milk alone.

PNLE3.question: A woman, 6 months pregnant, came to the center for consultation. Which of the following substances is contraindicated?
PNLE3.rationale: Retinol 200,000 I.U., 1 capsule. A capsule of Retinol 200,000 IU is given within 1 month after delivery. Potassium iodate is given during pregnancy; malunggay capsule is not routinely administered after delivery; and ferrous sulfate is taken for two months after delivery.

PNLE3.question: During prenatal consultation, a client asked you if she can have her delivery at home. After history taking and physical examination, you advised her against a home delivery. Which of the following findings disqualifies her for a home delivery?

choices.D: Her baby is in cephalic presentation.

PNLE3.rationale: Measles vaccine. Among the biologicals used in the Expanded Program on Immunization, measles vaccine and OPV are highly sensitive to heat, requiring storage in the freezer.

PNLE3.question: Inadequate intake by the pregnant woman of which vitamin may cause neural tube defects?
PNLE3.rationale: 4. While the unused portion of other biologicals in EPI may be given until the end of the day, only BCG is discarded 4 hours after reconstitution. This is why BCG immunization is scheduled only in the morning.

PNLE4.question: In immunizing school entrants with BCG, you are not obliged to secure parental consent. This is because of which legal document?
PNLE4.rationale: P.D. 996. Presidential Decree 996, enacted in 1976, made immunization in the EPI compulsory for children under 8 years of age. Hepatitis B vaccination was made compulsory for the same age group by R.A. 7846.

PNLE4.question: Which immunization produces a permanent scar?
PNLE4.rationale: BCG. BCG causes the formation of a superficial abscess, which begins 2 weeks after immunization. The abscess heals without treatment, with the formation of a permanent scar.

PNLE4.question: A 4-week old baby was brought to the health center for his first immunization. Which can be given to him?
PNLE4.rationale: Infant BCG. Infant BCG may be given at birth. All the other immunizations mentioned can be given at 6 weeks of age.

PNLE4.question: You will not give DPT 2 if the mother says that the infant had

choices.D: Local tenderness for 3 days after DPT 1.

PNLE4.rationale: Seizures a day after DPT 1. Seizures within 3 days after administration of DPT is an indication of hypersensitivity to pertussis vaccine, a component of DPT. This is considered a specific contraindication to subsequent doses of DPT.

PNLE4.question: A 2-month old infant was brought to the health center for immunization. During assessment, the infant’s temperature registered at 38.1°C. Which is the best course of action that you will take?

choices.A: Go on with the infant’s immunizations.
choices.B: Give Paracetamol and wait for his fever to subside.
choices.C: Refer the infant to the physician for further assessment.
choices.D: dvise the infant’s mother to bring him back for immunization when he is well.

PNLE4.rationale: Go on with the infant’s immunizations. In the EPI, fever up to 38.5°C is not a contraindication to immunization. Mild acute respiratory tract infection, simple diarrhea and malnutrition are not contraindications either.

PNLE4.question: A pregnant woman had just received her 4th dose of tetanus toxoid. Subsequently, her baby will have protection against tetanus for how long?
PNLE4.rationale: 1 year. The baby will have passive natural immunity by placental transfer of antibodies. The mother will have active artificial immunity lasting for about 10 years. 5 doses will give the mother lifetime protection.

PNLE4.question: A 4-month old infant was brought to the health center because of cough. Her respiratory rate is 42/minute. Using the Integrated Management of Child Illness (IMCI) guidelines of assessment, her breathing is considered
PNLE4.rationale: Normal. In IMCI, a respiratory rate of 50/minute or more is fast breathing for an infant aged 2 to 12 months.

PNLE4.question: Which of the following signs will indicate that a young child is suffering from severe pneumonia?
PNLE4.rationale: Chest indrawing. In IMCI, chest indrawing is used as the positive sign of dyspnea, indicating severe pneumonia.

PNLE4.question: Using IMCI guidelines, you classify a child as having severe pneumonia. What is the best management for the child?

choices.B: Refer him urgently to the hospital.
choices.C: Instruct the mother to increase fluid intake.
choices.D: Instruct the mother to continue breastfeeding.

PNLE4.rationale: Refer him urgently to the hospital. Severe pneumonia requires urgent referral to a hospital. Answers A, C and D are done for a client classified as having pneumonia.

PNLE4.question: A 5-month old infant was brought by his mother to the health center because of diarrhea occurring 4 to 5 times a day. His skin goes back slowly after a skin pinch and his eyes are sunken. Using the IMCI guidelines, you will classify this infant in which category?
PNLE4.rationale: Some dehydration. Using the assessment guidelines of IMCI, a child (2 months to 5 years old) with diarrhea is classified as having SOME DEHYDRATION if he shows 2 or more of the following signs: restless or irritable, sunken eyes, the skin goes back slow after a skin pinch.

PNLE4.question: Based on assessment, you classified a 3-month old infant with the chief complaint of diarrhea in the category of SOME DEHYDRATION. Based on IMCI management guidelines, which of the following will you do?

choices.A: ring the infant to the nearest facility where IV fluids can be given.
choices.B: Supervise the mother in giving 200 to 400 ml. of Oresol in 4 hours.
choices.C: Give the infant’s mother instructions on home management.
choices.D: Keep the infant in your health center for close observation.

PNLE4.rationale: Supervise the mother in giving 200 to 400 ml. of Oresol in 4 hours. In the IMCI management guidelines, SOME DEHYDRATION is treated with the administration of Oresol within a period of 4 hours. The amount of Oresol is best computed on the basis of the child’s weight (75 ml/kg body weight). If the weight is unknown, the amount of Oresol is based on the child’s age.

PNLE4.question: A mother is using Oresol in the management of diarrhea of her 3-year old child. She asked you what to do if her child vomits. You will tell her to

choices.A: ring the child to the nearest hospital for further assessment.
choices.B: ring the child to the health center for intravenous fluid therapy.
choices.C: ring the child to the health center for assessment by the physician.
choices.D: Let the child rest for 10 minutes then continue giving Oresol more slowly.

PNLE4.rationale: Let the child rest for 10 minutes then continue giving Oresol more slowly. If the child vomits persistently, that is, he vomits everything that he takes in, he has to be referred urgently to a hospital. Otherwise, vomiting is managed by letting the child rest for 10 minutes and then continuing with Oresol administration. Teach the mother to give Oresol more slowly.

PNLE4.question: A 1 ½ year old child was classified as having 3rd degree protein energy malnutrition, kwashiorkor. Which of the following signs will be most apparent in this child?
PNLE4.rationale: Edema. Edema, a major sign of kwashiorkor, is caused by decreased colloidal osmotic pressure of the blood brought about by hypoalbuminemia. Decreased blood albumin level is due a protein-deficient diet.

PNLE4.question: Assessment of a 2-year old child revealed “baggy pants”. Using the IMCI guidelines, how will you manage this child?

choices.A: Refer the child urgently to a hospital for confinement.
choices.B: oordinate with the social worker to enroll the child in a feeding program.
choices.C: Make a teaching plan for the mother, focusing on menu planning for her child.
choices.D: ssess and treat the child for health problems like infections and intestinal parasitism.

PNLE4.rationale: Refer the child urgently to a hospital for confinement. “Baggy pants” is a sign of severe marasmus. The best management is urgent referral to a hospital.

PNLE4.question: During the physical examination of a young child, what is the earliest sign of xerophthalmia that you may observe?
PNLE4.rationale: Conjunctival xerosis. The earliest sign of Vitamin A deficiency (xerophthalmia) is night blindness. However, this is a functional change, which is not observable during physical examination.The earliest visible lesion is conjunctival xerosis or dullness of the conjunctiva due to inadequate tear production.

PNLE4.question: To prevent xerophthalmia, young children are given Retinol capsule every 6 months. What is the dose given to preschoolers?
PNLE4.rationale: 200,000 IU. Preschoolers are given Retinol 200,000 IU every 6 months. 100,000 IU is given once to infants aged 6 to 12 months. The dose for pregnant women is 10,000 IU.

PNLE4.question: The major sign of iron deficiency anemia is pallor. What part is best examined for pallor?
PNLE4.rationale: Palms. The anatomic characteristics of the palms allow a reliable and convenient basis for examination for pallor.

PNLE4.question: Food fortification is one of the strategies to prevent micronutrient deficiency conditions. R.A. 8976 mandates fortification of certain food items. Which of the following is among these food items?
PNLE4.rationale: Sugar. R.A. 8976 mandates fortification of rice, wheat flour, sugar and cooking oil with Vitamin A, iron and/or iodine.

PNLE4.question: What is the best course of action when there is a measles epidemic in a nearby municipality?

choices.A: Give measles vaccine to babies aged 6 to 8 months.
choices.B: Give babies aged 6 to 11 months one dose of 100,000 I.U. of Retinol
choices.C: Instruct mothers to keep their babies at home to prevent disease transmission.
choices.D: Instruct mothers to feed their babies adequately to enhance their babies’ resistance.

PNLE4.rationale: Give measles vaccine to babies aged 6 to 8 months. Ordinarily, measles vaccine is given at 9 months of age. During an impending epidemic, however, one dose may be given to babies aged 6 to 8 months. The mother is instructed that the baby needs another dose when the baby is 9 months old.

PNLE4.question: A mother brought her daughter, 4 years old, to the RHU because of cough and colds. Following the IMCI assessment guide, which of the following is a danger sign that indicates the need for urgent referral to a hospital?
PNLE4.rationale: Inability to drink. A sick child aged 2 months to 5 years must be referred urgently to a hospital if he/she has one or more of the following signs: not able to feed or drink, vomits everything, convulsions, abnormally sleepy or difficult to awaken.

PNLE4.question: Management of a child with measles includes the administration of which of the following?

choices.C: Tetracycline eye ointment for corneal opacity
choices.D: Retinol capsule regardless of when the last dose was given

PNLE4.rationale: Retinol capsule regardless of when the last dose was given. An infant 6 to 12 months classified as a case of measles is given Retinol 100,000 IU; a child is given 200,000 IU regardless of when the last dose was given.

PNLE4.question: A mother brought her 10 month old infant for consultation because of fever, which started 4 days prior to consultation. To determine malaria risk, what will you do?

choices.C: Get a specimen for blood smear.
choices.D: sk if the fever is present everyday.

PNLE4.rationale: Ask where the family resides. Because malaria is endemic, the first question to determine malaria risk is where the client’s family resides. If the area of residence is not a known endemic area, ask if the child had traveled within the past 6 months, where he/she was brought and whether he/she stayed overnight in that area.

PNLE4.question: The following are strategies implemented by the Department of Health to prevent mosquito-borne diseases. Which of these is most effective in the control of Dengue fever?

choices.C: hemoprophylaxis of non-immune persons going to endemic areas
choices.D: Teaching people in endemic areas to use chemically treated mosquito nets

PNLE4.rationale: Destroying breeding places of mosquitoes. Aedes aegypti, the vector of Dengue fever, breeds in stagnant, clear water. Its feeding time is usually during the daytime. It has a cyclical pattern of occurrence, unlike malaria which is endemic in certain parts of the country.

PNLE4.question: Secondary prevention for malaria includes

choices.A: Planting of neem or eucalyptus trees
choices.B: Residual spraying of insecticides at night
choices.C: etermining whether a place is endemic or not
choices.D: Growing larva-eating fish in mosquito breeding places

PNLE4.rationale: Determining whether a place is endemic or not. This is diagnostic and therefore secondary level prevention. The other choices are for primary prevention.

PNLE4.question: Scotch tape swab is done to check for which intestinal parasite?
PNLE4.rationale: Pinworm. Pinworm ova are deposited around the anal orifice.

PNLE4.question: Which of the following signs indicates the need for sputum examination for AFB?
PNLE4.rationale: Cough for 3 weeks. A client is considered a PTB suspect when he has cough for 2 weeks or more, plus one or more of the following signs: fever for 1 month or more; chest pain lasting for 2 weeks or more not attributed to other conditions; progressive, unexplained weight loss; night sweats; and hemoptysis.

PNLE4.question: Which clients are considered targets for DOTS Category I?

choices.C: Relapses and failures of previous PTB treatment regimens
choices.D: lients diagnosed for the first time through a positive sputum exam

PNLE4.rationale: Clients diagnosed for the first time through a positive sputum exam. Category I is for new clients diagnosed by sputum examination and clients diagnosed to have a serious form of extrapulmonary tuberculosis, such as TB osteomyelitis.

PNLE4.question: To improve compliance to treatment, what innovation is being implemented in DOTS?

choices.A: Having the health worker follow up the client at home
choices.B: Having the health worker or a responsible family member monitor drug intake
choices.C: Having the patient come to the health center every month to get his medications
choices.D: Having a target list to check on whether the patient has collected his monthly supply of drugs

PNLE4.rationale: Having the health worker or a responsible family member monitor drug intake. Directly Observed Treatment Short Course is so-called because a treatment partner, preferably a health worker accessible to the client, monitors the client’s compliance to the treatment.

PNLE4.question: Diagnosis of leprosy is highly dependent on recognition of symptoms. Which of the following is an early sign of leprosy?
PNLE4.rationale: Thickened painful nerves. The lesion of leprosy is not macular. It is characterized by a change in skin color (either reddish or whitish) and loss of sensation, sweating and hair growth over the lesion. Inability to close the eyelids (lagophthalmos) and sinking of the nosebridge are late symptoms.

PNLE4.question: Which of the following clients should be classified as a case of multibacillary leprosy?

choices.A: 3 skin lesions, negative slit skin smear
choices.B: 3 skin lesions, positive slit skin smear
choices.C: 5 skin lesions, negative slit skin smear
choices.D: 5 skin lesions, positive slit skin smear

PNLE4.rationale: 5 skin lesions, positive slit skin smear. A multibacillary leprosy case is one who has a positive slit skin smear and at least 5 skin lesions.

PNLE5.question: In the Philippines, which condition is the most frequent cause of death associated with schistosomiasis?
PNLE5.rationale: Liver cirrhosis. The etiologic agent of schistosomiasis in the Philippines is Schistosoma japonicum, which affects the small intestine and the liver. Liver damage is a consequence of fibrotic reactions to schistosoma eggs in the liver.

PNLE5.question: What is the most effective way of controlling schistosomiasis in an endemic area?

choices.D: Use of protective footwear, such as rubber boots

PNLE5.rationale: Proper use of sanitary toilets. The ova of the parasite get out of the human body together with feces. Cutting the cycle at this stage is the most effective way of preventing the spread of the disease to susceptible hosts.

PNLE5.question: When residents obtain water from an artesian well in the neighborhood, the level of this approved type of water facility is
PNLE5.rationale: II. A communal faucet or water standpost is classified as Level II.

PNLE5.question: For prevention of hepatitis A, you decided to conduct health education activities. Which of the following is IRRELEVANT?

choices.A: Use of sterile syringes and needles
choices.B: Safe food preparation and food handling by vendors
choices.C: Proper disposal of human excreta and personal hygiene
choices.D: Immediate reporting of water pipe leaks and illegal water connections

PNLE5.rationale: Use of sterile syringes and needles. Hepatitis A is transmitted through the fecal oral route. Hepatitis B is transmitted through infected body secretions like blood and semen.

PNLE5.question: Which biological used in Expanded Program on Immunization (EPI) should NOT be stored in the freezer?
PNLE5.rationale: DPT. DPT is sensitive to freezing. The appropriate storage temperature of DPT is 2 to 8° C only. OPV and measles vaccine are highly sensitive to heat and require freezing. MMR is not an immunization in the Expanded Program on Immunization.

PNLE5.question: You will conduct outreach immunization in a barangay with a population of about 1500. Estimate the number of infants in the barangay.
PNLE5.rationale: 45. To estimate the number of infants, multiply total population by 3%.

PNLE5.question: In Integrated Management of Childhood Illness, severe conditions generally require urgent referral to a hospital. Which of the following severe conditions DOES NOT always require urgent referral to a hospital?
PNLE5.rationale: Severe dehydration. The order of priority in the management of severe dehydration is as follows: intravenous fluid therapy, referral to a facility where IV fluids can be initiated within 30 minutes, Oresol/nasogastric tube, Oresol/orem. When the foregoing measures are not possible or effective, tehn urgent referral to the hospital is done.

PNLE5.question: A client was diagnosed as having Dengue fever. You will say that there is slow capillary refill when the color of the nailbed that you pressed does not return within how many seconds?
PNLE5.rationale: 3. Adequate blood supply to the area allows the return of the color of the nailbed within 3 seconds.

PNLE5.question: A 3-year old child was brought by his mother to the health center because of fever of 4-day duration. The child had a positive tourniquet test result. In the absence of other signs, which is the most appropriate measure that the PHN may carry out to prevent Dengue shock syndrome?

choices.A: Insert an NGT and give fluids per NGT.
choices.B: Instruct the mother to give the child Oresol.
choices.C: Start the patient on intravenous fluids STAT.
choices.D: Refer the client to the physician for appropriate management.

PNLE5.rationale: Instruct the mother to give the child Oresol. Since the child does not manifest any other danger sign, maintenance of fluid balance and replacement of fluid loss may be done by giving the client Oresol.

PNLE5.question: The pathognomonic sign of measles is Koplik’s spot. You may see Koplik’s spot by inspecting the _____.
PNLE5.rationale: Buccal mucosa. Koplik’s spot may be seen on the mucosa of the mouth or the throat.

PNLE5.question: Among the following diseases, which is airborne?
PNLE5.rationale: Measles. Viral conjunctivitis is transmitted by direct or indirect contact with discharges from infected eyes. Acute poliomyelitis is spread through the fecal-oral route and contact with throat secretions, whereas diphtheria is through direct and indirect contact with respiratory secretions.

PNLE5.question: Among children aged 2 months to 3 years, the most prevalent form of meningitis is caused by which microorganism?
PNLE5.rationale: Hemophilus influenzae. Hemophilus meningitis is unusual over the age of 5 years. In developing countries, the peak incidence is in children less than 6 months of age. Morbillivirus is the etiology of measles. Streptococcus pneumoniae and Neisseria meningitidis may cause meningitis, but age distribution is not specific in young children.

PNLE5.question: Human beings are the major reservoir of malaria. Which of the following strategies in malaria control is based on this fact?
PNLE5.rationale: Zooprophylaxis. Zooprophylaxis is done by putting animals like cattle or dogs close to windows or doorways just before nightfall. The Anopheles mosquito takes his blood meal from the animal and goes back to its breeding place, thereby preventing infection of humans.

PNLE5.question: The use of larvivorous fish in malaria control is the basis for which strategy of malaria control?
PNLE5.rationale: Stream seeding. Stream seeding is done by putting tilapia fry in streams or other bodies of water identified as breeding places of the Anopheles mosquito

PNLE5.question: Mosquito-borne diseases are prevented mostly with the use of mosquito control measures. Which of the following is NOT appropriate for malaria control?

choices.A: Use of chemically treated mosquito nets
choices.B: Seeding of breeding places with larva-eating fish
choices.C: Destruction of breeding places of the mosquito vector
choices.D: Use of mosquito-repelling soaps, such as those with basil or citronella

PNLE5.rationale: Destruction of breeding places of the mosquito vector. Anopheles mosquitoes breed in slow-moving, clear water, such as mountain streams.

PNLE5.question: A 4-year old client was brought to the health center with the chief complaint of severe diarrhea and the passage of “rice water” stools. The client is most probably suffering from which condition?
PNLE5.rationale: Cholera. Passage of profuse watery stools is the major symptom of cholera. Both amebic and bacillary dysentery are characterized by the presence of blood and/or mucus in the stools. Giardiasis is characterized by fat malabsorption and, therefore, steatorrhea.

PNLE5.question: In the Philippines, which specie of schistosoma is endemic in certain regions?
PNLE5.rationale: S. japonicum. S. mansoni is found mostly in Africa and South America; S. haematobium in Africa and the Middle East; and S. malayensis only in peninsular Malaysia.

PNLE5.question: A 32-year old client came for consultation at the health center with the chief complaint of fever for a week. Accompanying symptoms were muscle pains and body malaise. A week after the start of fever, the client noted yellowish discoloration of his sclera. History showed that he waded in flood waters about 2 weeks before the onset of symptoms. Based on his history, which disease condition will you suspect?
PNLE5.rationale: Leptospirosis. Leptospirosis is transmitted through contact with the skin or mucous membrane with water or moist soil contaminated with urine of infected animals, like rats.

PNLE5.question: MWSS provides water to Manila and other cities in Metro Manila. This is an example of which level of water facility?
PNLE5.rationale: III. Waterworks systems, such as MWSS, are classified as level III.

PNLE5.question: You are the PHN in the city health center. A client underwent screening for AIDS using ELISA. His result was positive. What is the best course of action that you may take?

choices.A: Get a thorough history of the client, focusing on the practice of high risk behaviors.
choices.B: Ask the client to be accompanied by a significant person before revealing the result.
choices.C: Refer the client to the physician since he is the best person to reveal the result to the client.
choices.D: Refer the client for a supplementary test, such as Western blot, since the ELISA result may be false.

PNLE5.rationale: Refer the client for a supplementary test, such as Western blot, since the ELISA result may be false. A client having a reactive ELISA result must undergo a more specific test, such as Western blot. A negative supplementary test result means that the ELISA result was false and that, most probably, the client is not infected.

PNLE5.question: Which is the BEST control measure for AIDS?

choices.A: Being faithful to a single sexual partner
choices.B: Using a condom during each sexual contact
choices.C: Avoiding sexual contact with commercial sex workers
choices.D: Making sure that one’s sexual partner does not have signs of AIDS

PNLE5.rationale: Being faithful to a single sexual partner. Sexual fidelity rules out the possibility of getting the disease by sexual contact with another infected person. Transmission occurs mostly through sexual intercourse and exposure to blood or tissues.

PNLE5.question: The most frequent causes of death among clients with AIDS are opportunistic diseases. Which of the following opportunistic infections is characterized by tonsillopharyngitis?
PNLE5.rationale: Infectious mononucleosis. Cytomegalovirus disease is an acute viral disease characterized by fever, sore throat and lymphadenopathy.

PNLE5.question: To determine possible sources of sexually transmitted infections, which is the BEST method that may be undertaken by the public health nurse?
PNLE5.rationale: Contact tracing. Contact tracing is the most practical and reliable method of finding possible sources of person-to-person transmitted infections, such as sexually transmitted diseases.

PNLE5.question: Antiretroviral agents, such as AZT, are used in the management of AIDS. Which of the following is NOT an action expected of these drugs.

choices.A: They prolong the life of the client with AIDS.
choices.B: They reduce the risk of opportunistic infections
choices.C: They shorten the period of communicability of the disease.
choices.D: They are able to bring about a cure of the disease condition.

PNLE5.rationale: They are able to bring about a cure of the disease condition. There is no known treatment for AIDS. Antiretroviral agents reduce the risk of opportunistic infections and prolong life, but does not cure the underlying immunodeficiency.

PNLE5.question: A barangay had an outbreak of German measles. To prevent congenital rubella, what is the BEST advice that you can give to women in the first trimester of pregnancy in the barangay?

choices.A: Advice them on the signs of German measles.
choices.B: Avoid crowded places, such as markets and moviehouses.
choices.C: Consult at the health center where rubella vaccine may be given.
choices.D: Consult a physician who may give them rubella immunoglobulin.

PNLE5.rationale: Consult a physician who may give them rubella immunoglobulin. Rubella vaccine is made up of attenuated German measles viruses. This is contraindicated in pregnancy. Immune globulin, a specific prophylactic against German measles, may be given to pregnant women.

PNLE5.question: You were invited to be the resource person in a training class for food handlers. Which of the following would you emphasize regarding prevention of staphylococcal food poisoning?

choices.A: All cooking and eating utensils must be thoroughly washed.
choices.B: Food must be cooked properly to destroy staphylococcal microorganisms.
choices.C: Food handlers and food servers must have a negative stool examination result.
choices.D: Proper handwashing during food preparation is the best way of preventing the condition.

PNLE5.rationale: Proper handwashing during food preparation is the best way of preventing the condition. Symptoms of this food poisoning are due to staphylococcal enterotoxin, not the microorganisms themselves. Contamination is by food handling by persons with staphylococcal skin or eye infections.

PNLE5.question: In a mothers’ class, you discussed childhood diseases such as chicken pox. Which of the following statements about chicken pox is correct?

choices.A: The older one gets, the more susceptible he becomes to the complications of chicken pox.
choices.B: A single attack of chicken pox will prevent future episodes, including conditions such as shingles.
choices.C: To prevent an outbreak in the community, quarantine may be imposed by health authorities.
choices.D: Chicken pox vaccine is best given when there is an impending outbreak in the community.

PNLE5.rationale: The older one gets, the more susceptible he becomes to the complications of chicken pox. Chicken pox is usually more severe in adults than in children. Complications, such as pneumonia, are higher in incidence in adults.

PNLE5.question: Complications to infectious parotitis (mumps) may be serious in which type of clients?
PNLE5.rationale: Young adult males. Epididymitis and orchitis are possible complications of mumps. In post-adolescent males, bilateral inflammation of the testes and epididymis may cause sterility.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: The four major concepts in nursing theory are the
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Person, Environment, Nursing, Health. This is an actual board exam question and is a common board question. Theorist always describes The nursing profession by first defining what is NURSING, followed by the PERSON, ENVIRONMENT and HEALTH CONCEPT. The most popular theory was perhaps Nightingale’s. She defined nursing as the utilization of the persons environment to assist him towards recovery. She defined the person as somebody who has a reparative capabilities mediated and enhanced by factors in his environment. She describes the environment as something that would facilitate the person’s reparative process and identified different factors like sanitation, noise, etc. that affects a person’s reparative state.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: The act of utilizing the environment of the patient to assist him in his recovery is theorized by
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Nightingale. Florence nightingale do not believe in the germ theory, and perhaps this was her biggest mistake. Yet, her theory was the first in nursing. She believed that manipulation of environment that includes appropriate noise, nutrition, hygiene, light, comfort, sanitation etc. could provide the client’s body the nurturance it needs for repair and recovery.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: For her, Nursing is a theoretical system of knowledge that prescribes a process of analysis and action related to care of the ill person
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Roy. Remember the word “ THEOROYTICAL “ For Callista Roy, Nursing is a theoretical body of knowledge that prescribes analysis and action to care for an ill person. She introduced the ADAPTATION MODEL and viewed person as a BIOSPSYCHOSOCIAL BEING. She believed that by adaptation, Man can maintain homeostasis.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: According to her, Nursing is a helping or assistive profession to persons who are wholly or partly dependent or when those who are supposedly caring for them are no longer able to give care.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Orem. In self care deficit theory, Nursing is defined as A helping or assistive profession to person who are wholly or partly dependent or when people who are to give care to them are no longer available. Self care, are the activities that a person do for himself to maintain health, life and well being.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Nursing is a unique profession, Concerned with all the variables affecting an individual’s response to stressors, which are intra, inter and extra personal in nature.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Neuman. Neuman divided stressors as either intra, inter and extra personal in nature. She said that NURSING is concerned with eliminating these stressors to obtain a maximum level of wellness. The nurse helps the client through PRIMARY, SECONDARY AND TERTIARY prevention modes. Please do not confuse this with LEAVELL and CLARK’S level of prevention.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: The unique function of the nurse is to assist the individual, sick or well, in the performance of those activities contributing to health that he would perform unaided if he has the necessary strength, will and knowledge, and do this in such a way as to help him gain independence as rapidly as possible.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Henderson. This was an actual board question. Remember this definition and associate it with Virginia Henderson. Henderson also describes the NATURE OF NURSING theory. She identified 14 basic needs of the client. She describes nursing roles as SUBSTITUTIVE : Doing everything for the client, SUPPLEMENTARY : Helping the client and COMPLEMENTARY : Working with the client. Breathing normally, Eliminating waste, Eating and drinking adquately, Worship and Play are some of the basic needs according to her.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Caring is the essence and central unifying, a dominant domain that distinguishes nursing from other health disciplines. Care is an essential human need.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Leininger. There are many theorist that describes nursing as CARE. The most popular was JEAN WATSON’S Human Caring Model. But this question pertains to Leininger’s definition of caring. CUD I LIE IN GER? [ Could I Lie In There ] Is the Mnemonics I am using not to get confused. C stands for CENTRAL , U stands for UNIFYING, D stands for DOMINANT DOMAIN. I emphasize on this matter due to feedback on the last June 2006 batch about a question about CARING.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Caring involves 5 processes, KNOWING, BEING WITH, DOING FOR, ENABLING and MAINTAINING BELIEF.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Swanson . Caring according to Swanson involves 5 processes. Knowing means understanding the client. Being with emphasizes the Physical presence of the nurse for the patient. Doing for means doing things for the patient when he is incapable of doing it for himself. Enabling means helping client transcend maturational and developmental stressors in life while Maintaining belief is the ability of the Nurse to inculcate meaning to these events.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Caring is healing, it is communicated through the consciousness of the nurse to the individual being cared for. It allows access to higher human spirit.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Watson. The deepest and spiritual definition of Caring came from Jean watson. For her, Caring expands the limits of openess and allows access to higher human spirit.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Caring means that person, events, projects and things matter to people. It reveals stress and coping options. Caring creates responsibility. It is an inherent feature of nursing practice. It helps the nurse assist clients to recover in the face of the illness.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Benner.  I think of CARE BEAR to facilitate retainment of BENNER. As in, Care Benner. For her, Caring means being CONNECTED or making things matter to people. Caring according to Benner give meaning to illness and re establish connection.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Which of the following is NOT TRUE about profession according to Marie Jahoda?

choices.A: A profession is an organization of an occupational group based on the application of special knowledge
choices.B: It serves specific interest of a group
choices.D: Quality of work is of greater importance than the rewards

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: It serves specific interest of a group.Believe it or not, you should know the definition of profession according to Jahoda because it is asked in the Local boards. A profession should serve the WHOLE COMMUNITY and not just a specific intrest of a group. Everything else, are correct.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Which of the following is NOT an attribute of a professional?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Concerned with quantity. A professional is concerned with QUALITY and not QUANTITY. In nursing, We have methods of quality assurance and control to evaluate the effectiveness of nursing care. Nurses, are never concerned with QUANTITY of care provided.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: The most unique characteristic of nursing as a profession is
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Caring. Caring and caring alone, is the most unique quality of the Nursing Profession. It is the one the delineate Nursing from other professions.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: This is the distinctive individual qualities that differentiate a person to another
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Personality. Personality are qualities that make us different from each other. These are impressions that we made, or the footprints that we leave behind. This is the result of the integration of one’s talents, behavior, appearance, mood, character, morals and impulses into one harmonious whole. Philosophy is the basic truth that fuel our soul and give our life a purpose, it shapes the facets of a person’s character. Charm is to attract other people to be a change agent. Character is our moral values and belief that guides our actions in life.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Refers to the moral values and beliefs that are used as guides to personal behavior and actions
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Character.Rationale: Refer to number 14

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: As a nurse manager, which of the following best describes this function?

choices.C: Coordinates the activities of other members of the health team in managing patient care
choices.D: Provide in service education programs, Use accurate nursing audit, formulate philosophy and vision of the institution

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Provide in service education programs, Use accurate nursing audit, formulate philosophy and vision of the institution .  A refers to being a change agent. B is a role of a patient advocate. C is a case manager while D basically summarized functions of a nurse manager. If you haven’t read Lydia Venzon’s Book : NURSING MANAGEMENT TOWARDS QUALITY CARE, I suggest reading it in advance for your management subjects in the graduate school. Formulating philosophy and vision is in PLANNING. Nursing Audit is in CONTROLLING, In service education programs are included in DIRECTING. These are the processes of Nursing Management, I just forgot to add ORGANIZING which includes formulating an organizational structure and plans, Staffing and developing qualifications and job descriptions.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: What best describes nurses as a care provider?

choices.C: Help client recognize and cope with stressful psychological situation
choices.D: Works in combined effort with all those involved in patient’s care

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Determine client’s need.You can never provide nursing care if you don’t know what are the needs of the client. How can you provide an effective postural drainage if you do not know where is the bulk of the client’s secretion. Therefore, the best description of a care provider is the accurate and prompt determination of the client’s need to be able to render an appropriate nursing care.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: The nurse questions a doctors order of Morphine sulfate 50 mg, IM for a client with pancreatitis. Which role best fit that statement?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Client advocate. As a client’s advocate, Nurses are to protect the client’s right and promotes what is best for the client. Knowing that Morphine causes spasm of the sphincter of Oddi and will lead to further increase in the client’s pain, The nurse knew that the best treatment option for the client was not provided and intervene to provide the best possible care.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: These are nursing intervention that requires knowledge, skills and expertise of multiple health professionals.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Interdependent. Interdependent functions are those that needs expertise and skills of multiple health professionals. Example is when A child was diagnosed with nephrotic syndrome and the doctor ordered a high protein diet, Budek then work together with the dietician about the age appropriate high protein foods that can be given to the child, Including the preparation to entice the child into eating the food. NOTE : It is still debated if the diet in NS is low, moderate or high protein, In the U.S, Protein is never restricted and can be taken in moderate amount. As far as the local examination is concerned, answer LOW PROTEIN HIGH CALORIC DIET.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: What type of patient care model is the most common for student nurses and private duty nurses?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Total patient care. This is also known as case nursing. It is a method of nursing care wherein, one nurse is assigned to one patient for the delivery of total care. These are the method use by Nursing students, Private duty nurses and those in critical or isolation units.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: This is the best patient care model when there are many nurses but few patients.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Total patient care .Total patient care works best if there are many nurses but few patients.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: This patient care model works best when there are plenty of patient but few nurses
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Functional nursing. Functional nursing is task oriented, One nurse is assigned on a particular task leading to task expertise and efficiency. The nurse will work fast because the procedures are repetitive leading to task mastery. This care is not recommended as this leads fragmented nursing care.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: RN assumes 24 hour responsibility for the client to maintain continuity of care across shifts, days or visits.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Primary nursing. Your keyword in Primary nursing is the 24 hours. This does not necessarily means the nurse is awake for 24 hours, She can have a SECONDARY NURSES that will take care of the patient in shifts where she is not arround.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Who developed the first theory of nursing?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Nightingale .  Refer to question # 2. Hammurabi is the king of babylon that introduces the LEX TALIONES law, If you kill me, you should be killed… If you rob me, You should be robbed, An eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth. Alexander the great was the son of King Philip II and is from macedonia but he ruled Greece including Persia and Egypt. He is known to use a hammer to pierce a dying soldier’s medulla towards speedy death when he thinks that the soldier will die anyway, just to relieve their suffering. Fabiola was a beautiful roman matron who converted her house into a hospital.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: She introduces the NATURE OF NURSING MODEL.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Henderson. Refer to question # 6.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: She described the four conservation principle.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Levin. Myra Levin described the 4 Conservation principles which are concerned with the Unity and Integrity of an individual. These are ENERGY : Our output to facilitate meeting of our needs. STRUCTURAL INTEGRITY : We mus maintain the integrity of our organs, tissues and systems to be able to function and prevent harmful agents entering our body. PERSONAL INTEGRITY : These refers to our self esteem, self worth, self concept, identify and personality. SOCIAL INTEGRITY : Reflects our societal roles to our society, community, family, friends and fellow individuals.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Proposed the HEALTH CARE SYSTEM MODEL.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Neuman . Betty Neuman asserted that nursing is a unique profession and is concerned with all the variables affecting the individual’s response to stressors. These are INTRA or within ourselves, EXTRA or outside the individual, INTER means between two or more people. She proposed the HEALTH CARE SYSTEM MODEL which states that by PRIMARY, SECONDARY and TERTIARY prevention, The nurse can help the client maintain stability against these stressors.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Conceptualized the BEHAVIORAL SYSTEM MODEL
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Johnson. According to Dorothy Johnson, Each person is a behavioral system that is composed of 7 subsystems. Man adjust or adapt to stressors by a using a LEARNED PATTERN OF RESPONSE. Man uses his behavior to meet the demands of the environment, and is able to modified his behavior to support these demands.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Developed the CLINICAL NURSING – A HELPING ART MODEL
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Weidenbach.Just remember ERNESTINE WEIDENBACHLINICAL.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Developed the ROLE MODELING and MODELING theory
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Erickson,Tomlin,Swain

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Proposed the GRAND THEORY OF NURSING AS CARING
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Boykin,Schoenhofer . This theory was called GRAND THEORY because boykin and schoenofer thinks that ALL MAN ARE CARING, And that nursing is a response to this unique call. According to them, CARING IS A MORAL IMPERATIVE, meaning, ALL PEOPLE will tend to help a man who fell down the stairs even if he is not trained to do so.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Postulated the INTERPERSONAL ASPECT OF NURSING
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Travelbee. Travelbee’s theory was referred to as INTERPERSONAL theory because she postulated that NURSING is to assist the individual and all people that affects this individual to cope with illness, recover and FIND MEANING to this experience. For her, Nursing is a HUMAN TO HUMAN relationship that is formed during illness. To her, an individual is a UNIQUE and irreplaceable being in continuous process of becoming, evolving and changing. PLEASE do remember, that it is PARSE who postulated the theory of HUMAN BECOMING and not TRAVELBEE, for I read books that say it was TRAVELBEE and not PARSE.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: He proposed the theory of morality that is based on MUTUAL TRUST
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Kohlberg. Kohlber states that relationships are based on mutual trust. He postulated the levels of morality development. At the first stage called the PREMORAL or preconventional, A child do things and label them as BAD or GOOD depending on the PUNISHMENT or REWARD they get. They have no concept of justice, fairness and equity, for them, If I punch this kid and mom gets mad, thats WRONG. But if I dance and sing, mama smiles and give me a new toy, then I am doing something good. In the Conventional level, The individual actuates his act based on the response of the people around him. He will follow the rules, regulations, laws and morality the society upholds. If the law states that I should not resuscitate this man with a DNR order, then I would not. However, in the Post conventional level or the AUTONOMOUS level, the individual still follows the rules but can make a rule or bend part of these rules according to his own MORALITY. He can change the rules if he thinks that it is needed to be changed. Example is that, A nurse still continue resuscitating the client even if the client has a DNR order because he believes that the client can still recover and his mission is to save lives, not watch patients die.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: He proposed the theory of morality based on PRINCIPLES
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Peters . Remember PETERS for PRINCIPLES. P is to P. He believes that morality has 3 components : EMOTION or how one feels, JUDGEMENT or how one reason and BEHAVIOR or how one actuates his EMOTION and JUDGEMENT. He believes that MORALITY evolves with the development of PRINCPLES or the person’s vitrue and traits. He also believes in AUTOMATICITY of virtues or he calls HABIT, like kindness, charity, honesty, sincerity and thirft which are innate to a person and therfore, will be performed automatically.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Freud postulated that child adopts parental standards and traits through
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Identification. A child, according to Freud adopts parental standards, traits, habits and norms through identication. A good example is the corned beef commercial ” WALK LIKE A MAN, TALK LIKE A MAN ” Where the child identifies with his father by wearing the same clothes and doing the same thing.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: According to them, Morality is measured of how people treat human being and that a moral child strives to be kind and just
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Schulman and Mekler . According to Schulman and Mekler, there are 2 components that makes an action MORAL : The intention should be good and the Act must be just. A good example is ROBIN HOOD, His intention is GOOD but the act is UNJUST, which makes his action IMMORAL.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Postulated that FAITH is the way of behaving. He developed four theories of faith and development based on his experience.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Westerhoff. There are only 2 theorist of FAITH that might be asked in the board examinations. Fowler and Westerhoff. What differs them is that, FAITH of fowler is defined abstractly, Fowler defines faith as a FORCE that gives a meaning to a person’s life while Westerhoff defines faith as a behavior that continuously develops through time.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: He described the development of faith. He suggested that faith is a spiritual dimension that gives meaning to a persons life. Faith according to him, is a relational phenomenon.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Fowler. Rationale: Refer to # 37
