HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: She dies of yellow fever in her search for truth to prove that yellow fever is carried by a mosquitoes.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Clara louise Maas. Clara Louise Maas sacrificed her life in research of YELLOW FEVER. People during her time do not believe that yellow fever was brought by mosquitoes. To prove that they are wrong, She allowed herself to be bitten by the vector and after days, She died.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: He was called the father of sanitation.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Moses

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: The country where SHUSHURUTU originated
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: India

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: They put girls clothes on male infants to drive evil forces away
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Chinese. Chinese believes that male newborns are demon magnets. To fool those demons, they put female clothes to their male newborn.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: In what period of nursing does people believe in TREPHINING to drive evil forces away?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Intuitive period.Egyptians believe that a sick person is someone with an evil force or demon that is inside their heads. To release these evil spirits, They would tend to drill holes on the patient’s skull and it is called TREPHINING.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: This period ended when Pastor Fliedner, build Kaiserwerth institute for the training of Deaconesses
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Apprentice period.What dilineates apprentice period among others is that, it ENDED when formal schools were established. During the apprentice period, There is no formal educational institution for nurses. Most of them receive training inside the convent or church. Some of them are trained just for the purpose of nursing the wounded soldiers. But almost all of them are influenced by the christian faith to serve and nurse the sick. When Fliedner build the first formal school for nurses, It marked the end of the APPRENTICESHIP period.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Period of nursing where religious Christian orders emerged to take care of the sick
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Apprentice period. Apprentice period is marked by the emergence of religious orders the are devoted to religious life and the practice of nursing.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Founded the second order of St. Francis of Assisi
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: St. Clare. The poor clares, is the second order of St. Francis of assisi. The first order was founded by St. Francis himself. St. Catherine of Siena was the first lady with the lamp. St. Anne is the mother of mama mary. St. Elizabeth is the patron saint of Nursing.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: This period marked the religious upheaval of Luther, Who questions the Christian faith.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Dark period. Protestantism emerged with Martin Luther questions the Pope and Christianity. This started the Dark period of nursing when the christian faith was smeared by controversies. These leads to closure of some hospital and schools run by the church. Nursing became the work of prostitutes, slaves, mother and least desirable of women.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: According to the Biopsychosocial and spiritual theory of Sister Callista Roy, Man, As a SOCIAL being is
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Like some other men.According to ROY, Man as a social being is like some other man. As a spiritual being and Biologic being, Man are all alike. As a psychologic being, No man thinks alike. This basically summarized her BIOPSYHOSOCIAL theory which is included in our licensure exam coverage.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: She conceptualized that man, as an Open system is in constant interaction and transaction with a changing environment.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Roy. OPEN system theory is ROY. As an open system, man continuously allows input from the environment. Example is when you tell me Im good looking, I will be happy the entire day, Because I am an open system and continuously interact and transact with my environment. A close system is best exemplified by a CANDLE. When you cover the candle with a glass, it will die because it will eventually use all the oxygen it needs inside the glass for combustion. A closed system do not allow inputs and output in its environment.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: In a CLOSED system, which of the following is true?

choices.B: A sole island in vast ocean
choices.D: Constantly affected by matter, energy, information

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: A sole island in vast ocean

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Who postulated the WHOLISTIC concept that the totality is greater than sum of its parts?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Rogers. The wholistic theory by Martha Rogers states that MAN is greater than the sum of all its parts and that his dignity and worth will not be lessen even if one of this part is missing. A good example is ANNE BOLEYN, The mother of Queen Elizabeth and the wife of King Henry VIII. She was beheaded because Henry wants to mary another wife and that his divorce was not approved by the pope. Outraged, He insisted on the separation of the Church and State and divorce Anne himself by making everyone believe that Anne is having an affair to another man. Anne was beheaded while her lips is still saying a prayer. Even without her head, People still gave respect to her diseased body and a separate head. She was still remembered as Anne boleyn, Mother of Elizabeth who lead england to their GOLDEN AGE.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: She theorized that man is composed of sub and supra systems. Subsystems are cells, tissues, organs and systems while the suprasystems are family, society and community.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Rogers. According to Martha Rogers, Man is composed of 2 systems : SUB which includes cells, tissues, organs and system and SUPRA which includes our famly, community and society. She stated that when any of these systems are affected, it will affect the entire individual.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Which of the following is not true about the human needs?

choices.A: Certain needs are common to all people
choices.B: Needs should be followed exactly in accordance with their hierarchy
choices.C: Needs are stimulated by internal factors
choices.D: Needs are stimulated by external factors

I can save my money that are supposedly for my lunch to watch my idols in concert. The physiologic needs can be meet later for some other needs and need not be strictly followed according to their hierarchy.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Defines health as the ability to maintain internal milieu. Illness according to him/her/them is the failure to maintain internal environment.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Bernard. According to Bernard, Health is the ability to maintain and Internal Milieu and Illness is the failure to maintain the internal environment.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Postulated that health is a state and process of being and becoming an integrated and whole person.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Roy. According to ROY, Health is a state and process of becoming a WHOLE AND INTEGRATED Person.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: What regulates HOMEOSTASIS according to the theory of Walter Cannon?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Negative feedback. The theory of Health as the ability to maintain homeostasis was postulated by Walter Cannon. PAIN is a negative feedback that signals us that our arm needs a rest.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Stated that health is WELLNESS. A termed define by the culture or an individual.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Rogers. Martha Rogers states that HEALTH is synonymous with WELLNESS and that HEALTH and WELLNESS is subjective depending on the definition of one’s culture.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Defined health as a dynamic state in the life cycle, and Illness as interference in the life cycle.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: King .Emogene King states that health is a state in the life cycle and Illness is any interference on this cycle. I enjoyed the Movie LION KING and like what Mufasa said that they are all part of the CIRCLE OF LIFE, or the Life cycle.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: She defined health as the soundness and wholness of developed human structure and bodily mental functioning.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Orem. Orem defined health as the SOUNDNESS and WHOLENESS of developed human structure and of bodily and mental functioning.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: According to her, Wellness is a condition in which all parts and subparts of an individual are in harmony with the whole system.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Neuman. Neuman believe that man is composed of subparts and when this subparts are in harmony with the whole system, Wellness results. Please do not confuse this with the SUB and SUPRA systems of martha rogers.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Postulated that health is reflected by the organization, interaction, interdependence and integration of the subsystem of the behavioral system.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Johnson . Once you see the phrase BEHAVIORAL SYSTEM, answer Dorothy Johnson.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: According to them, Well being is a subjective perception of BALANCE, HARMONY and VITALITY
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Leddy and Pepper .According to Leddy and Pepper, Wellness is subjective and depends on an individuals perception of balance, harmony and vitality. Leavell and Clark postulared the ecologic model of health and illness or the AGENT-HOST-ENVIRONMENT model. Peterson and Zderad developed the HUMANISTIC NURSING PRACTICE theory while Benner and Wruber postulate the PRIMACY OF CARING MODEL.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: He describes the WELLNESS-ILLNESS Continuum as interaction of the environment with well being and illness.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Dunn

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: An integrated method of functioning that is oriented towards maximizing one’s potential within the limitation of the environment.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: High level Wellness

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: What kind of illness precursor, according to DUNN is cigarette smoking?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Behavioral. Behavioral precursors includes smoking, alcoholism, high fat intake and other lifestyle choices. Environmental factors involved poor sanitation and over crowding. Heridity includes congenital and diseases acquired through the genes. There are no social precursors according to DUNN.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: According to DUNN, Overcrowding is what type of illness precursor?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Environmental

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Health belief model was formulated in 1975 by who?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Becker. According to Becker, The belief of an individual greatly affects his behavior. If a man believes that he is susceptible to an illness, He will alter his behavior in order to prevent its occurence. For example, If a man thinks that diabetes is acquired through high intake of sugar and simple carbohydrates, then he will limit the intake of foods rich in these components.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: In health belief model, Individual perception matters. Which of the following is highly UNLIKELY to influence preventive behavior?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Perceived curability of an illness . If a man think he is susceptibe to a certain disease, thinks that the disease is serious and it is a threat to his life and functions, he will use preventive behaviors to avoid the occurence of this threat.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Which of the following is not a PERCEIVED BARRIER in preventive action?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Difficulty adhering to the lifestyle and B. Economic factors. Perceived barriers are those factors that affects the individual’s health preventive actions. Both A and B can affect the individual’s ability to prevent the occurence of diseases. C and D are called Preventive Health Behaviors which enhances the individual’s preventive capabilities.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Conceptualizes that health is a condition of actualization or realization of person’s potential. Avers that the highest aspiration of people is fulfillment and complete development actualization.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Eudaemonistic Model . Smith formulated 5 models of health. Clinical model simply states that when people experience sign and symptoms, they would think that they are unhealthy therefore, Health is the absence of clinical sign and symptoms of a disease. Role performance model states that when a person does his role and activities without deficits, he is healthy and the inability to perform usual roles means that the person is ill. Adaptive Model states that if a person adapts well with his environment, he is healthy and maladaptation equates illness. Eudaemonistic Model of health according to smith is the actualization of a person’s fullest potential. If a person functions optimally and develop self actualization, then, no doubt that person is healthy.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Views people as physiologic system and Absence of sign and symptoms equates health.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Clinical Model. Rationale: Refer to question # 89.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Knowledge about the disease and prior contact with it is what type of VARIABLE according to the health belief model?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Structural. Modifying variables in Becker’s health belief model includes DEMOGRAPHIC : Age, sex, race etc. SOCIOPSYCHOLOGIC : Social and Peer influence. STRUCTURAL : Knowledge about the disease and prior contact with it and CUES TO ACTION : Which are the sign and symptoms of the disease or advice from friends, mass media and others that forces or makes the individual seek help.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: It includes internal and external factors that leads the individual to seek help
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Cues to action . Refer to question # 91.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Influence from peers and social pressure is included in what variable of HBM?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Sociopsychologic. Refer to question # 91.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Age, Sex, Race etc. is included in what variable of HBM?
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Demographic. Refer to question # 91.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: According to Leavell and Clark’s ecologic model, All of this are factors that affects health and illness except
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Reservoir. According to L&C’s Ecologic model, there are 3 factors that affect health and illness. These are the AGENT or the factor the leads to illness, either a bacteria or an event in life. HOST are persons that may or may not be affected by these agents. ENVIRONMENT are factors external to the host that may or may not predispose him to the AGENT.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Is a multi dimensional model developed by PENDER that describes the nature of persons as they interact within the environment to pursue health
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Health Promotion Model. Pender developed the concept of HEALTH PROMOTION MODEL which postulated that an individual engages in health promotion activities to increase well being and attain self actualization. These includes exercise, immunization, healthy lifestyle, good food, self responsibility and all other factors that minimize if not totally eradicate risks and threats of health.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Defined by Pender as all activities directed toward increasing the level of well being and self actualization.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Health promotion. Refer to question # 96.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Defined as an alteration in normal function resulting in reduction of capacities and shortening of life span.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Disease. Disease are alteration in body functions resulting in reduction of capabilities or shortening of life span.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: Personal state in which a person feels unhealthy
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Illness. Illness is something PERSONAL. Unlike disease, Illness are personal state in which person feels unhealthy. An old person might think he is ILL but in fact, he is not due, to diminishing functions and capabilities, people might think they are ILL. Disease however, is something with tangible basis like lab results, X ray films or clinical sign and symptoms.

HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.question: According to her, Caring is defined as a nurturant way of responding to a valued client towards whom the nurse feels a sense of commitment and responsibility.
HISTO_CONCEPT_THEORY.rationale: Watson. This is Jean Watson’s definition of Nursing as caring. This was asked word per word last June 06′ NLE. Benner defines caring as something that matters to people. She postulated the responsibility created by Caring in nursing. She was also responsible for the PRIMACY OF CARING MODEL. choices.C: Respiratory rate greater than 20 breaths per minute

Pulse greater than 100 beats per minute is tachycardia. Frequent bowel sounds refer to hyper-active bowel sounds.

PNLE1.rationale: 37.95 degrees C. To convert °F to °C use this formula, ( °F – 32 ) (0.55). While when converting °C to °F use this formula, ( °C x 1.8) + 32. Note that 0.55 is 5/9 and 1.8 is 9/5.

Giving medications) after performing the nursing intervention (not before). Recording should also be done using a pen, be complete, and signed with the nurse’s full name and title.

PNLE1.question: During the planning phase of the nursing process, which of the following is the outcome?

Orem’s theory is called self-care deficit theory and is based on the belief that individual has a need for self-care actions. King’s theory is the Goal attainment theory and described nursing as a helping profession that assists individuals and groups in society to attain, maintain, and restore health. PNLE1.question: Which expected outcome is correctly written?

choices.A: “The patient will feel less nauseated in 24 hours.”
choices.B: “The patient will eat the right amount of food daily.”
choices.C: “The patient will identify all the high-salt food from a prepared list by discharge.”

PNLE1.rationale: Nurse and patient. Although diagnosing is basically the nurse’s responsibility, input from the patient is essential to formulate the correct nursing diagnosis.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following behaviors by Nurse Jane Robles demonstrates that she understands well th elements of effecting charting?

PNLE1.rationale: Stop the infusion. The sign and symptoms indicate extravasation so the IVF should be stopped immediately and put warm not cold towel on the affected site.

PNLE1.rationale: After few minutes, return to that patient’s room and do not leave until the patient takes the medication. This is to verify or to make sure that the medication was taken by the patient as directed.

PNLE1.question: Becky is on NPO since midnight as preparation for blood test. Adreno-cortical response is activated. Which of the following is an expected response?

PNLE1.question: What nursing action is appropriate when obtaining a sterile urine specimen from an indwelling catheter to prevent infection?

choices.A: Use sterile gloves when obtaining urine.
choices.B: Open the drainage bag and pour out the urine.

PNLE1.question: A client is receiving 115 ml/hr of continuous IVF. The nurse notices that the venipuncture site is red and swollen. Which of the following interventions would the nurse perform first?

choices.D: Place a clod towel on the site

PNLE1.rationale: Capillary refill greater than 3 seconds and buccal cyanosis. Capillary refill greater than 3 seconds and buccal cyanosis indicate decreased oxygen to the tissues which requires immediate attention/intervention. Oriented to date, time and place, hemoglobin of 13 g/dl are normal data.

PNLE1.question: The nurse enters the room to give a prescribed medication but the patient is inside the bathroom. What should the nurse do?

choices.A: Leave the medication at the bedside and leave the room.
choices.B: fter few minutes, return to that patient’s room and do not leave until the patient takes the medication.
choices.C: Instruct the patient to take the medication and leave it at the bedside.
choices.D: Wait for the patient to return to bed and just leave the medication at the bedside.

PNLE1.rationale: Patient’s NGT was removed 2 hours ago. The change-of-shift report should indicate significant recent changes in the patient’s condition that the nurse assuming responsibility for care of the patient will need to monitor. The other options are not critical enough to include in the report.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following is inappropriate nursing action when administering NGT feeding?

choices.A: Place the feeding 20 inches above the pint if insertion of NGT.

PNLE1.question: A female patient is being discharged after thyroidectomy. After providing the medication teaching. The nurse asks the patient to repeat the instructions. The nurse is performing which professional role?
PNLE1.rationale: Making of individualized patient care. To be effective, the nursing care plan developed in the planning phase of the nursing process must reflect the individualized needs of the patient.

PNLE1.question: Which data would be of greatest concern to the nurse when completing the nursing assessment of a 68-year-old woman hospitalized due to Pneumonia?

choices.A: Oriented to date, time and place
choices.C: apillary refill greater than 3 seconds and buccal cyanosis

PNLE1.rationale: Ineffective breathing pattern related to pain, as evidenced by shortness of breath.. Physiologic needs (ex. Oxygen, fluids, nutrition) must be met before lower needs (such as safety and security, love and belongingness, self-esteem and self-actualization) can be met. Therefore, physiologic needs have the highest priority.

PNLE1.question: During a change-of-shift report, it would be important for the nurse relinquishing responsibility for care of the patient to communicate. Which of the following facts to the nurse assuming responsibility for care of the patient?

choices.A: That the patient verbalized, “My headache is gone.”

PNLE2.question: A patient is wearing a soft wrist-safety device. Which of the following nursing assessment is considered abnormal?

choices.D: luish fingernails, cool and pale fingers

PNLE2.rationale: Bluish fingernails, cool and pale fingers. A safety device on the wrist may impair blood circulation. Therefore, the nurse should assess the patient for signs of impaired circulation such as bluish fingernails, cool and pale fingers. Palpable radial and ulnar pulses, capillary refill within 3 seconds are all normal findings.

PNLE2.question: Pia’s serum sodium level is 150 mEq/L. Which of the following food items does the nurse instruct Pia to avoid?
PNLE2.rationale: sardines. The normal serum sodium level is 135 to 145 mEq/L, the client is having hypernatremia. Pia should avoid food high in sodium like processed food. Broccoli, cabbage and tomatoes are good source of Vitamin C.

PNLE2.question: Jason, 3 years old vomited. His mom stated, “He vomited 6 ounces of his formula this morning.” This statement is an example of:

choices.A: objective data from a secondary source
choices.B: objective data from a primary source
choices.C: subjective data from a primary source
choices.D: subjective data from a secondary source

PNLE2.rationale: objective data from a secondary source. Jason is the primary source; his mother is a secondary source. The data is objective because it can be perceived by the senses, verified by another person observing the same patient, and tested against accepted standards or norms.

PNLE2.question: Which of the following is a nursing diagnosis?
PNLE2.rationale: Hypethermia. Hyperthermia is a NANDA-approved nursing diagnosis. Diabetes Mellitus, Angina and Chronic Renal Failure are medical diagnoses.

PNLE2.question: What is the characteristic of the nursing process?
PNLE2.rationale: goal-oriented. The nursing process is goal-oriented. It is also systematic, patient-centered, and dynamic.

PNLE2.question: A skin lesion which is fluid-filled, less than 1 cm in size is called:
PNLE2.rationale: vesicle. Vesicle is a circumscribed circulation containing serous fluid or blood and less than 1 cm (ex. Blister, chicken pox).

PNLE2.question: During application of medication into the ear, which of the following is inappropriate nursing action?

choices.A: In an adult, pull the pinna upward.
choices.B: Instill the medication directly into the tympanic membrane.
choices.C: Warm the medication at room or body temperature.
choices.D: Press the tragus of the ear a few times to assist flow of medication into the ear canal.

PNLE2.rationale: Instill the medication directly into the tympanic membrane. During the application of medication it is inappropriate to instill the medication directly into the tympanic membrane. The right thing to do is instill the medication along the lateral wall of the auditory canal.

PNLE2.question: Which of the following is appropriate nursing intervention for a client who is grieving over the death of her child?

choices.A: Tell her not to cry and it will be better.
choices.B: Provide opportunity to the client to tell their story.
choices.C: Encourage her to accept or to replace the lost person.
choices.D: iscourage the client in expressing her emotions.

PNLE2.rationale: Provide opportunity to the client to tell their story. Providing a grieving person an opportunity to tell their story allows the person to express feelings. This is therapeutic in assisting the client resolve grief.

PNLE2.question: It is the gradual decrease of the body’s temperature after death.
PNLE2.rationale: algor mortis. Algor mortis is the decrease of the body’s temperature after death. Livor mortis is the discoloration of the skin after death. Rigor mortis is the stiffening of the body that occurs about 2-4 hours after death.

PNLE2.question: When performing an admission assessment on a newly admitted patient, the nurse percusses resonance. The nurse knows that resonance heard on percussion is most commonly heard over which organ?
PNLE2.rationale: lung. Resonance is loud, low-pitched and long duration that’s heard most commonly over an air-filled tissue such as a normal lung.

PNLE2.question: The nurse is aware that Bell’s palsy affects which cranial nerve?
PNLE2.rationale: 7th CN (Facial). Bells’ palsy is the paralysis of the motor component of the 7th caranial nerve, resulting in facial sag, inability to close the eyelid or the mouth, drooling, flat nasolabial fold and loss of taste on the affected side of the face.

PNLE2.question: Prolonged deficiency of Vitamin B9 leads to:
PNLE2.rationale: megaloblastic anemia. Prolonged Vitamin B9 deficiency will lead to megaloblastic anemia while pernicious anemia results in deficiency in Vitamin B12. Prolonged deficiency of Vitamin C leads to scurvy and Pellagra results in deficiency in Vitamin B3.

PNLE2.question: Nurse Cherry is teaching a 72 year old patient about a newly prescribed medication. What could cause a geriatric patient to have difficulty retaining knowledge about the newly prescribed medication?

choices.C: Patient has no interest on learning

PNLE2.rationale: Decreased sensory functions. Decreased in sensory functions could cause a geriatric patient to have difficulty retaining knowledge about the newly prescribed medications. Absence of family support and no interest on learning may affect compliance, not knowledge retention. Decreased plasma levels do not alter patient’s knowledge about the drug.

PNLE2.question: When assessing a patient’s level of consciousness, which type of nursing intervention is the nurse performing?
PNLE2.rationale: Independent. Independent nursing interventions involve actions that nurses initiate based on their own knowledge and skills without the direction or supervision of another member of the health care team.

PNLE2.question: Claire is admitted with a diagnosis of chronic shoulder pain. By definition, the nurse understands that the patient has had pain for more than:
PNLE2.rationale: 6 months. Chronic pain s usually defined as pain lasting longer than 6 months.

PNLE2.question: Which of the following statements regarding the nursing process is true?

choices.A: It is useful on outpatient settings.
choices.B: It progresses in separate, unrelated steps.
choices.C: It focuses on the patient, not the nurse.
choices.D: It provides the solution to all patient health problems.

PNLE2.rationale: It focuses on the patient, not the nurse. The nursing process is patient-centered, not nurse-centered. It can be use in any setting, and the steps are related. The nursing process can’t solve all patient health problems.

PNLE2.question: Which of the following is considered significant enough to require immediate communication to another member of the health care team?

choices.A: Weight loss of 3 lbs in a 120 lb female patient.
choices.B: iminished breath sounds in patient with previously normal breath sounds
choices.D: hange of heart rate from 70 to 83 beats per minute.

PNLE2.rationale: Diminished breath sounds in patient with previously normal breath sounds. Diminished breath sound is a life threatening problem therefore it is highly priority because they pose the greatest threat to the patient’s well-being.

PNLE2.question: To assess the adequacy of food intake, which of the following assessment parameters is best used?
PNLE2.rationale: 3-day diet recall. 3-day diet recall is an example of dietary history. This is used to indicate the adequacy of food intake of the client.

PNLE2.question: Van Fajardo is a 55 year old who was admitted to the hospital with newly diagnosed hepatitis. The nurse is doing a patient teaching with Mr. Fajardo. What kind of role does the nurse assume?
PNLE2.rationale: teacher. The nurse will assume the role of a teacher in this therapeutic relationship. The other roles are inappropriate in this situation.

PNLE2.question: When providing a continuous enteral feeding, which of the following action is essential for the nurse to do?

choices.A: Place the client on the left side of the bed.
choices.B: ttach the feeding bag to the current tubing.
choices.C: Elevate the head of the bed.
choices.D: old the formula before administering it.

PNLE2.rationale: Elevate the head of the bed. Elevating the head of the bed during an enteral feeding prevents aspiration. The patient may be placed on the right side to prevent aspiration. Enteral feedings are given at room temperature to lessen GI distress. The enteral tubing should be changed every 24 hours to limit microbial growth.

PNLE2.question: Kussmaul’s breathing is;

choices.B: Prolonged gasping inspiration followed by a very short, usually inefficient expiration.
choices.C: Marked rhythmic waxing and waning of respirations from very deep to very shallow breathing and temporary apnea.
choices.D: Increased rate and depth of respiration.

PNLE2.rationale: Increased rate and depth of respiration. Kussmaul breathing is also called as hyperventilation. Seen in metabolic acidosis and renal failure. Option A refers to Biot’s breathing. Option B is apneustic breathing and option C is the Cheyne-stokes breathing.

PNLE2.question: Presty has terminal cancer and she refuses to believe that loss is happening ans she assumes artificial cheerfulness. What stage of grieving is she in?
PNLE2.rationale: denial. The client is in denial stage because she is unready to face the reality that loss is happening and she assumes artificial cheerfulness.

PNLE2.question: Immunization for healthy babies and preschool children is an example of what level of preventive health care?
PNLE2.rationale: Primary. The primary level focuses on health promotion. Secondary level focuses on health maintenance. Tertiary focuses on rehabilitation. There is n Curative level of preventive health care problems.

PNLE2.question: Which is an example of a subjective data?
PNLE2.rationale: Patient stated, “My arms still hurt.”. Subjective data are apparent only to the person affected and can or verified only by that person.

PNLE2.question: The nurse is assessing the endocrine system. Which organ is part of the endocrine system?
PNLE2.rationale: Thyroid. The thyroid is part of the endocrine system. Heart, sinus and thymus are not.

PNLE3.question: Nurse Brenda is teaching a patient about a newly prescribed drug. What could cause a geriatric patient to have difficulty retaining knowledge about prescribed medications?
PNLE3.rationale: Sensory deficits. Sensory deficits could cause a geriatric patient to have difficulty retaining knowledge about prescribed medications. Decreased plasma drug levels do not alter the patient’s knowledge about the drug. A lack of family support may affect compliance, not knowledge retention. Toilette syndrome is unrelated to knowledge retention.

PNLE3.question: When examining a patient with abdominal pain the nurse in charge should assess:

choices.D: The symptomatic quadrant either second or third

PNLE3.rationale: The symptomatic quadrant last. The nurse should systematically assess all areas of the abdomen, if time and the patient’s condition permit, concluding with the symptomatic area. Otherwise, the nurse may elicit pain in the symptomatic area, causing the muscles in other areas to tighten. This would interfere with further assessment.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is assessing a postoperative adult patient. Which of the following should the nurse document as subjective data?
PNLE3.rationale: Patient’s description of pain. Subjective data come directly from the patient and usually are recorded as direct quotations that reflect the patient’s opinions or feelings about a situation. Vital signs, laboratory test result, and ECG waveforms are examples of objective data.

PNLE3.question: A male patient has a soft wrist-safety device. Which assessment finding should the nurse consider abnormal?
PNLE3.rationale: Cool, pale fingers. A safety device on the wrist may impair circulation and restrict blood supply to body tissues. Therefore, the nurse should assess the patient for signs of impaired circulation, such as cool, pale fingers. A palpable radial or lunar pulse and pink nail beds are normal findings.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following planes divides the body longitudinally into anterior and posterior regions?
PNLE3.rationale: Frontal plane. Frontal or coronal plane runs longitudinally at a right angle to a sagittal plane dividing the body in anterior and posterior regions. A sagittal plane runs longitudinally dividing the body into right and left regions; if exactly midline, it is called a midsagittal plane. A transverse plane runs horizontally at a right angle to the vertical axis, dividing the structure into superior and inferior regions.

PNLE3.question: A female patient with a terminal illness is in denial. Indicators of denial include:
PNLE3.rationale: Shock dismay. Shock and dismay are early signs of denial-the first stage of grief. The other options are associated with depression—a later stage of grief.

PNLE3.question: The nurse in charge is transferring a patient from the bed to a chair. Which action does the nurse take during this patient transfer?

choices.A: Position the head of the bed flat
choices.B: Helps the patient dangle the legs
choices.D: Places the chair facing away from the bed

PNLE3.rationale: Helps the patient dangle the legs. After placing the patient in high Fowler’s position and moving the patient to the side of the bed, the nurse helps the patient sit on the edge of the bed and dangle the legs; the nurse then faces the patient and places the chair next to and facing the head of the bed.

PNLE3.question: A female patient who speaks a little English has emergency gallbladder surgery, during discharge preparation, which nursing action would best help this patient understand wound care instruction?

choices.A: sking frequently if the patient understands the instruction
choices.B: sking an interpreter to replay the instructions to the patient.
choices.C: Writing out the instructions and having a family member read them to the patient
choices.D: emonstrating the procedure and having the patient return the demonstration

PNLE3.rationale: Demonstrating the procedure and having the patient return the demonstration. Demonstrating by the nurse with a return demonstration by the patient ensures that the patient can perform wound care correctly. Patients may claim to understand discharge instruction when they do not. An interpreter of family member may communicate verbal or written instructions inaccurately.

PNLE3.question: Before administering the evening dose of a prescribed medication, the nurse on the evening shift finds an unlabeled, filled syringe in the patient’s medication drawer. What should the nurse in charge do?

choices.A: iscard the syringe to avoid a medication error
choices.B: Obtain a label for the syringe from the pharmacy
choices.C: Use the syringe because it looks like it contains the same medication the nurse was prepared to give
choices.D: all the day nurse to verify the contents of the syringe

PNLE3.rationale: Discard the syringe to avoid a medication error. As a safety precaution, the nurse should discard an unlabeled syringe that contains medication. The other options are considered unsafe because they promote error.

PNLE3.question: When administering drug therapy to a male geriatric patient, the nurse must stay especially alert for adverse effects. Which factor makes geriatric patients to adverse drug effects?

choices.D: Enhanced blood flow to the GI tract

PNLE3.rationale: Aging-related physiological changes. Aging-related physiological changes account for the increased frequency of adverse drug reactions in geriatric patients. Renal and hepatic changes cause drugs to clear more slowly in these patients. With increasing age, neurons are lost and blood flow to the GI tract decreases.

PNLE3.question: A female patient is being discharged after cataract surgery. After providing medication teaching, the nurse asks the patient to repeat the instructions. The nurse is performing which professional role?
PNLE3.rationale: Educator. When teaching a patient about medications before discharge, the nurse is acting as an educator. The nurse acts as a manager when performing such activities as scheduling and making patient care assignments. The nurse performs the care giving role when providing direct care, including bathing patients and administering medications and prescribed treatments. The nurse acts as a patient advocate when making the patient’s wishes known to the doctor.

PNLE3.question: A female patient exhibits signs of heightened anxiety. Which response by the nurse is most likely to reduce the patient’s anxiety?

choices.B: “Read this manual and then ask me any questions you may have.”
choices.C: “Why don’t you listen to the radio?”

PNLE3.rationale: “Let’s talk about what’s bothering you.” Anxiety may result from feeling of helplessness, isolation, or insecurity. This response helps reduce anxiety by encouraging the patient to express feelings. The nurse should be supportive and develop goals together with the patient to give the patient some control over an anxiety-inducing situation. Because the other options ignore the patient’s feeling and block communication, they would not reduce anxiety.

PNLE3.question: A scrub nurse in the operating room has which responsibility?

choices.C: Handling surgical instruments to the surgeon

PNLE3.rationale: Handling surgical instruments to the surgeon. The scrub nurse assist the surgeon by providing appropriate surgical instruments and supplies, maintaining strict surgical asepsis and, with the circulating nurse, accounting for all gauze, sponges, needles, and instruments. The circulating nurse assists the surgeon and scrub nurse, positions the patient, applies appropriate equipment and surgical drapes, assists with gowning and gloving, and provides the surgeon and scrub nurse with supplies.

PNLE3.question: A patient is in the bathroom when the nurse enters to give a prescribed medication. What should the nurse in charge do?

choices.A: Leave the medication at the patient’s bedside
choices.B: Tell the patient to be sure to take the medication. And then leave it at the bedside
choices.C: Return shortly to the patient’s room and remain there until the patient takes the medication
choices.D: Wait for the patient to return to bed, and then leave the medication at the bedside

PNLE3.rationale: Return shortly to the patient’s room and remain there until the patient takes the medication. The nurse should return shortly to the patient’s room and remain there until the patient takes the medication to verify that it was taken as directed. The nurse should never leave medication at the patient’s bedside unless specifically requested to do so.

PNLE3.question: The physician orders heparin, 7,500 units, to be administered subcutaneously every 6 hours. The vial reads 10,000 units per millilitre. The nurse should anticipate giving how much heparin for each dose?
PNLE3.rationale: ¾ ml. The nurse solves the problem as follows: 10,000 units/7,500 units = 1 ml/X 10,000 X = 7,500 X= 7,500/10,000 or ¾ ml

PNLE3.question: The nurse in charge measures a patient’s temperature at 102 degrees F. what is the equivalent Centigrade temperature? 39 degrees C 47 degrees C
PNLE3.rationale: 38.9 degrees C. To convert Fahrenheit degrees to centigrade, use this formula: C degrees = (F degrees – 32) x 5/9 C degrees = (102 – 32) 5/9 + 70 x 5/9 38.9 degrees C

PNLE3.question: 9 degrees C
PNLE3.rationale: Arterial blood gas (ABG) analysis. All of these test help evaluate a patient with respiratory problems. However, ABG analysis is the only test evaluates gas exchange in the lungs, providing information about patient’s oxygenation status.

PNLE3.question: 1 degrees C
PNLE3.rationale: The diaphragm detects high-pitched sounds best. The diaphragm of a stethoscope detects high-pitched sound best; the bell detects low pitched sounds best. Palpation detects thrills best.

PNLE3.question: To evaluate a patient for hypoxia, the physician is most likely to order which laboratory test?
PNLE3.rationale: Within 6 months. In most cases, an outpatient must fill a prescription for a controlled substance within 6 months of the date on which the prescription was written.

PNLE3.question: The nurse uses a stethoscope to auscultate a male patient’s chest. Which statement about a stethoscope with a bell and diaphragm is true?

choices.A: The bell detects high-pitched sounds best
choices.B: The diaphragm detects high-pitched sounds best
choices.D: The diaphragm detects low-pitched sounds best

PNLE3.rationale: The patient’s cognitive abilities. The nurse must consider the patient’s cognitive abilities to understand drug instructions. If not, the nurse must find a family member or significant other to take on the responsibility of administering medications in the home setting. The patient’s ability to recover, occupational hazards, and socioeconomic status do not affect drug administration.

PNLE3.question: A male patient is to be discharged with a prescription for an analgesic that is a controlled substance. During discharge teaching, the nurse should explain that the patient must fill this prescription how soon after the date on which it was written?
PNLE3.rationale: Give simple directions shortly before the I.V. therapy is to start. Because a 2-year-old child has limited understanding, the nurse should give simple directions and explanations of what will occur shortly before the procedure. She should try to avoid frightening the child with the explanation and allow the child to make simple choices, such as choosing the I.V. insertion site, if possible. However, she shouldn’t ask the child if he wants the therapy, because the answer may be “No!” Telling the child that the treatment is for his own good is ineffective because a 2-year-old perceives pain as a negative sensation and cannot understand that a painful procedure can have position results. All syringes have three parts: a tip, which connects the needle to the syringe; a barrel, the outer part on which the measurement scales are printed; and a plunger, which fits inside the barrel to expel the medication. choices.C: Visual learning is the best for every individual
choices.D: Do not teach a client when he is in pain

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is D: Do not teach a client when he is in pain

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: According to Bloom, there are 3 domains in learning. Which of these domains is responsible for the ability of Donya Delilah to inject insulin?
STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is C: Psychomotor

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: Which domains of learning is responsible for making John and Marsha understand the different kinds of family planning methods?
STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is A: Cognitive

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: Which of the following statement clearly defines therapeutic communication?

choices.A: Therapeutic communication is an interaction process which is primarily directed by the nurse
choices.B: It conveys feeling of warmth, acceptance and empathy from the nurse to a patient in relaxed atmosphere
choices.C: Therapeutic communication is a reciprocal interaction based on trust and aimed at identifying patient needs and developing mutual goals
choices.D: Therapeutic communication is an assessment component of the nursing process

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is C: Therapeutic communication is a reciprocal interaction based on trust and aimed at identifying patient needs and developing mutual goals

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: Which of the following concept is most important in establishing a therapeutic nurse patient relationship?

choices.A: The nurse must fully understand the patient’s feelings, perception and reactions before goals can be established
choices.B: The nurse must be a role model for health fostering behavior
choices.C: The nurse must recognize that the patient may manifest maladaptive behavior after illness
choices.D: The nurse should understand that patients might test her before trust is established

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is D: The nurse should understand that patients might test her before trust is established

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: Which of the following communication skill is most effective in dealing with covert communication?
STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is A: Validation

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: Which of the following are qualities of a good recording?
STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is D: Accuracy

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: All of the following chart entries are correct except
STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is C: Seems agitated

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: Which of the following teaching method is effective in client who needs to be educated about self injection of insulin?
STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is B: Demonstration

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: What is the most important characteristic of a nurse patient relationship?
STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is A: It is growth facilitating

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: Which of the following nursing intervention is needed before teaching a client post spleenectomy deep breathing and coughing exercises?

choices.A: Tell the patient that deep breathing and coughing exercises is needed to promote good breathing, circulation and prevent complication
choices.B: Tell the client that deep breathing and coughing exercises is needed to prevent Thrombophlebitis, hydrostatic pneumonia and atelectasis
choices.D: Tell client that cooperation is vital to improve recovery

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is A: Tell the patient that deep breathing and coughing exercises is needed to promote good breathing, circulation and prevent complication

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: The client has an allergy with penicillin. What is the best way to communicate this information?

choices.A: Place an allergy alert in the Kardex
choices.C: Write it on the patient’s chart

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is B: Notify the attending physician

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: An adult client is on extreme pain. He is moaning and grimacing. What is the best way to assess the client’s pain?

choices.B: Have the client rate his pain on the smiley pain rating scale
choices.C: Active listening on what the patient says

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is C: Active listening on what the patient says

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: Therapeutic communication begins with?
STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is B: Knowing yourself

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.question: The PCS gave new guidelines including leaflets to educate cancer patients. As a nurse, When using materials like this, what is your responsibility?

choices.B: Give it for the patient to read himself
choices.C: Let the family member read the material for the patient
choices.D: Read it yourself then, Have the client read the material

STRESS_CRISIS_COMMS.rationale: The correct answer is D: Read it yourself then, Have the client read the material

PNLE1.question: A client asks the nurse what a third degree laceration is. She was informed that she had one. The nurse explains that this is:

choices.B: through the skin and into the muscles
choices.D: that extends through the perineal muscle.

PNLE1.rationale: that extended their anal sphincter. Third degree laceration involves all in the second degree laceration and the external sphincter of the rectum. Options B, C and D are under the second degree laceration.

PNLE1.question: Betina 30 weeks AOG discharged with a diagnosis of placenta previa. The nurse knows that the client understands her care at home when she says:

choices.A: I am happy to note that we can have sex occasionally when I have no bleeding.
choices.B: I am afraid I might have an operation when my due comes
choices.C: I will have to remain in bed until my due date comes
choices.D: I may go back to work since I stay only at the office.

PNLE1.rationale: I will have to remain in bed until my due date comes. Placenta previa means that the placenta is the presenting part. On the first and second trimester there is spotting. On the third trimester there is bleeding that is sudden, profuse and painless.

PNLE1.question: The uterus has already risen out of the pelvis and is experiencing farther into the abdominal area at about the:
PNLE1.rationale: 18th week of pregnancy. On the 8th week of pregnancy, the uterus is still within the pelvic area. On the 10th week, the uterus is still within the pelvic area. On the 12th week, the uterus and placenta have grown, expanding into the abdominal cavity. On the 18th week, the uterus has already risen out of the pelvis and is expanding into the abdominal area.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following urinary symptoms does the pregnant woman most frequently experience during the first trimester:
PNLE1.rationale: frequency. Pressure and irritation of the bladder by the growing uterus during the first trimester is responsible for causing urinary frequency. Dysuria, incontinence and burning are symptoms associated with urinary tract infection.

PNLE1.question: Mrs. Jimenez went to the health center for pre-natal check-up. the student nurse took her weight and revealed 142 lbs. She asked the student nurse how much should she gain weight in her pregnancy.
PNLE1.rationale: 25-35 lbs. A weight gain of 11. 2 to 15.9 kg (25 to 35 lbs) is currently recommended as an average weight gain in pregnancy. This weight gain consists of the following: fetus- 7.5 lb; placenta- 1.5 lb; amniotic fluid- 2 lb; uterus- 2.5 lb; breasts- 1.5 to 3 lb; blood volume- 4 lb; body fat- 7 lb; body fluid- 7 lb.

PNLE1.question: The nurse is preparing Mrs. Jordan for cesarean delivery. Which of the following key concept should the nurse consider when implementing nursing care?

choices.A: Explain the surgery, expected outcome and kind of anesthetics.
choices.B: Modify preoperative teaching to meet the needs of either a planned or emergency cesarean birth.
choices.C: rrange for a staff member of the anesthesia department to explain what to expect post-operatively.
choices.D: Instruct the mother’s support person to remain in the family lounge until after the delivery.

PNLE1.rationale: Modify preoperative teaching to meet the needs of either a planned or emergency cesarean birth. A key point to consider when preparing the client for a cesarean delivery is to modify the preoperative teaching to meet the needs of either planned or emergency cesarean birth, the depth and breadth of instruction will depend on circumstances and time available.

PNLE1.question: Bettine Gonzales is hospitalized for the treatment of severe preecplampsia. Which of the following represents an unusual finding for this condition?
PNLE1.rationale: convulsions. Options A, B and C are findings of severe preeclampsia. Convulsions is a finding of eclampsia—an obstetrical emergency.

PNLE1.question: Nurse Geli explains to the client who is 33 weeks pregnant and is experiencing vaginal bleeding that coitus:

choices.A: Need to be modified in any way by either partner
choices.B: Is permitted if penile penetration is not deep.
choices.C: Should be restricted because it may stimulate uterine activity.
choices.D: Is safe as long as she is in side-lying position.

PNLE1.rationale: Should be restricted because it may stimulate uterine activity.. Coitus is restricted when there is watery discharge, uterine contraction and vaginal bleeding. Also those women with a history of spontaneous miscarriage may be advised to avoid coitus during the time of pregnancy when a previous miscarriage occurred.

PNLE1.question: Mrs. Precilla Abuel, a 32 year old mulripara is admitted to labor and delivery. Her last 3 pregnancies in short stage one of labor. The nurses decide to observe her closely. The physician determines that Mrs. Abuel’s cervix is dilated to 6 cm. Mrs. Abuel states that she is extremely uncomfortable. To lessen Mrs. Abuel’s discomfort, the nurse can advise her to:
PNLE1.rationale: assume Sim’s position. When the woman is in Sim’s position, this puts the weight of the fetus on bed, not on the woman and allows good circulation in the lower extremities.

PNLE1.question: Which is true regarding the fontanels of the newborn?

choices.A: The anterior is large in shape when compared to the posterior fontanel.
choices.B: The anterior is triangular shaped; the posterior is diamond shaped.
choices.C: The anterior is bulging; the posterior appears sunken.
choices.D: The posterior closes at 18 months; the anterior closes at 8 to 12 months.

PNLE1.rationale: The anterior is large in shape when compared to the posterior fontanel.. The anterior fontanel is larger in size than the posterior fontanel. Additionally, the anterior fontanel, which is diamond shaped closes at 18 month, whereas the posterior fontanel, which is triangular in shape closes at 8 to 12 weeks. Neither fontanel should appear bulging, which may indicate increases ICP or sunken, which may indicate hydration.

PNLE1.question: Mrs. Quijones gave birth by spontaneous delivery to a full term baby boy. After a minute after birth, he is crying and moving actively. His birth weight is 6.8 lbs. What do you expect baby Quijones to weigh at 6 months?
PNLE1.rationale: 13 -14 lbs. The birth weight of an infant is doubled at 6 months and is tripled at 12 months.

PNLE1.question: During the first hours following delivery, the post partum client is given IVF with oxytocin added to them. The nurse understands the primary reason for this is:
PNLE1.rationale: To promote uterine contraction. Oxytocin is a hormone produced by the pituitary gland that produces intermittent uterine contractions, helping to promote uterine involution.

PNLE1.question: Nurse Luis is assessing the newborn’s heart rate. Which of the following would be considered normal if the newborn is sleeping?
PNLE1.rationale: 100 beats per minute. The normal heart rate for a newborn that is sleeping is approximately 100 beats per minute. If the newborn was awake, the normal heart rate would range from 120 to 160 beats per minute.

PNLE1.question: The infant with Down Syndrome should go through which of the Erikson’s developmental stages first?
PNLE1.rationale: Trust vs. Mistrust. The child with Down syndrome will go through the same first stage, trust vs. mistrust, only at a slow rate. Therefore, the nurse should concentrate on developing on bond between the primary caregiver and the child.

PNLE1.question: The child with phenylketonuria (PKU) must maintain a low phenylalanine diet to prevent which of the following complications?
PNLE1.rationale: Irreversible brain damage. The child with PKU must maintain a strict low phenylalanine diet to prevent central nervous system damage, seizures and eventual death.

PNLE1.question: Which age group is with imaginative minds and creates imaginary friends?
PNLE1.rationale: Preschool. During preschool, this is the time when children do imitative play, imaginative play—the occurrence of imaginative playmates, dramatic play where children like to act, dance and sing.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following situations would alert you to a potentially developmental problem with a child?

choices.A: Pointing to body parts at 15 months of age.
choices.B: Using gesture to communicate at 18 months.
choices.D: Saying “mama” or “dada” for the first time at 18 months of age.

PNLE1.rationale: Saying “mama” or “dada” for the first time at 18 months of age.. A child should say “mama” or “dada” during 10 to 12 months of age. Options A, B and C are all normal assessments of language development of a child.

PNLE1.question: Isabelle, a 2 year old girl loves to move around and oftentimes manifests negativism and temper tantrums. What is the best way to deal with her behavior?

choices.A: Tell her that she would not be loved by others is she behaves that way..
choices.B: Withholding giving her toys until she behaves properly.
choices.C: Ignore her behavior as long as she does not hurt herself and others.
choices.D: sk her what she wants and give it to pacify her.

PNLE1.rationale: Ignore her behavior as long as she does not hurt herself and others.. If a child is trying to get attention or trying to get something through tantrums—ignore his/her behavior.

PNLE1.question: Baby boy Villanueva, 4 months old, was seen at the pediatric clinic for his scheduled check-up. By this period, baby Villanueva has already increased his height by how many inches?
PNLE1.rationale: 4 inches. From birth to 6 months, the infant grows 1 inch (2.5 cm) per month. From 6 to 12 months, the infant grows ½ inch (1.25 cm) per month.

PNLE1.question: Alice, 10 years old was brought to the ER because of Asthma. She was immediately put under aerosol administration of Terbutaline. After sometime, you observe that the child does not show any relief from the treatment given. Upon assessment, you noticed that both the heart and respiratory rate are still elevated and the child shows difficulty of exhaling. You suspect:
PNLE1.rationale: Status Asthmaticus. Status asthmaticus leads to respiratory distress and bronchospasm despite of treatment and interventions. Mechanical ventilation maybe needed due to respiratory failure.

PNLE1.question: Nurse Jonas assesses a 2 year old boy with a tentative diagnosis of nephroblastoma. Symptoms the nurse observes that suggest this problem include:
PNLE1.rationale: Abdominal mass and weakness. Nephroblastoma or Wilm’s tumor is caused by chromosomal abnormalities, most common kidney cancer among children characterized by abdominal mass, hematuria, hypertension and fever.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following danger sings should be reported immediately during the antepartum period?
PNLE1.rationale: blurred vision. Danger signs that require prompt reporting are leaking of amniotic fluid, blurred vision, vaginal bleeding, rapid weight gain and elevated blood pressure. Nasal stuffiness, breast tenderness, and constipation are common discomforts associated with pregnancy.

PNLE1.question: Nurse Jacob is assessing a 15 month old child with acute otitis media. Which of the following symptoms would the nurse anticipate finding?

choices.A: periorbital edema, absent light reflex and translucent tympanic membrane
choices.B: irritability, purulent drainage in middle ear, nasal congestion and cough
choices.C: iarrhea, retracted tympanic membrane and enlarged parotid gland
choices.D: Vomiting, pulling at ears and pearly white tympanic membrane

PNLE1.rationale: irritability, purulent drainage in middle ear, nasal congestion and cough. Irritability, purulent drainage in middle ear, nasal congestion and cough, fever, loss of appetite, vomiting and diarrhea are clinical manifestations of otitis media. Acute otitis media is common in children 6 months to 3 years old and 8 years old and above. Breast fed infants have higher resistance due to protection of Eustachian tubes and middle ear from breast milk.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following is the most appropriate intervention to reduce stress in a preterm infant at 33 weeks gestation?

choices.A: Sensory stimulation including several senses at a time
choices.B: tactile stimulation until signs of over stimulation develop
choices.C: n attitude of extension when prone or side lying

PNLE1.rationale: Kangaroo care. Kangaroo care is the use of skin-to-skin contact to maintain body heat. This method of care not only supplies heat but also encourages parent-child interaction.

PNLE1.question: The parent of a client with albinism would need to be taught which preventive healthcare measure by the nurse:
PNLE1.rationale: Use of a high-SPF sunblock. Without melanin production, the child with albinism is at risk for severe sunburns. Maximum sun protection should be taken, including use of hats, long sleeves, minimal time in the sun and high-SPF sunblock, to prevent any problems.

PNLE2.question: Nurse Bella explains to a 28 year old pregnant woman undergoing a non-stress test that the test is a way of evaluating the condition of the fetus by comparing the fetal heart rate with:
PNLE2.rationale: Fetal movement. Non-stress test measures response of the FHR to the fetal movement. With fetal movement, FHR increase by 15 beats and remain for 15 seconds then decrease to average rate. No increase means poor oxygenation perfusion to fetus.

PNLE2.question: During a 2 hour childbirth focusing on labor and delivery process for primigravida. The nurse describes the second maneuver that the fetus goes through during labor progress when the head is the presenting part as which of the following:
PNLE2.rationale: Flexion. The 6 cardinal movements of labor are descent, flexion, internal rotation, extension, external rotation and expulsion.

PNLE2.question: Mrs. Jovel Diaz went to the hospital to have her serum blood test for alpha-fetoprotein. The nurse informed her about the result of the elevation of serum AFP. The patient asked her what was the test for:
PNLE2.rationale: Neural tube defects. Alpha-fetoprotein is a substance produces by the fetal liver that is present in amniotic fluid and maternal serum. The level is abnormally high in the maternal serum if the fetus has an open spinal or abdominal defect because the open defect allows more AFP to appear.

PNLE2.question: Fetal heart rate can be auscultated with a fetoscope as early as:
PNLE2.rationale: 20 weeks of gestation. The FHR can be auscultated with a fetoscope at about 20 weeks of gestation. FHR is usually auscultated at the midline suprapubic region with Doppler ultrasound at 10 to 12 weeks of gestation. FHR cannot be heard any earlier than 10 weeks of gestation.

PNLE2.question: Mrs. Bendivin states that she is experiencing aching swollen, leg veins. The nurse would explain that this is most probably the result of which of the following:

choices.C: Pressure on blood vessels from the enlarging uterus
choices.D: The force of gravity pulling down on the uterus

PNLE2.rationale: Pressure on blood vessels from the enlarging uterus. Pressure of the growing fetus on blood vessels results in an increase risk for venous stasis in the lower extremities. Subsequently, edema and varicose vein formation may occur.

PNLE2.question: Mrs. Ella Santoros is a 25 year old primigravida who has Rheumatic heart disease lesion. Her pregnancy has just been diagnosed. Her heart disease has not caused her to limit physical activity in the past. Her cardiac disease and functional capacity classification is:
PNLE2.rationale: Class I. Clients under class I has no physical activity limitation. There is a slight limitation of physical activity in class II, ordinary activity causes fatigue, palpitation, dyspnea or angina. Class III is moderate limitation of physical activity; less than ordinary activity causes fatigue. Unable to carry on any activity without experiencing discomfort is under class IV.

PNLE2.question: The client asks the nurse, “When will this soft spot at the top of the head of my baby will close?” The nurse should instruct the mother that the neonate’s anterior fontanel will normally close by age:
PNLE2.rationale: 12-18 months. Anterior fontanel closes at 12-18 months while posterior fontanel closes at birth until 2 months.

PNLE2.question: When a mother bleeds and the uterus is relaxed, soft and non-tender, you can account the cause to:
PNLE2.rationale: Atony of the uterus. Uterine atony, or relaxation of the uterus is the most frequent cause of postpartal hemorrhage. It is the inability to maintain the uterus in contracted state.

PNLE2.question: Mrs. Pichie Gonzales’s LMP began April 4, 2010. Her EDD should be which of the following:
PNLE2.rationale: January 11, 20111. Using the Nagel’s rule, he use this formula ( -3 calendar months + 7 days).

PNLE2.question: Which of the following prenatal laboratory test values would the nurse consider as significant?

choices.D: One hour glucose challenge test 110 g/dL

PNLE2.rationale: Rubella titer less than 1:8. A rubella titer should be 1:8 or greater. Thus, a finding of a titer less than 1:8 is significant, indicating that the client may not possess immunity to rubella. A hematocrit of 33.5%, WBC of 8,000/mm3, and a 1 hour glucose challenge test of 110 g/dL are within normal parameters.

PNLE2.question: Aling Patricia is a patient with preeclampsia. You advise her about her condition, which would tell you that she has not really understood your instructions?

choices.A: “I will restrict my fat in my diet.”
choices.B: “I will limit my activities and rest more frequently throughout the day.”
choices.C: “I will avoid salty foods in my diet.”
choices.D: “I will come more regularly for check-up.”

PNLE2.rationale: “I will limit my activities and rest more frequently throughout the day.”Pregnant woman with preeclampsia should be in a complete bed rest. When body is in recumbent position, sodium tends to be excreted at a faster rate. It is the best method of aiding increased excretion of sodium and encouraging diuresis. Rest should always be in a lateral recumbent position to avoid uterine pressure on the vena cava and prevent supine hypotension.

PNLE2.question: Mrs. Grace Evangelista is admitted with severe preeclampsia. What type of room should the nurse select this patient?

choices.B: The room farthest from the nursing station.
choices.C: The quietest room on the floor.

PNLE2.rationale: The quietest room on the floor.A loud noise such as a crying baby, or a dropped tray of equipment may be sufficient to trigger a seizure initiating eclampsia, a woman with severe preeclampsia should be admiotted to a private room so she can rest as undisturbed as possible. Darken the room if possible because bright light can trigger seizures.

PNLE2.question: During a prenatal check-up, the nurse explains to a client who is Rh negative that RhoGAM will be given:

choices.A: Weekly during the 8th month because this is her third pregnancy.
choices.B: uring the second trimester, if amniocentesis indicates a problem.
choices.C: To her infant immediately after delivery if the Coomb’s test is positive.
choices.D: Within 72 hours after delivery if infant is found to be Rh positive.

PNLE2.rationale: Within 72 hours after delivery if infant is found to be Rh positive. RhoGAM is given to Rh-negative mothers within 72 hours after birth of Rh-positive baby to prevent development of antibodies in the maternal blood stream, which will be fata to succeeding Rh-positive offspring.

PNLE2.question: A baby boy was born at 8:50pm. At 8:55pm, the heart rate was 99 bpm. She has a weak cry, irregular respiration. She was moving all extremities and only her hands and feet were still slightly blue. The nurse should enter the APGAR score as:
PNLE2.rationale: 6. Heart rate of 99 bpm-1; weak cry-1; irregular respiration-1; moving all extremities-2; extremities are slightly blue-1; with a total score of 6.

PNLE2.question: Billy is a 4 year old boy who has an IQ of 140 which means:
PNLE2.rationale: genius. IQ= mental age/chronological age x 100. Mental age refers to the typical intelligence level found for people at a give chronological age. OQ of 140 and above is considered genius.

PNLE2.question: A newborn is brought to the nursery. Upon assessment, the nurse finds that the child has short palpebral fissures, thinned upper lip. Based on this data, the nurse suspects that the newborn is MOST likely showing the effects of:
PNLE2.rationale: Fetal alcohol syndrome. The newborn with fetal alcohol syndrome has a number of possible problems at birth. Characteristics that mark the syndrome include pre and postnatal growth retardation; CNS involvement such as cognitive challenge, microcephally and cerebral palsy; and a distinctive facial feature of a short palpebral fissure and thin upper lip.

PNLE2.question: A priority nursing intervention for the infant with cleft lip is which of the following:
PNLE2.rationale: Monitoring for adequate nutritional intake. The infant with cleft lip is unable to create an adequate seal for sucking. The child is at risk for inadequate nutritional intake as well as aspiration.

PNLE2.question: Nurse Jacob is assessing a 12 year old who has hemophilia A. Which of the following assessment findings would the nurse anticipate?
PNLE2.rationale: a deficiency of clotting factor VIII. Hemophillia A (classic hemophilia) is a deficiency in factor VIII (an alpha globulin that stabilizes fibrin clots).

PNLE2.question: Celine, a mother of a 2 year old tells the nurse that her child “cries and has a fit when I have to leave him with a sitter or someone else.” Which of the following statements would be the nurse’s most accurate analysis of the mother’s comment?

choices.A: The child has not experienced limit-setting or structure.
choices.B: The child is expressing a physical need, such as hunger.
choices.C: The mother has nurtured overdependence in the child.
choices.D: The mother is describing her child’s separation anxiety.

PNLE2.rationale: The mother is describing her child’s separation anxiety. Before coming to any conclusion, the nurse should ask the mother focused questions; however, based on initial information, the analysis of separation anxiety would be most valid. Separation anxiety is a normal toddler response. When the child senses he is being sent away from those who most provide him with love and security. Crying is one way a child expresses a physical need; however, the nurse would be hasty in drawing this as first conclusion based on what the mother has said. Nurturing overdependence or not providing structure for the toddler are inaccurate conclusions based on the information provided.

PNLE2.question: Mylene Lopez, a 16 year old girl with scoliosis has recently received an invitation to a pool party. She asks the nurse how she can disguise her impairment when dressed in a bathing suit. Which nursing diagnosis can be justified by Mylene’s statement?
PNLE2.rationale: Body image disturbance. Mylene is experiencing uneasiness about the curvative of her spine, which will be more evident when she wears a bathing suit. This data suggests a body image disturbance. There is no evidence of anxiety or ineffective coping. The fact that Mylene is planning to attend a pool party dispels a diagnosis of social isolation.

PNLE2.question: The foul-smelling, frothy characteristic of the stool in cystic fibrosis results from the presence of large amounts of which of the following:
PNLE2.rationale: undigested fat. The client with cystic fibrosis absorbs fat poorly because of the think secretions blocking the pancreatic duct. The lack of natural pancreatic enzyme leads to poor absorption of predominantly fats in the duodenum. Foul-smelling, frothy stool is termed steatorrhea.

PNLE2.question: Which of the following would be a disadvantage of breast feeding?

choices.B: the incidence of allergies increases due to maternal antibodies
choices.C: the father may resent the infant’s demands on the mother’s body
choices.D: there is a greater chance of error during preparation

PNLE2.rationale: the father may resent the infant’s demands on the mother’s body. With breast feeding, the father’s body is not capable of providing the milk for the newborn, which may interfere with feeding the newborn, providing fewer chances for bonding, or he may be jealous of the infant’s demands on his wife time and body. Breast feeding is advantageous because uterine involution occurs more rapidly, thus minimizing blood loss. The presence of maternal antibodies in breast milk helps decrease the incidence of allergies in the newborn. A greater chance for error is associated with bottle feeding. No preparation required for breast feeding.

PNLE2.question: A client is noted to have lymphedema, webbed neck and low posterior hairline. Which of the following diagnoses is most appropriate?
PNLE2.rationale: Turner’s syndrome. Lymphedema, webbed neck and low posterior hairline, these are the 3 key assessment features in Turner’s syndrome. If the child is diagnosed early in age, proper treatment can be offered to the family. All newborns should be screened for possible congenital defects.

PNLE2.question: A 4 year old boy most likely perceives death in which way:

choices.A: n insignificant event unless taught otherwise
choices.B: Punishment for something the individual did
choices.C: Something that just happens to older people
choices.D: Temporary separation from the loved one.

PNLE2.rationale: Temporary separation from the loved one. The predominant perception of death by preschool age children is that death is temporary separation. Because that child is losing someone significant and will not see that person again, it’s inaccurate to infer death is insignificant, regardless of the child’s response.

PNLE2.question: Catherine Diaz is a 14 year old patient on a hematology unit who is being treated for sickle cell crisis. During a crisis such as that seen in sickle cell anemia, aldosterone release is stimulated. In what way might this influence Catherine’s fluid and electrolyte balance?

choices.A: sodium loss, water loss and potassium retention
choices.B: sodium loss, water los and potassium loss
choices.C: sodium retention, water loss and potassium retention
choices.D: sodium retention, water retention and potassium loss

PNLE2.rationale: sodium retention, water retention and potassium loss. Stress stimulates the adrenal cortex to increase the release of aldosterone. Aldosterone promotes the resorption of sodium, the retention of water and the loss of potassium.

PNLE3.question: A pregnant woman who is at term is admitted to the birthing unit in active labor. The client has only progressed from 2cm to 3 cm in 8 hours. She is diagnosed with hypotonic dystocia and the physician ordered Oxytocin (Pitocin) to augment her contractions. Which of the following is the most important aspect of nursing intervention at this time?

choices.A: Timing and recording length of contractions.
choices.C: Preparing for an emergency cesarean birth.

PNLE3.rationale: The oxytocic effect of Pitocin increases the intensity and durations of contractions; prolonged contractions will jeopardize the safetyof the fetus and necessitate discontinuing the drug.

PNLE3.question: A client who hallucinates is not in touch with reality. It is important for the nurse to:

choices.A: Isolate the client from other patients.
choices.C: Orient the client to time, place, and person.

PNLE3.rationale: It is of paramount importance to prevent the client from hurting himself or herself or others.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is caring to a child client who has had a tonsillectomy. The child complains of having dryness of the throat. Which of the following would the nurse give to the child?
PNLE3.rationale: After tonsillectomy, clear, cool liquids should be given. Citrus, carbonated, and hot or cold liquids should be avoided because they may irritate the throat. Red liquids should be avoided because they give the appearance of blood if the child vomits. Milk and milk products including pudding are avoided because they coat the throat, cause the child to clear the throat, and increase the risk of bleeding.

PNLE3.question: The physician ordered Phenylephrine (Neo-Synephrine) nasal spray to a 13-year-old client. The nurse caring to the client provides instructions that the nasal spray must be used exactly as directed to prevent the development of:
PNLE3.rationale: Phenylephrine, with frequent and continued use, can cause rebound congestion of mucous membranes.

PNLE3.question: A client with tuberculosis is to be admitted in the hospital. The nurse who will be assigned to care for the client must institute appropriate precautions. The nurse should:

choices.A: Place the client in a private room.
choices.B: Wear an N 95 respirator when caring for the client.
choices.C: Put on a gown every time when entering the room.
choices.D: on a surgical mask with a face shield when entering the room.

PNLE3.rationale: The N 95 respirator is a high-particulate filtration mask that meets the CDC performance criteria for a tuberculosis respirator.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following is the most frequent cause of noncompliance to the medical treatment of open-angle glaucoma?

choices.A: The frequent nausea and vomiting accompanying use of miotic drug.
choices.B: Loss of mobility due to severe driving restrictions.
choices.C: ecreased light and near-vision accommodation due to miotic effects of pilocarpine.
choices.D: The painful and insidious progression of this type of glaucoma.

PNLE3.rationale: The most frequent cause of noncompliance to the treatment of chronic, or open-angle glaucoma is the miotic effects of pilocarpine. Pupillary constriction impedes normal accommodation, making night driving difficult and hazardous, reducing the client’s ability to read for extended periods and making participation in games with fast-moving objects impossible.

PNLE3.question: In the morning shift, the nurse is making rounds in the nursing care units. The nurse enters in a client’s room and notes that the client’s tube has become disconnected from the Pleurovac. What would be the initial nursing action?

choices.A: pply pressure directly over the incision site.
choices.B: lamp the chest tube near the incision site.
