choices.C: lamp the chest tube closer to the drainage system.
choices.D: Reconnect the chest tube to the Pleurovac.

PNLE3.rationale: This stops the sucking of air through the tube and prevents the entry of contaminants. In addition, clamping near the chest wall provides for some stability and may prevent the clamp from pulling on the chest tube.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following complications during a breech birth the nurse needs to be alarmed?
PNLE3.rationale: Because umbilical cord’s insertion site is born before the fetal head, the cord may be compressed by the after-coming head in a breech birth.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is caring to a client diagnosed with severe depression. Which of the following nursing approach is important in depression?

choices.A: Protect the client against harm to others.
choices.B: Provide the client with motor outlets for aggressive, hostile feelings.
choices.D: eemphasizing preoccupation with elimination, nourishment, and sleep.

PNLE3.rationale: It is important to externalize the anger away from self.

PNLE3.question: A 3-month-old client is in the pediatric unit. During assessment, the nurse is suspecting that the baby may have hypothyroidism when mother states that her baby does not:

choices.B: Pick up and hold a rattle.

PNLE3.rationale: Development normally proceeds cephalocaudally; so the first major developmental milestone that the infant achieves is the ability to hold the head up within the first 8-12 weeks of life. In hypothyroidism, the infant’s muscle tone would be poor and the infant would not be able to achieve this milestone.

PNLE3.question: The physician calls the nursing unit to leave an order. The senior nurse had conversation with the other staff. The newly hired nurse answers the phone so that the senior nurses may continue their conversation. The new nurse does not knowthe physician or the client to whom the order pertains. The nurse should:

choices.A: sk the physician to call back after the nurse has read the hospital policy manual.
choices.C: Refuse to take the telephone order.
choices.D: sk the charge nurse or one of the other senior staff nurses to take the telephone order.

PNLE3.rationale: Get a senior nurse who know s the policies, the client, and the doctor. Generally speaking, a nurse should not accept telephone orders. However, if it is necessary to take one, follow the hospital’s policy regarding telephone orders. Failure to followhospital policy could be considered negligence. In this case, the nurse was new and did not know the hospital’s policy concerning telephone orders. The nurse was also unfamiliar with the doctor and the client. Therefore the nurse should not take the order unless a) no one else is available and b) it is an emergency situation.

PNLE3.question: The staff nurse on the labor and delivery unit is assigned to care to a primigravida in transition complicated by hypertension. A new pregnant woman in active labor is admitted in the same unit. The nurse manager assigned the same nurse to the second client. The nurse feels that the client with hypertension requires one-to-one care. What would be the initial actionof the nurse?

choices.A: ccept the new assignment and complete an incident report describing a shortage of nursing staff.
choices.B: Report the incident to the nursing supervisor and request to be floated.
choices.C: Report the nursing assessment of the client in transitional labor to the nurse manager and discuss misgivings about the new assignment.
choices.D: ccept the new assignment and provide the best care.

PNLE3.rationale: The nurse is obligated to inform the nurse manager about changes in the condition of the client, which may change the decision made by the nurse manager.

PNLE3.question: A newborn infant with Down syndrome is to be discharged today. The nurse is preparing to give the discharge teaching regarding the proper care at home. The nurse would anticipate that the mother is probably at the:
PNLE3.rationale: Perinatal risk factors for the development of Down syndrome include advanced maternal age, especially with the first pregnancy.

PNLE3.question: The emergency department has shortage of staff. The nurse manager informs the staff nurse in the critical care unit that she has to float to the emergency department. What should the staff nurse expect under these conditions?

choices.A: The float staff nurse will be informed of the situation before the shift begins.
choices.B: The staff nurse will be able to negotiate the assignments in the emergency department.
choices.C: ross training will be available for the staff nurse.
choices.D: lient assignments will be equally divided among the nurses.

PNLE3.rationale: Assignments should be based on scope of practice and expertise.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is assigned to care for a child client admitted in the pediatrics unit. The client is receiving digoxin. Which of the following questions will be asked by the nurse to the parents of the child in order to assess the client’s risk for digoxin toxicity?

choices.A: “Has he been exposed to any childhood communicable diseases in the past 2-3 weeks?”
choices.B: “Has he been taking diuretics at home?”
choices.C: “Do any of his brothers and sisters have history of cardiac problems?”
choices.D: “Has he been going to school regularly?”

PNLE3.rationale: The child who is concurrently taking digoxin and diuretics is at increased risk for digoxin toxicity due to the loss of potassium. The child and parents should be taught what foods are high in potassium, and the child should be encouraged to eat a high-potassium diet. In addition, the child’s serum potassium level should be carefully monitored.

PNLE3.question: The nurse noticed that the signed consent form has an error. The form states, “Amputation of the right leg” instead of the left leg that is to be amputated. The nurse has administered already the preoperative medications. What should the nurse do?

choices.A: all the physician to reschedule the surgery.
choices.B: all the nearest relative to come in to sign a new form.
choices.C: ross out the error and initial the form.
choices.D: Have the client sign another form.

PNLE3.rationale: The responsible for an accurate informed consent is the physician. An exception to this answer would be a life-threatening emergency, but there are no data to support another response.

PNLE3.question: The nurse in the nursing care unit checks the fluctuation in the water-seal compartment of a closed chest drainage system. The fluctuation has stopped, the nurse would:

choices.A: Vigorously strip the tube to dislodge a clot.
choices.B: Raise the apparatus above the chest to move fluid.
choices.C: Increase wall suction above 20 cm H2O pressure.
choices.D: sk the client to cough and take a deep breath.

PNLE3.rationale: Asking the client to cough and take a deep breath will help determine if the chest tube is kinked or if the lungs has reexpanded.

PNLE3.question: The pediatric nurse in the neonatal unit was informed that the baby that is brought to the mother in the hospital room is wrong. The nurse determines that two babies were placed in the wrong cribs. The most appropriate nursing action would be to:

choices.A: etermine who is responsible for the mistake and terminate his or her employment.
choices.B: Record the event in an incident/variance report and notify the nursing supervisor.
choices.C: Reassure both mothers, report to the charge nurse, and do not record.
choices.D: Record detailed notes of the event on the mother’s medical record.

PNLE3.rationale: Every event that exposes a client to harm should be recorded in an incident report, as well as reported to the appropriate supervisors in order to resolve the current problems and permit the institution to prevent the problem from happening again.

PNLE3.question: Before the administration of digoxin, the nurse completes an assessment to a toddler client for signs and symptoms of digoxin toxicity. Which of the following is the earliest and most significant sign of digoxin toxicity?
PNLE3.rationale: One of the earliest signs of digoxin toxicity is Bradycardia. For a toddler, any heart rate that falls below the norm of about 100-120 bpm would indicate Bradycardia and would necessitate holding the medication and notifying the physician.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following treatment modality is appropriate for a client with paranoid tendency?
PNLE3.rationale: This option is least threatening.

PNLE3.question: The client with rheumatoid arthritis is for discharge. In preparing the client for discharge on prednisone therapy, the nurse should advise the client to:

choices.A: Wear sunglasses if exposed to bright light for an extended period of time.
choices.B: Take oral preparations of prednisone before meals.
choices.C: Have periodic complete blood counts while on the medication.
choices.D: Never stop or change the amount of the medication without medical advice.

PNLE3.rationale: In preparing the client for discharge that is receiving prednisone, the nurse should caution the client to (a) take oral preparations after meals; (b) remember that routine checks of vital signs, weight, and lab studies are critical; (c) NEVER STOP OR CHANGE THE AMOUNT OF MEDICATION WITHOUT MEDICAL ADVICE; (d) store the medication in a light-resistant container.

PNLE3.question: A pregnant client tells the nurse that she is worried about having urinary frequency. What will be the most appropriate nursing response?

choices.A: “Try using Kegel (perineal) exercises and limiting fluids before bedtime. If you have frequency associated with fever, pain on voiding, or blood in the urine, call your doctor/nurse-midwife.
choices.B: “Placental progesterone causes irritability of the bladder sphincter. Your symptoms will go away after the baby comes.”
choices.C: “Pregnant women urinate frequently to get rid of fetal wastes. Limit fluids to 1L/daily.”
choices.D: “Frequency is due to bladder irritation from concentrate urine and is normal in pregnancy. Increase your daily fluid intake to 3L.”

PNLE3.rationale: Progesterone also reduces smooth muscle motility in the urinary tract and predisposes the pregnant woman to urinary tract infections. Women should contact their doctors if they exhibit signs of infection. Kegel exercise will help strengthen the perineal muscles; limiting fluids at bedtime reduces the possibility of being awakened by the necessity of voiding.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following will help the nurse determine that the expression of hostility is useful?

choices.A: Expression of anger dissipates the energy.
choices.B: Energy from anger is used to accomplish what needs to be done.
choices.D: egree of hostility is less than the provocation.

PNLE3.rationale: This is the proper use of anger.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is providing an orientation regarding case management to the nursing students. Which characteristics should the nurse include in the discussion in understanding case management?

choices.A: Main objective is a written plan that combines discipline-specific processes used to measure outcomes of care.
choices.B: Main purpose is to identify expected client, family and staff performance against the timeline for clients with the same diagnosis.
choices.C: Main focus is comprehensive coordination of client care, avoid unnecessary duplication of services, improve resource utilization and decrease cost.
choices.D: Primary goal is to understand why predicted outcomes have not been met and the correction of identified problems.

PNLE3.rationale: There are several models of case management, but the commonality is comprehensive coordination of care to better predict needs of high-risk clients, decrease exacerbations and continually monitor progress overtime.

PNLE3.question: The physician orders a dose of IV phenytoin to a child client. In preparing in the administration of the drug, which nursing action is not correct?

choices.A: Infuse the phenytoin into a smaller vein to prevent purple glove syndrome.
choices.B: heck the phenytoin solution to be sure it is clear or light yellow in color, never cloudy.
choices.C: Plan to give phenytoin over 30-60 minutes, using an in-line filter.
choices.D: Flush the IV tubing with normal saline before starting phenytoin.

PNLE3.rationale: Phenytoin should be infused or injected into larger veins to avoid the discoloration know as purple glove syndrome; infusing into a smaller vein is not appropriate.

PNLE3.question: The pregnant woman visits the clinic for check –up. Which assessment findings will help the nurse determine that the client is in 8-week gestation?
PNLE3.rationale: Serum radioimmunoassay (RIA) is accurate within 7days of conception. This test is specific for HCG, and accuracy is not compromised by confusion with LH.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following nursing intervention is essential for the client who had pneumonectomy?

choices.A: Medicate for pain only when needed.
choices.B: onnect the chest tube to water-seal drainage.
choices.C: Notify the physician if the chest drainage exceeds 100mL/hr.

PNLE3.rationale: Surgery and anesthesia can increase mucus production. Deep breathing and coughing are essential to prevent atelectasis and pneumonia in the client’s only remaining lung.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is providing a health teaching to a group of parents regarding Chlamydia trachomatis. The nurse is correct in the statement, “Chlamydia trachomatis is not only an intracellular bacterium that causes neonatal conjunctivitis, but it also can cause:

choices.A: iscoloration of baby and adult teeth.
choices.C: Snuffles and rhagades in the newborn.

PNLE3.rationale: Newborns can get pneumonia (tachypnea, mild hypoxia, cough, eosinophilia) and conjunctivitis from Chlamydia.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is assigned to care to a 17-year-old male client with a history of substance abuse. The client asks the nurse, “Have you ever tried or used drugs?” The most correct response of the nurse would be:

choices.C: “Why do you want to know that?”

PNLE3.rationale: The client may perceive this as avoidance, but it is more important to redirect back to the client, especially in light of the manipulative behavior of drug abusers and adolescents.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following describes a health care team with the principles of participative leadership?

choices.A: Each member of the team can independently make decisions regarding the client’s care without necessarily consulting the other members.
choices.B: The physician makes most of the decisions regarding the client’s care.
choices.C: The team uses the expertise of its members to influence the decisions regarding the client’s care.
choices.D: Nurses decide nursing care; physicians decide medical and other treatment for the client.

PNLE3.rationale: It describes a democratic process in which all members have input in the client’s care.

PNLE3.question: A nurse is giving a health teaching to a woman who wants to breastfeed her newborn baby. Which hormone, normally secreted during the postpartum period, influences both the milk ejection reflex and uterine involution?
PNLE3.rationale: Contraction of the milk ducts and let-down reflex occur under the stimulation of oxytocin released by the posterior pituitary gland.

PNLE3.question: One staff nurse is assigned to a group of 5 patients for the 12-hour shift. The nurse is responsible for the overall planning, giving and evaluating care during the entire shift. After the shift, same responsibility will be endorsed to the next nurse in charge. This describes nursing care delivered via the:
PNLE3.rationale: In case management, the nurse assumes total responsibility for meeting the needs of the client during the entire time on duty.

PNLE3.question: The ambulance team calls the emergency department that they are going to bring a client who sustained burns in a house fire. While waiting for the ambulance, the nurse will anticipate emergency care to include assessment for:
PNLE3.rationale: Smoke inhalation affects gas exchange.

PNLE3.question: Most couples are using “natural” family planning methods. Most accidental pregnancies in couples preferred to use this method have been related to unprotected intercourse before ovulation. Which of the following factor explains why pregnancy may be achieved by unprotected intercourse during the preovulatory period?
PNLE3.rationale: Sperm deposited during intercourse may remain viable for about 3 days. If ovulation occurs during this period, conception may result.

PNLE3.question: An older adult client wakes up at 2 o’clock in the morning and comes to the nurse’s station saying, “I am having difficulty in sleeping.” What is the best nursing response to the client?

choices.A: “I’ll give you a sleeping pill to help you get more sleep now.”
choices.B: “Perhaps you’d like to sit here at the nurse’s station for a while.”
choices.C: “Would you like me to show you where the bathroom is?”

PNLE3.rationale: This option shows acceptance (key concept) of this age-typical sleep pattern (that of waking in the early morning).

PNLE3.question: The nurse is taking care of a multipara who is at 42 weeks of gestation and in active labor, her membranes ruptured spontaneously 2 hours ago. While auscultating for the point of maximum intensity of fetal heart tones before applying an external fetal monitor, the nurse counts 100 beats per minute. The immediate nursing action is to:

choices.A: Start oxygen by mask to reduce fetal distress.
choices.B: Examine the woman for signs of a prolapsed cord.
choices.C: Turn the woman on her left side to increase placental perfusion.
choices.D: Take the woman’s radial pulse while still auscultating the FHR.

PNLE3.rationale: Taking the mother’s pulse while listening to the FHR will differentiate between the maternal and fetal heart rates and rule out fetal Bradycardia.

PNLE3.question: The nurse must instruct a client with glaucoma to avoid taking over-the-counter medications like:
PNLE3.rationale: Antihistamines cause pupil dilation and should be avoided with glaucoma.

PNLE3.question: A male client is brought to the emergency department due to motor vehicle accident. While monitoring the client, the nurse suspects increasing intracranial pressure when:

choices.A: lient is oriented when aroused from sleep, and goes back to sleep immediately.
choices.B: lood pressure is decreased from 160/90 to 110/70.
choices.C: lient refuses dinner because of anorexia.
choices.D: Pulse is increased from 88-96 with occasional skipped beat.

PNLE3.rationale: This suggests that the level of consciousness is decreasing.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is conducting a lecture to a class of nursing students about advance directives to preoperative clients. Which of the following statement by the nurse js correct?

choices.A: “The spouse, but not the rest of the family, may override the advance directive.”
choices.B: “An advance directive is required for a “do not resuscitate” order.”
choices.C: “A durable power of attorney, a form of advance directive, may only be held by a blood relative.”
choices.D: “The advance directive may be enforced even in the face of opposition by the spouse.”

PNLE3.rationale: An advance directive is a form of informed consent, and only a competent adult or the holder of a durable power of attorney has the right to consent or refuse treatment. If the spouse does not hold the power of attorney, the decisions of the holder, even if opposed by the spouse, are enforced.

PNLE3.question: A client diagnosed with schizophrenia is shouting and banging on the door leading to the outside, saying, “I need to go to an appointment.” What is the appropriate nursing intervention?

choices.A: Tell the client that he cannot bang on the door.
choices.C: Escort the client going back into the room.
choices.D: sk the client to move away from the door.

PNLE3.rationale: Gentle but firm guidance and nonverbal direction is needed to intervene when a client with schizophrenic symptoms is being disruptive.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following action is an accurate tracheal suctioning technique?

choices.A: 25 seconds of continuous suction during catheter insertion.
choices.B: 20 seconds of continuous suction during catheter insertion.
choices.C: 10 seconds of intermittent suction during catheter withdrawal.
choices.D: 15 seconds of intermittent suction during catheter withdrawal.

PNLE3.rationale: Suctioning is only done for 10 seconds, intermittently, as the catheter is being withdrawn.

PNLE3.question: The client’s jaw and cheekbone is sutured and wired. The nurse anticipates that the most important thing that must be ready at the bedside is:
PNLE3.rationale: The priority for this client is being able to establish an airway.

PNLE3.question: A mother is in the third stage of labor. Which of the following signs will help the nurse determine the signs of placental separation?

choices.C: The fundus appears at the introitus.

PNLE3.rationale: Signs of placental separation include a change in the shape of the uterus from ovoid to globular.

PNLE3.question: After therapy with the thrombolytic alteplase (t-PA), what observation will the nurse report to the physician?

choices.B: hange in level of consciousness and headache.

PNLE3.rationale: This could indicate intracranial bleeding. Alteplase is a thrombolytic enzyme that lyses thrombi and emboli. Bleeding is an adverse effect. Monitor clotting times and signs of any gastrointestinal or internal bleeding.

PNLE3.question: A client who undergone left nephrectomy has a large flank incision. Which of the following nursing action will facilitate deep breathing and coughing?

choices.A: Push fluid administration to loosen respiratory secretions.
choices.B: Have the client lie on the unaffected side.
choices.C: Maintain the client in high Fowler’s position.
choices.D: oordinate breathing and coughing exercise with administration of analgesics.

PNLE3.rationale: Because flank incision in nephrectomy is directly below the diaphragm, deep breathing is painful. Additionally, there is a greater incisional pull each time the person moves than there is with abdominal surgery. Incisional pain following nephrectomy generally requires analgesics administration every 3-4 hours for 24-48 hours after surgery. Therefore, turning, coughing and deep-breathing exercises should be planned to maximize the analgesic effects.

PNLE3.question: The community nurse is teaching the group of mothers about the cervical mucus method of natural family planning. Which characteristics are typical of the cervical mucus during the “fertile” period of the menstrual cycle?
PNLE3.rationale: Under high estrogen levels, during the period surrounding ovulation, the cervical mucus becomes thin, clear, and elastic (spinnbarkeit), facilitating sperm passage.

PNLE3.question: A client with ruptured appendix had surgery an hour ago and is transferred to the nursing care unit. The nurse placed the client in a semi-Fowler’s position primarily to:

choices.A: Facilitate movement and reduce complications from immobility.
choices.D: Promote drainage and prevent subdiaphragmatic abscesses.

PNLE3.rationale: After surgery for a ruptured appendix, the client should be placed in a semi-Fowler’s position to promote drainage and to prevent possible complications.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following will best describe a management function?

choices.A: Writing a letter to the editor of a nursing journal.
choices.C: irecting and evaluating nursing staff members.
choices.D: Explaining medication side effects to a client.

PNLE3.rationale: Directing and evaluation of staff is a major responsibility of a nursing manager.

PNLE3.question: The parents of an infant client ask the nurse to teach them how to administer Cortisporin eye drops. The nurse is correct in advising the parents to place the drops:

choices.A: In the middle of the lower conjunctival sac of the infant’s eye.
choices.C: In the outer canthus of the infant’s eye.
choices.D: In the inner canthus of the infant’s eye.

PNLE3.rationale: The recommended procedure for administering eyedrops to any client calls for the drops to be placed in the middle of the lower conjunctival sac.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is assessing on the client who is admitted due to vehicle accident. Which of the following findings will help the nurse that there is internal bleeding?
PNLE3.rationale: Thirst and restlessness indicate hypovolemia and hypoxemia. Internal bleeding is difficult to recognized and evaluate because it is not apparent.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is completing an assessment to a newborn baby boy. The nurse observes that the skin of the newborn is dry and flaking and there are several areas of an apparent macular rash. The nurse charts this as:
PNLE3.rationale: Erythema toxicum is the normal, nonpathological macular newborn rash.

PNLE3.question: The client is brought to the emergency department because of serious vehicle accident. After an hour, the client has been declared brain dead. The nurse who has been with the client must now talk to the family about organ donation. Which of the following consideration is necessary?

choices.A: Include as many family members as possible.
choices.B: Take the family to the chapel.
choices.D: larify the family’s understanding of brain death.

PNLE3.rationale: The family needs to understand what brain death is before talking about organ donation. They need time to accept the death of their family member. An environment conducive to discussing an emotional issue is needed.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is teaching exercises that are good for pregnant women increasing tone and fitness and decreasing lower backache. Which of the following should the nurse exclude in the exercise program?

choices.A: Stand with legs apart and touch hands to floor three times per day.
choices.B: Ten minutes of walking per day with an emphasis on good posture.
choices.C: Ten minutes of swimming or leg kicking in pool per day.
choices.D: Pelvic rock exercise and squats three times a day.

PNLE3.rationale: Bending from the waist in pregnancy tends to make backache worse.

PNLE3.question: A client with obsessive-compulsive behavior is admitted in the psychiatric unit. The nurse taking care of the client knows that the primary treatment goal is to:
PNLE3.rationale: Support and limit setting decrease anxiety and provide external control.

PNLE3.question: After ileostomy, the nurse expects that the drainage appliance will be applied to the stoma:

choices.A: When the client is able to begin self-care procedures.
choices.B: 24 hours later, when the swelling subsided.
choices.C: In the operating room after the ileostomy procedure.
choices.D: fter the ileostomy begins to function.

PNLE3.rationale: The stoma drainage bag is applied in the operating room. Drainage from the ileostomy contains secretions that are rich in digestive enzymes and highly irritating to the skin. Protection of the skin from the effects of these enzymes is begun at once. Skin exposed to these enzymes even for a short time becomes reddened, painful and excoriated.

PNLE3.question: A female client who has a 28-day menstrual cycle asks the community health nurse when she get pregnant during her cycle. What will be the best nursing response?

choices.A: It is impossible to determine the fertile period reliably. So it is best to assume that a woman is always fertile.
choices.B: In a 28-day cycle, ovulation occurs at or about day 14. The egg lives for about 24 hours and the sperm live for about 72 hours. The fertile period would be approximately between day 11 and day 15.
choices.C: In a 28- day cycle, ovulation occurs at or about day 14. The egg lives for about 72 hours and the sperm live for about 24 hours. The fertile period would be approximately between day 13 and 17.
choices.D: In a 28-day cycle, ovulation occurs 8 days before the next period or at about day 20. The fertile period is between day 20 and the beginning of the next period.

PNLE3.rationale: It is the most accurate statement of physiological facts for a 28-day menstrual cycle: ovulation at day 14, egg life span 24 hours, sperm life span of 72 hours. Fertilization could occur from sperm deposited before ovulation.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following statement describes the role of a nurse as a client advocate?

choices.A: nurse may override clients’ wishes for their own good.
choices.B: nurse has the moral obligation to prevent harm and do well for clients.
choices.C: nurse helps clients gain greater independence and self-determination.
choices.D: nurse measures the risk and benefits of various health situations while factoring in cost.

PNLE3.rationale: An advocate role encourage freedom of choice, includes speaking out for the client, and supports the client’s best interests.

PNLE3.question: A community health nurse is providing a health teaching to a woman infected with herpes simplex 2. Which of the following health teaching must the nurse include to reduce the chances of transmission of herpes simplex 2?

choices.C: “Penicillin is the drug of choice for treatment.”
choices.D: “The organism is associated with later development of hydatidiform mole.

PNLE3.rationale: Abstinence will eliminate any unnecessary pain during intercourse and will reduce the possibility of transmitting infection to one’s sexual partner.

PNLE3.question: The nurse in the psychiatric ward informed the male client that he will be attending the 9:00 AM group therapy sessions. The client tells the nurse that he must wash his hands from 9:00 to 9:30 AM each day and therefore he cannot attend. Which concept does the nursing staff need to keep in mind in planning nursing intervention for this client?

choices.B: Fear and tensions are often expressed in disguised form through symbolic processes.
choices.D: Unmet needs are discharged through ritualistic behavior.

PNLE3.rationale: Anxiety is generated by group therapy at 9:00 AM. The ritualistic behavioral defense of hand washing decreases anxiety by avoiding group therapy.

PNLE3.question: The nurse assesses the health condition of the female client. The client tells the nurse that she discovered a lump in the breast last year and hesitated to seek medical advice. The nurse understands that, women who tend to delay seeking medical advice after discovering the disease are displaying what common defense mechanism?
PNLE3.rationale: Denial is a very strong defense mechanism used to allay the emotional effects of discovering a potential threat. Although denial has been found to be an effective mechanism for survival in some instances, such as during natural disasters, it may in greater pathology in a woman with potential breast carcinoma.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following situations cannot be delegated by the registered nurse to the nursing assistant?

choices.A: postoperative client who is stable needs to ambulate.
choices.B: lient in soft restraint who is very agitated and crying.
choices.C: confused elderly woman who needs assistance with eating.
choices.D: Routine temperature check that must be done for a client at end of shift.

PNLE3.rationale: The registered nurse cannot delegate the responsibility for assessment and evaluation of clients. The status of the client in restraint requires further assessment to determine if there are additional causes for the behavior.

PNLE3.question: In the admission care unit, which of the following client would the nurse give immediate attention?

choices.A: client who is 3 days postoperative with left calf pain.
choices.B: client who is postoperative hip pinning who is complaining of pain.
choices.C: New admitted client with chest pain.
choices.D: client with diabetes who has a glucoscan reading of 180.

PNLE3.rationale: The client with chest pain may be having a myocardial infarction, and immediate assessment and intervention is a priority.

PNLE3.question: A couple seeks medical advice in the community health care unit. A couple has been unable to conceive; the man is being evaluated for possible problems. The physician ordered semen analysis. Which of the following instructions is correct regarding collection of a sperm specimen?

choices.A: ollect a specimen at the clinic, place in iced container, and give to laboratory personnel immediately.
choices.B: ollect specimen after 48-72 hours of abstinence and bring to clinic within 2 hours.
choices.C: ollect specimen in the morning after 24 hours of abstinence and bring to clinic immediately.
choices.D: ollect specimen at night, refrigerate, and bring to clinic the next morning.

PNLE3.rationale: Is correct because semen analysis requires that a freshly masturbated specimen be obtained after a rest (abstinence) period of 48-72 hours.

PNLE3.question: The physician ordered Betamethasone to a pregnant woman at 34 weeks of gestation with sign of preterm labor. The nurse expects that the drug will:
PNLE3.rationale: Betamethasone, a form of cortisone, acts on the fetal lungs to produce surfactant.

PNLE3.question: A tracheostomy cuff is to be deflated, which of the following nursing intervention should be implemented before starting the procedures?
PNLE3.rationale: Secretions may have pooled above the tracheostomy cuff. If these are not suctioned before deflation, the secretions may be aspirated.

PNLE3.question: A client is diagnosed with Tuberculosis and respiratory isolation is initiated. This means that:

choices.A: Gloves are worn when handling the client’s tissue, excretions, and linen.
choices.B: oth client and attending nurse must wear masks at all times.
choices.C: Nurse and visitors must wear masks until chemotherapy is begun. Client is instructed in cough and tissue techniques.
choices.D: Full isolation; that is, caps and gowns are required during the period of contagion.

PNLE3.rationale: Proper handling of sputum is essential to allay droplet transference of bacilli in the air. Clients need to be taught to cover their nose and mouth with tissues when sneezing or coughing. Chemotherapy generally renders the client noninfectious within days to a few weeks, usually before cultures for tubercle bacilli are negative. Until chemical isolation is established, many institutions require the client to wear a mask when visitors are in the room or when the nurse is in attendance. Client should be in a well-ventilated room, without air recirculation, to prevent air contamination.

PNLE3.question: A client with lung cancer is admitted in the nursing care unit. The husband wants to know the condition of his wife. How should the nurse respond to the husband?

choices.A: Find out what information he already has.
choices.B: Suggest that he discuss it with his wife.
choices.D: Refer him to the nurse in charge.

PNLE3.rationale: It is best to establish baseline information first.

PNLE3.question: A hospitalized client cannot find his handkerchief and accuses other cient in the room and the nurse of stealing them. Which is the most therapeutic approach to this client?

choices.B: Listen without reinforcing the client’s belief.
choices.C: Inject humor to defuse the intensity.
choices.D: Logically point out that the client is jumping to conclusions.

PNLE3.rationale: Listening is probably the most effective response of the four choices.

PNLE3.question: After a cystectomy and formation of an ileal conduit, the nurse provides instruction regarding prevention of leakage of the pouch and backflow of the urine. The nurse is correct to include in the instruction to empty the urine pouch:
PNLE3.rationale: Urine flow is continuous. The pouch has an outlet valve for easy drainage every 3-4 hours. (the pouch should be changed every 3-5 days, or sooner if the adhesive is loose).

PNLE3.question: Which telephone call from a student’s mother should the school nurse take care of at once?

choices.A: telephone call notifying the school nurse that the child’ pediatrician has informed the mother that the child will need cardiac repair surgery within the next few weeks.
choices.B: telephone call notifying the school nurse that the child’s pediatrician has informed the mother that the child has head lice.
choices.C: telephone call notifying the school nurse that a child has a temperature of 102ºF and a rash covering the trunk and upper extremities of the body.
choices.D: telephone call notifying the school nurse that a child underwent an emergency appendectomy during the previous night.

PNLE3.rationale: A high fever accompanied by a body rash could indicate that the child has a communicable disease and would have exposed other students to the infection. The school nurse would want to investigate this telephone call immediately so that plans could be instituted to control the spread of such infection.

PNLE3.question: Which of the following signs and symptoms that require immediate attention and may indicate most serious complications during pregnancy?

choices.A: Severe abdominal pain or fluid discharge from the vagina.
choices.B: Excessive saliva, “bumps around the areolae, and increased vaginal mucus.
choices.C: Fatigue, nausea, and urinary frequency at any time during pregnancy.
choices.D: nkle edema, enlarging varicosities, and heartburn.

PNLE3.rationale: Severe abdominal pain may indicate complications of pregnancy such as abortion, ectopic pregnancy, or abruption placenta; fluid discharge from the vagina may indicate premature rupture of the membrane.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is assessing the newborn boy. Apgar scores are 7 and 9. The newborn becomes slightly cyanotic. What is the initial nursing action?

choices.A: Elevate his head to promote gravity drainage of secretions.
choices.B: Wrap him in another blanket, to reduce heat loss.
choices.C: Stimulate him to cry,, to increase oxygenation.
choices.D: spirate his mouth and nose with bulb syringe.

PNLE3.rationale: Gentle aspiration of mucus helps maintain a patent airway, required for effective gas exchange.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is formulating a plan of care to a client with a somatoform disorder. The nurse needs to have knowledge of which psychodynamic principle?

choices.A: The symptoms of a somatoform disorder are an attempt to adjust to painful life situations or to cope with conflicting sexual, aggressive, or dependent feelings.
choices.B: The major fundamental mechanism is regression.
choices.C: The client’s symptoms are imaginary and the suffering is faked.
choices.D: n extensive, prolonged study of the symptoms will be reassuring to the client, who seeks sympathy, attention and love.

PNLE3.rationale: Somatoform disorders provide a way of coping with conflicts.

PNLE3.question: An infant is brought to the health care clinic for three immunizations at the same time. The nurse knows that hepatitis B, DPT, and Haemophilus influenzae type B immunizations should:

choices.A: e drawn in the same syringe and given in one injection.
choices.B: e mixed and inject in the same sites.
choices.C: Not be mixed and the nurse must give three injections in three sites.
choices.D: e mixed and the nurse must give the injection in three sites.

PNLE3.rationale: Immunization should never be mixed together in a syringe, thus necessitating three separate injections in three sites. Note: some manufacturers make a premixed combination of immunization that is safe and effective.

PNLE3.question: A female client with cancer has radium implants. The nurse wants to maintain the implants in the correct position. The nurse should position the client:

choices.C: With the foot of the bed elevated.

PNLE3.rationale: Clients with radioactive implants should be positioned flat in bed to prevent dislodgement of the vaginal packing. The client may roll to the side for meals but the upper body should not be raised more than 20 degrees.

PNLE3.question: The nurse wants to know if the mother of a toddler understands the instructions regarding the administration of syrup of ipecac. Which of the following statement will help the nurse to know that the mother needs additional teaching?

choices.A: “I’ll give the medicine if my child gets into some toilet bowl cleaner.”
choices.B: “I’ll give the medicine if my child gets into some aspirin.”
choices.C: “I’ll give the medicine if my child gets into some plant bulbs.”
choices.D: “I’ll give the medicine if my child gets into some vitamin pills.”

PNLE3.rationale: Syrup of ipecac is not administered when the ingested substances is corrosive in nature. Toilet bowl cleaners, as a collective whole, are highly corrosive substances. If the ingested substance “burned” the esophagus going down, it will “burn” the esophagus coming back up when the child begins to vomit after administration of syrup of ipecac.

PNLE3.question: To assess if the cranial nerve VII of the client was damaged, which changes would not be expected?

choices.A: rooling and drooping of the mouth.
choices.B: Inability to open eyelids on operative side.
choices.C: Sagging of the face on the operative side.
choices.D: Inability to close eyelid on operative side.

PNLE3.rationale: Inability to open eyelids on operative side is seen with cranial nerve III damage.

PNLE3.question: The community health nurse makes a home visit to a family. During the visit, the nurse observes that the mother is beating her child. What is the priority nursing intervention in this situation?

choices.B: Report the incident to protective agencies.
choices.C: Refer the family to appropriate support group.
choices.D: ssist the family to identify stressors and use of other coping mechanisms to prevent further incidents.

PNLE3.rationale: Assessment of physical injuries (like bruises, lacerations, bleeding and fractures) is the first priority.

PNLE3.question: The nurse in the neonatal care unit is supervising the actions of a certified nursing assistant in giving care to the newborns. The nursing assistant mistakenly gives a formula feeding to a newborn that is on water feeding only. The nurse is responsible for the mistake of the nursing assistant:

choices.A: lways, as a representative of the institution.
choices.B: lways, because nurses who supervise less-trained individuals are responsible for their mistakes.
choices.C: If the nurse failed to determine whether the nursing assistant was competent to take care of the client.
choices.D: Only if the nurse agreed that the newborn could be fed formula.

PNLE3.rationale: The nurse who is supervising others has a legal obligation to determine that they are competent to perform the assignment, as well as legal obligation to provide adequate supervision.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is assigned to care for a client with urinary calculi. Fluid intake of 2L/day is encouraged to the client. the primary reason for this is to:

choices.A: Reduce the size of existing stones.
choices.B: Prevent crystalline irritation to the ureter.
choices.C: Reduce the size of existing stones
choices.D: Increase the hydrostatic pressure in the urinary tract.

PNLE3.rationale: Increasing hydrostatic pressure in the urinary tract will facilitate passage of the calculi.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is counseling a couple in their mid 30’s who have been unable to conceive for about 6 months. They are concerned that one or both of them may be infertile. What is the best advice the nurse could give to the couple?

choices.A: “it is no unusual to take 6-12 months to get pregnant, especially when the partners are in their mid-30s. Eat well, exercise, and avoid stress.”
choices.B: “Start planning adoption. Many couples get pregnant when they are trying to adopt.”
choices.C: “Consult a fertility specialist and start testing before you get any older.”
choices.D: “Have sex as often as you can, especially around the time of ovulation, to increase your chances of pregnancy.”

PNLE3.rationale: Infertility is not diagnosed until atleast 12months of unprotected intercourse has failed to produce a pregnancy. Older couples will experience a longer time to get pregnant.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is caring for a cient who Is a retired nurse. A 24-hour urine collection for Creatinine clearance is to be done. The client tells the nurse, “I can’t remember what this test is for.” The best response by the nurse is:

choices.A: “It provides a way to see if you are passing any protein in your urine.”
choices.B: “It tells how well the kidneys filter wastes from the blood.”
choices.C: “It tells if your renal insufficiency has affected your heart.”
choices.D: “The test measures the number of particles the kidney filters.”

PNLE3.rationale: Determining how well the kidneys filter wastes states the purpose of a Creatinine clearance test.

PNLE3.question: The nurse observes the female client in the psychiatric ward that she is having a hard time sleeping at night. The nurse asks the client about it and the client says, “I can’t sleep at night because of fear of dying.” What is the best initial nursing response?

choices.A: “It must be frightening for you to feel that way. Tell me more about it.”
choices.B: “Don’t worry, you won’t die. You are just here for some test.”
choices.D: “Try to sleep. You need the rest before tomorrow’s test.”

PNLE3.rationale: Acknowledging a feeling tone is the most therapeutic response and provides a broad opening for the client to elaborate feelings.

PNLE3.question: In the hospital lobby, the registered nurse overhears a two staff members discussing about the health condition of her client. What would be the appropriate action for the registered nurse to take?

choices.A: Join in the conversation, giving her input about the case.
choices.B: Ignore them, because they have the right to discuss anything they want to.
choices.C: Tell them it is not appropriate to discuss such things.
choices.D: Report this incident to the nursing supervisor.

PNLE3.rationale: The behavior should be stopped. The first is to remind the staff that confidentiality maybe violated.

PNLE3.question: The client has had a right-sided cerebrovascular accident. In transferring the client from the wheelchair to bed, in what position should a client be placed to facilitate safe transfer?

choices.A: Weakened (L) side of the cient next to bed.
choices.B: Weakened (R) side of the client next to bed.
choices.C: Weakened (L) side of the client away from bed.
choices.D: Weakened (R) side of the cient away from bed.

PNLE3.rationale: With a right-sided cerebrovascular accident the client would have left-sided hemiplegia or weakness. The client’s good side should be closest to the bed to facilitate the transfer.

PNLE3.question: The child client has undergone hip surgery and is in a spica cast. Which of the following toy should be avoided to be in the child’s bed?
PNLE3.rationale: Legos are small plastic building blocks that could easily slip under the child’s cast and lead to a break in skin integrity and even infection. Pencils, backscratchers, and marbles are some other narrow or small items that could easily slip under the child’s cast and lead to a break in skin integrity and infection.

PNLE3.question: The LPN/LVN asks the registered nurse why oxytocin (Pitocin), 10 units (IV or IM) must be given to a client after birth fo the fetus. The nurse is correct to explain that oxytocin:
PNLE3.rationale: Oxytocin (Pitocin) is used to maintain uterine tone.

PNLE3.question: The nurse in the nursing care unit is aware that one of the medical staff displays unlikely behaviors like confusion, agitation, lethargy and unkempt appearance. This behavior has been reported to the nurse manager several times, but no changes observed. The nurse should:

choices.A: ontinue to report observations of unusual behavior until the problem is resolved.
choices.B: onsider that the obligation to protect the patient from harm has been met by the prior reports and do nothing further.
choices.C: iscuss the situation with friends who are also nurses to get ideas .
choices.D: pproach the partner of this medical staff member with these concerns.

PNLE3.rationale: The submission of reports about incidents that expose clients to harm does not remove the obligation to report ongoing behavior as long as the risk to the client continues.

PNLE3.question: The physician ordered tetracycline PO qid to a child client who weights 20kg. The recommended PO tetracycline dose is 25-50 mg/kg/day. What is the maximum single dose that can be safely administered to this child?
PNLE3.rationale: The recommended dosage of tetracycline is 25-50mg/kg/day. If the child weighs 20kg and the maximum dose is 50mg/kg, this would indicate a total daily dose of 1000mg of tetracycline. In this case, the child is being given this medication four times a day. Therefore the maximum single dose that can be given is 250mg (1000 mg of tetracycline divided by four doses.)

PNLE3.question: The nurse is completing an obstetric history of a woman in labor. Which event in the obstetric history will help the nurse suspects dysfunctional labor in the current pregnancy?

choices.A: Total time of ruptured membranes was 24 hours with the second birth.
choices.C: Uterine fibroid noted at time of cesarean delivery.
choices.D: Second birth by cesarean for face presentation.

PNLE3.rationale: An abnormality in the uterine muscle could reduce the effectiveness of uterine contractions and lengthen the duration of subsequent labors.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is planning to talk to the client with an antisocial personality disorder. What would be the most therapeutic approach?

choices.C: Give the client opportunities to test reality.

PNLE3.rationale: Personality disorders stem from a weak superego, implying a lack of adequate controls.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is teaching a group of women about fertility awareness, the nurse should emphasize that basal body temperature:

choices.A: an be done with a mercury thermometer but no a digital one.
choices.B: The average temperature taken each morning.
choices.C: Should be recorded each morning before any activity.
choices.D: Has a lower degree of accuracy in predicting ovulation than the cervical mucus test.

PNLE3.rationale: The basal body temperature is the lowest body temperature of a healthy person that is taken immediately after waking and before getting out of bed. The BBT usually varies from 36.2 ºC to 36.3ºC during menses and for about 5-7 days afterward. About the time of ovulation, a slight drop in temperature may be seen, after ovulation in concert with the increasing progesterone levels of the early luteal phase, the BBT rises 0.2-0.4 ºC. This elevation remains until 2-3 days before menstruation, or if pregnancy has occurred.

PNLE3.question: The nursing applicant has given the chance to ask questions during a job interview at a local hospital. What should be the most important question to ask that can increase chances of securing a job offer?

choices.A: egin with questions about client care assignments, advancement opportunities, and continuing education.
choices.B: ecline to ask questions, because that is the responsibility of the interviewer.
choices.C: sk as many questions about the facility as possible.
choices.D: larify information regarding salary, benefits, and working hours first, because this will help in deciding whether or not to take the job.

PNLE3.rationale: This choice implies concern for client care and self-improvement.

PNLE3.question: The nurse advised the pregnant woman that smoking and alcohol should be avoided during pregnancy. The nurse takes into account that the developing fetus is most vulnerable to environment teratogens that cause malformation during:
PNLE3.rationale: The first trimester is the period of organogenesis, that is, cell differentiation into the various organs, tissues, and structures.

PNLE3.question: A male client tells the nurse that there is a big bug in his bed. The most therapeutic nursing response would be:

choices.B: “Where’s the bug? I’ll kill it for you.”
choices.C: “I don’t see a bug in your bed, but you seem afraid.”

PNLE3.rationale: This response does not contradict the client’s perception, is honest, and shows empathy.

PNLE3.question: A pregnant client in late pregnancy is complaining of groin pain that seems worse on the right side. Which of the following is the most likely cause of it?
PNLE3.rationale: Tension on round ligament occurs because of the erect human posture and pressure exerted by the growing fetus.

PNLE3.question: The nurse is conducting a lecture to a group of volunteer nurses. The nurse is correct in imparting the idea that the Good Samaritan law protects the nurse from a suit for malpractice when:

choices.A: The nurse stops to render emergency aid and leaves before the ambulance arrives.
choices.B: The nurse acts in an emergency at his or her place of employment.
choices.C: The nurse refuses to stop for an emergency outside of the scope of employment.
choices.D: The nurse is grossly negligent at the scene of an emergency.

PNLE3.rationale: The Good Samaritan Law does not impose a duty to stop at the scene of an emergency outside of the scope of employment, therefore nurses who do not stop are not liable for suit.

PNLE3.question: A woman is hospitalized with mild preeclampsia. The nurse is formulating a plan of care for this client, which nursing care is least likely to be done?

choices.B: Vital signs and FHR and rhythm q4h while awake.

PNLE3.rationale: Although reducing environment stimuli and activity is necessary for a woman with mild preeclampsia, she will most probably have bathroom privileges.

PNLE3.question: While feeding a newborn with an unrepaired cardiac defect, the nurse keeps on assessing the condition of the client. The nurse notes that the newborn’s respiration is 72 breaths per minute. What would be the initial nursing action?
PNLE3.rationale: A normal respiratory rate for a newborn is 30-40 breaths per minute.

PNLE3.question: A client who undergone appendectomy 3 days ago is scheduled for discharge today. The nurse notes that the client is restless, picking at bedclothes and saying, “I am late on my appointment,” and calling the nurse by the wrong name. The nurse suspects:
PNLE3.rationale: The behavior described is likely to be symptoms of delirium tremens, or alcohol withdrawal (often unsuspected on a surgical unit.)

PNLE5.question: Which of the following is characterized the rate of growth during this period?
PNLE5.rationale: a decline in growth rate.  During the Preschooler stage growth is very minimal. Weight gain is only 4.5lbs (2kgs) per year and Height is 3.5in (6-8cm) per year. Review: Most rapid growth and development- Infancy Slow growth- Toddler hood and Preschooler Slower growth- School age Rapid growth- Adolescence

PNLE5.question: In assessing Raphael’s growth and development, the nurse is guided by principles of growth and development. Which is not included?

choices.A: ll individuals follow cephalo-caudal and proximo-distal
choices.B: ifferent parts of the body grows at different rate
choices.C: ll individual follow standard growth rate
choices.D: Rate and pattern of growth can be modified

PNLE5.rationale: Rate and pattern of growth can be modified. Growth and development occurs in cephalo-caudal meaning development occurs through out the body’s axis. Example: the child must be able to lift the head before he is able to lift his chest. Proximo-distal is development that progresses from center of the body to the extremities. Example: a child first develops arm movement before fine-finger movement. Different parts of the body grows at different range because some body tissue mature faster than the other such as the neurologic tissues peaks its growth during the first years of life while the genital tissue doesn’t till puberty. Also G&D is predictable in the sequence which a child normally precedes such as motor skills and behavior. Lastly G&D can never be modified .

PNLE5.question: What type of play will be ideal for Raphael at this period?
PNLE5.rationale: Make believe. Make believe is most appropriate because it enhances the imitative play and imagination of the preschooler. C and D are for infants while letter A is B is recommended for schoolers because it enhances competitive play.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following information indicate that Raphael is normal for his age?

choices.B: evelop sense of whether he can trust the world
choices.C: Has the ability to try new things
choices.D: Learn basic skills within his culture

PNLE5.rationale: Has the ability to try new things.  Erickson defines the developmental task of a preschool period is learning Initiative vs. Guilt. Children can initiate motor activities of various sorts on their own and no longer responds to or imitate the actions of other children or of their parents.

PNLE5.question: Based on Kohlberg’s theory, what is the stage of moral development of Raphael? Punishment-obedience

choices.D: Situation 2 Baby boy Lacson delivered at 36 weeks gestation weighs 3,400 gm and height of 59 cm (6-10)

PNLE5.rationale: naïve instrumental orientation. According to Kohlber, a preschooler is under Pre-conventional where a child learns about instrumental purpose and exchange, that is they will something do for another if that that person does something with the child in return. Letter A is applicable for Toddlers and letter B is for a School age child.

PNLE5.question: Baby boy Lacson’s height is
PNLE5.rationale: Long. The average length of full-term babies at birth is 20 in. (51 cm), although the normal range is 46 cm (18 in.) to 56 cm (22 in.).

PNLE5.question: Growth and development in a child progresses in the following ways EXCEPT

choices.B: From trunk to the tip of the extremities

PNLE5.rationale: From cognitive to psychosexual. Growth and development occurs in cephalo-caudal (head to toe), proximo-distal (trunk to tips of the extremities and general to specific, but it doesn’t occurs in cognitive to psychosexual because they can develop at the same time.

PNLE5.question: As described by Erikson, the major psychosexual conflict of the above situation is
PNLE5.rationale: Trust vs. mistrust. According to Erikson, children 0-18 months are under the developmental task of Trust vs. Mistrust.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following is true about Mongolian Spots?
PNLE5.rationale: Disappears in about a year. Mongolian spots are stale grey or bluish patches of discoloration commonly seen across the sacrum or buttocks due to accumulation of melanocytes and they disappears in 1 year. They are not linked to steroid use and pathologic conditions.

PNLE5.question: Signs of cold stress that the nurse must be alert when caring for a Newborn is: Hypothermia

choices.D: Situation 3 Nursing care after delivery has an important aspect in every stages of delivery

PNLE5.rationale: Increased RR. Hypothermia is inaccurate cause normally, temperature of a newborn drop, Also a child under cold stress will kick and cry to increase the metabolic rate thereby increasing heat so B isn’t a good choice. A newborn doesn’t have the ability to shiver, so letter B and C is wrong. A newborn will increase its RR because the NB will need more oxygen because of too much activity.

PNLE5.question: After the baby is delivered, the cord was cut between two clamps using a sterile scissors and blade, then the baby is placed at the:
PNLE5.rationale: Mother’s breast. Place it at the mother’s breast for latch-on. (Note: for NSD breast feed ASAP while for CS delivery, breast feed after 4 hours)

PNLE5.question: The baby’s mother is RH(-). Which of the following laboratory tests will probably be ordered for the newborn?
PNLE5.rationale: Direct Coomb’s. Coomb’s test is the test to determine if RH antibodies are present. Indirect Coomb’s is done to the mother and Direct Coomb’s is the one don’t to the baby. Blood culture and Platelet count doesn’t help detect RH antibodies.

PNLE5.question: Hypothermia is common in newborn because of their inability to control heat. The following would be an appropriate nursing intervention to prevent heat loss except:

choices.A: Place the crib beside the wall

PNLE5.rationale: Place the crib beside the wall. Placing the crib beside the wall is inappropriate because it can provide heat loss by radiation. Doing Kangaroo care or hugging the baby, mechanical pressure or incubators and drying and wrapping the baby will help conserve heat.

PNLE5.question: The following conditions are caused by cold stress except
PNLE5.rationale: Increase ICP. Hypoglycemia may occur due to increase metabolic rate, and because of newborns are born slightly acidic, and they catabolize brownfat which will produce ketones which is an acid will cause metabolic acidosis. Also a NB with severe hypothermia is in high risk for kernicterus (too much bilirubin in the brain) can lead to Cerebral palsy. There is no connection in the increase of ICP with hypothermia. (NOTE: pathognomonic sign of Kernicterus in adult- asterexis, or involuntary flapping of the hand.)

PNLE5.question: During the feto-placental circulation, the shunt between two atria is called
PNLE5.rationale: Foramen Ovale. Foramen ovale is opening between two atria, Ductus venosus is the shunt from liver to the inferior vena cava, and your Ductus Arteriosus is the shunt from the pulmonary artery to the aorta.

PNLE5.question: What would cause the closure of the Foramen ovale after the baby had been delivered?

choices.B: Shifting of pressures from right side to the left side of the heart

PNLE5.rationale: Shifting of pressures from right side to the left side of the heart. During feto-placental circulation, the pressure in the heart is much higher in the right side, but once breathing/crying is established, the pressure will shift from the R to the L side, and will facilitate the closure of Foramen Ovale. (Note: that is why you should position the NB in R side lying position to increase pressure in the L side of the heart.) Review: Increase PO2-> closure of ductus arteriosus Decreased bloodflow -> closure of the ductus venosus Circulation in the lungs is initiated by -> lung expansion and pulmonary ventilation What will sustain 1st breath-> decreased artery pressure What will complete circulation-> cutting of the cord

PNLE5.question: Failure of the Foramen Ovale to close will cause what Congenital Heart Disease? Total anomalous Pulmunary Artery

choices.D: Situation 4 Children are vulnerable to some minor health problems or injuries hence the nurse should be able to teach mothers to give appropriate home care.

PNLE5.rationale: Atrial Septal defect. Foramen ovale is the opening between two Atria so, if its will not close Atrial Septal defect can occur.

PNLE5.question: A mother brought her child to the clinic with nose bleeding. The nurse showed the mother the most appropriate position for the child which is:
PNLE5.rationale: Sitting up. The correct position is making the child having an upright sitting position with the head slightly tilted forward. This position will minimize the amount of blood pressure in nasal vessels and keep blood moving forward not back into the nasopharynx, which will have the choking sensation and increase risk of aspiration. Choices b, c, d, are inappropriate cause they can cause blood to enter the nasopharynx.

PNLE5.question: A common problem in children is the inflammation of the middle ear. This is related to the malfunctioning of the:
PNLE5.rationale: Eustachian tube. This is because children has short, horizontal Eustachian tubes. The dysfunction in the Eustachian tube enables bacterial invasion of the middle ear and obstructs drainage of secretions.

PNLE5.question: For acute otitis media, the treatment is prompt antibiotic therapy. Delayed treatment may result in complications of:
PNLE5.rationale: Brain damage. One of the complication of recurring acute otitis media is risk for having Meningitis, thereby causing possible brain damage. That is why patient must follow a complete treatment regimen and follow up care. A,B and D are not complications of AOM.

PNLE5.question: When assessing gross motor development in a 3 year old, which of the following activities would the nurse expect to finds?
PNLE5.rationale: Riding a tricycle. Answer is A, riding a tricycle is appropriate for a 3 y/o child. Hopping on one foot can be done by a 4 y/o child, as well as catching and throwing a ball over hand. Skipping can be done by a 5 y/o.

PNLE5.question: When assessing the weight of a 5-month old, which of the following indicates healthy growth?
PNLE5.rationale: Doubling of birth weight. During the first 6 months of life the weight from birth will be doubled and as soon as the baby reaches 1 year, its birth weight is tripled.

PNLE5.question: An appropriate toy for a 4 year old child is:
PNLE5.rationale: Doctor and nurse kits. Letter C is appropriate because it will enhance the creativity and imagination of a pre-school child. Letter B and D are inappropriate because they are too complex for a 4 y/o. Push-pull toys are recommended for infants.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following statements would the nurse expects a 5-year old boy to say whose pet gerbil just died

choices.C: “Ill be good from now own so I wont die like my gerbil”

PNLE5.rationale: “He’s just a bit dead”. A 5 y/o views death in “degrees”, so the child most likely will say that “he is just a bit dead”. Personification of death like boogeyman occurs in ages 7 to 9 as well as denying death can if they will be good. Denying death using jokes and attributing life qualities to death occurs during age 3-5.

PNLE5.question: When assessing the fluid and electrolyte balance in an infant, which of the following would be important to remember?

choices.A: Infant can concentrate urine at an adult level
choices.B: The metabolic rate of an infant is slower than in adults
choices.C: Infants have more intracellular water that adult do
choices.D: Infant have greater body surface area than adults

PNLE5.rationale: Infant have greater body surface area than adults. Infants have greater body surface area than adult, increasing their risk to F&E imbalances. Also infants cant concentrate a urine at an adult level and their metabolic rate, also called water turnover, is 2 to 3 times higher than adult. Plus more fluids of the infants are at the ECF spaces not in the ICF spaces.

PNLE5.question: When assessing a child with aspirin overdose, which of the following will be expected?
PNLE5.rationale: Metabolic acidosis. Remember that Aspirin is acid (Acetylsalicylic ACID).

PNLE5.question: Which of the following is not a possible systemic clinical manifestation of severe burns?
PNLE5.rationale: Blisters and edema. The question was asking for a SYSTEMIC clinical manifestation, Letters A,B and C are systemic manifestations while Blisters and Edema weren’t.

PNLE5.question: When assessing a family for potential child abuse risks, the nurse would observe for which of the following?
PNLE5.rationale: Problematic pregnancies. Typical factors that may be risk for Child abuse are problematic pregnancies, chronic exposure to stress not periodic, low level of self esteem not high level. Also child abuse can happen in all socio-economic status not just on low socio-economic status.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following is a possible indicator of Munchausen syndrome by proxy type of child abuse?

choices.A: ruises found at odd locations, with different stages of healing
choices.C: Unexplained symptoms of diarrhea, vomiting and apnea with no organic basis

PNLE5.rationale: Unexplained symptoms of diarrhea, vomiting and apnea with no organic basis. Munchausen syndrome by Proxy is the fabrication or inducement of an illness by one person to another person, usually mother to child. It is characterized by symptoms such as apnea and siezures, which may be due to suffocation, drugs or poisoning, vomiting which can be induced with poisons and diarrhea with the use of laxatives. Letter A can be seen in a Physical abuse, Letter B for sexual abuse and Letter C is for Physical Neglect.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following is an inappropriate interventions when caring for a child with HIV? Teaching family about disease transmission

choices.A: Offering large amount of fresh fruits and vegetables
choices.B: Encouraging child to perform at optimal level
choices.D: Situation 5 Agata, 2 years old is rushed to the ER due to cyanosis precipitated by crying. Her mother observed that after playing she gets tired. She was diagnosed with Tetralogy of Fallot.

PNLE5.rationale: Offering large amount of fresh fruits and vegetables. A child with HIV is immunocompromised. Fresh fruits and vegetables, which may be contaminated with organisms and pesticides can be harmful, if not fatal to the child, therefore these items should be avoided.

PNLE5.question: The goal of nursing care fro Agata is to:
PNLE5.rationale: Decrease hypoxic spells. The correct answer is letter C. Though letter B would be a good answer too, this goal is too vague and not specific. Nursing interventions will not solely promote normal G&D unless he will undergo surgical repair. So decreasing Hypoxic Spells is more SMART. Letter A and D are inappropriate.

PNLE5.question: The immediate nursing intervention for cyanosis of Agata is:

choices.B: Place her in knee chest position

PNLE5.rationale: Place her in knee chest position. The immediate intervention would be to place her on knee-chest or “squatting” position because it traps blood into the lower extremities. Though also letter C would be a good choice but the question is asking for “Immediate” so letter B is more appropriate. Letter A and D are incorrect because its normal for a child who have ToF to have hypoxic or “tets” spells so there is no need to transfer her to the NICU or to alert the Pediatrician.

PNLE5.question: Agata was scheduled for a palliative surgery, which creates anastomosis of the subclavian artery to the pulmonary artery. This procedure is:
PNLE5.rationale: Blalock-Taussig. Blalock-Taussig procedure its just a temporary or palliative surgery which creates a shunt between the aorta and pulmonary artery so that the blood can leave the aorta and enter the pulmonary artery and thus oxygenating the lungs and return to the left side of the heart, then to the aorta then to the body. This procedure also makes use of the subclavian vein so pulse is not palpable at the right arm. The full repair for ToF is called the Brock procedure. Raskkind is a palliative surgery for TOGA.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following is not an indicator that Agata experiences separation anxiety brought about her hospitalization?

choices.B: Prolonged loud crying, consoled only by mother
choices.C: Occasional temper tantrums and always says NO
choices.D: Repeatedly verbalizes desire to go home

PNLE5.rationale: Friendly with the nurse. Because toddlers views hospitalization is abandonment, separation anxiety is common. Its has 3 phases: PDD (parang c puff daddy LOL) 1. Protest 2. despair 3. detachment (or denial). Choices B, C, D are usually seen in a child with separation anxiety (usually in the protest stage). REVIEW: Separation anxiety begin at: 9 months Peaks: 18 months

PNLE5.question: When Agata was brought to the OR, her parents where crying. What would be the most appropriate nursing diagnosis?

choices.A: Infective family coping r/t situational crisis
choices.D: nticipatory grieving r/t gravity of child’s physical status

PNLE5.rationale: Anticipatory grieving r/t gravity of child’s physical status. In this item letter A and be are inappropriate response so remove them. The possible answers are C and D. Fear defined as the perceived threat (real or imagined) that is consciously recognized as danger (NANDA) is applicable in the situation but its defining characteristics are not applicable. Crying per se can not be a subjective cue to signify fear, and most of the symptoms of fear in NANDA are physiological. Anticipatory grieving on the other hand are intellectual and EMOTIONAL responses based on a potential loss. And remember that procedures like this cannot assure total recovery. So letter D is a more appropriate Nursing diagnosis.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following respiratory condition is always considered a medical emergency?
PNLE5.rationale: Epiglottitis. Acute and sever inflammation of the epiglottis can cause life threatening airway obstruction, that is why its always treated as a medical emergency. NSG intervention : Prepare tracheostomy set at bed side. LTB, can also cause airway obstruction but its not an emergency. Asthma is also not an emergency. CF is a chronic disease, so its not a medical emergency.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following statements by the family of a child with asthma indicates a need for additional teaching?

choices.A: “We need to identify what things triggers his attacks”
choices.B: “He is to use bronchodilator inhaler before steroid inhaler”
choices.C: “We’ll make sure he avoids exercise to prevent asthma attacks”
choices.D: “he should increase his fluid intake regularly to thin secretions”

PNLE5.rationale: “We’ll make sure he avoids exercise to prevent asthma attacks”. Asthmatic children don’t have to avoid exercise. They can participate on physical activities as tolerated. Using a bronchodilator before administering steroids is correct because steroids are just anti-inflammatory and they don’t have effects on the dilation of the bronchioles. OF course letters A and B are obviously correct.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following would require careful monitoring in the child with ADHD who is receiving Methylphenidate (Ritalin)? Dental health

choices.D: Situation 6 Laura is assigned as the Team Leader during the immunization day at the RHU

PNLE5.rationale: Height and weight. Dental problems are more likely to occur in children under going TCA therapy. Mouth dryness is a expected side effects of Ritalin since it activates the SNS. Also loss of appetite is more likely to happen, not increase in appetite. The correct answer is letter C, because Ritalin can affect the child’s G&D. Intervention: medication “holidays or vacation”. (This means during weekends or holidays or school vacations, where the child wont be in school, the drug can be withheld.)

PNLE5.question: What program for the DOH is launched at 1976 in cooperation with WHO and UNICEF to reduce morbidity and mortality among infants caused by immunizable disease?
PNLE5.rationale: Expanded program on immunization

PNLE5.question: One important principle of the immunization program is based on?

PNLE5.question: The main element of immunization program is one of the following?

choices.B: ssessment and evaluation of the program

PNLE5.rationale: Target setting

PNLE5.question: What does herd immunity means?
