PNLE4.question: The client is transferred from the operating room to recovery room after an open-heart surgery. The nurse assigned is taking the vital signs of the client. The nurse notified the physician when the temperature of the client rises to 38.8 ºC or 102 ºF because elevated temperatures:

choices.A: May be a forerunner of hemorrhage.
choices.B: re related to diaphoresis and possible chilling.

PNLE4.rationale: The temperature of 102 ºF (38.8ºC) or greater lead to an increased metabolism and cardiac workload.

PNLE4.question: After radiation therapy for cancer of the prostate, the client experienced irritation in the bladder. Which of the following sign of bladder irritability is correct?
PNLE4.rationale: Dysuria, nocturia, and urgency are all signs an irritable bladder after radiation therapy.

PNLE4.question: A client is diagnosed with a brain tumor in the occipital lobe. Which of the following will the client most likely experience?
PNLE4.rationale: The occipital lobe is involve with visual interpretation.

PNLE4.question: A client with Addison’s disease has a blood pressure of 65/60. The nurse understands that decreased blood pressure of the client with Addison’s disease involves a disturbance in the production of:
PNLE4.rationale: Mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone cause the kidneys to retain sodium ions. With sodium, water is also retained, elevating blood pressure. Absence of this hormone thus causes hypotension.

PNLE4.question: The nurse is planning to teach the client about a spontaneous pneumothorax. The nurse would base the teaching on the understanding that:

choices.A: Inspired air will move from the lung into the pleural space.
choices.B: There is greater negative pressure within the chest cavity.
choices.C: The heart and great vessels shift to the affected side.
choices.D: The other lung will collapse if not treated immediately.

PNLE4.rationale: As a person with a tear in the lung inhales, air moves through that opening into the intrapleural and causes partial or complete collapse of the lungs.

PNLE4.question: During an assessment, the nurse recognizes that the client has an increased risk for developing cancer of the tongue. Which of the following health history will be a concern?
PNLE4.rationale: Heavy alcohol ingestion predisposes an individual to the development of oral cancer.

PNLE4.question: The client in the orthopedic unit asks the nurse the reason behind why compact bone is stronger than cancellous bone. Which of the following is the correct response of the nurse?

choices.A: ompact bone is stronger than cancellous bone because of its greater size.
choices.B: ompact bone is stronger than cancellous bone because of its greater weight.
choices.C: ompact bone is stronger than cancellous bone because of its greater volume.
choices.D: ompact bone is stronger than cancellous bone because of its greater density.

PNLE4.rationale: The greater the density of compact bone makes it stronger than the cancellous bone. Compact bone forms from cancellous bone by the addition of concentric rings of bones substances to the marrow spaces of cancellous bone. The large marrow spaces are reduced to haversian canals.

PNLE4.question: The nurse is reviewing the laboratory results of the client. In reviewing the results of the RBC count, the nurse understands that the higher the red blood cell count, the :
PNLE4.rationale: Viscosity, a measure of a fluid’s internal resistance to flow, is increased as the number of red cells suspended in plasma.

PNLE4.question: The physician advised the client with Hemiparesis to use a cane. The client asks the nurse why cane will be needed. The nurse explains to the client that cane is advised specifically to:

choices.A: id in controlling involuntary muscle movements.
choices.D: Prevent further injury to weakened muscles.

PNLE4.rationale: Hemiparesis creates instability. Using a cane provides a wider base of support and, therefore greater stability.

PNLE4.question: The nurse is conducting a discharge teaching regarding the prevention of further problems to a client who undergone surgery for carpal tunnel syndrome of the right hand. Which of the following instruction will the nurse includes?

choices.A: Learn to type using your left hand only.
choices.B: void typing in a long period of time.
choices.C: void carrying heavy things using the right hand.
choices.D: o manual stretching exercise during breaks.

PNLE4.rationale: Manual stretching exercises will assist in keeping the muscles and tendons supple and pliable, reducing the traumatic consequences of repetitive activity.

PNLE4.question: A female client is admitted because of recurrent urinary tract infections. The client asks the nurse why she is prone to this disease. The nurse states that the client is most susceptible because of:
PNLE4.rationale: The length of the urethra is shorter in females than in males; therefore microorganisms have a shorter distance to travel to reach the bladder. The proximity of the meatus to the anus in females also increases this incidence.

PNLE4.question: A 55-year-old client is admitted with chest pain that radiates to the neck, jaw and shoulders that occurs at rest, with high body temperature, weak with generalized sweating and with decreased blood pressure. A myocardial infarction is diagnosed. The nurse knows that the most accurate explanation for one of these presenting adaptations is:

choices.A: atecholamines released at the site of the infarction causes intermittent localized pain.
choices.B: Parasympathetic reflexes from the infarcted myocardium causes diaphoresis.
choices.C: onstriction of central and peripheral blood vessels causes a decrease in blood pressure.
choices.D: Inflammation in the myocardium causes a rise in the systemic body temperature.

PNLE4.rationale: Temperature may increase within the first 24 hours and persist as long as a week.

PNLE4.question: Following an amputation of a lower limb to a male client, the nurse provides an instruction on how to prevent a hip flexion contracture. The nurse should instruct the client to:.

choices.A: Perform quadriceps muscle setting exercises twice a day.
choices.B: Sit in a chair for 30 minutes three times a day.
choices.C: Lie on the abdomen 30 minutes every four hours.
choices.D: Turn from side to side every 2 hours.

PNLE4.rationale: The hips are in extension when the client is prone; this keeps the hips from flexing.

PNLE4.question: The physician scheduled the client with rheumatoid arthritis for the injection of hydrocortisone into the knee joint. The client asks the nurse why there is a need for this injection. The nurse explains that the most important reason for doing this is to:
PNLE4.rationale: Steroids have an anti-inflammatory effect that can reduce arthritic pannus formation.

PNLE4.question: The nurse is assigned to care for a 57-year-old female client who had a cataract surgery an hour ago. The nurse should:

choices.A: dvise the client to refrain from vigorous brushing of teeth and hair.
choices.B: Instruct the client to avoid driving for 2 weeks.
choices.C: Encourage eye exercises to strengthen the ocular musculature.
choices.D: Teach the client coughing and deep-breathing techniques.

PNLE4.rationale: Activities such as rigorous brushing of hair and teeth cause increased intraocular pressure and may lead to hemorrhage in the anterior chamber.

PNLE4.question: A client with AIDS develops bacterial pneumonia is admitted in the emergency department. The client’s arterial blood gases is drawn and the result is PaO2 80mmHg. then arterial blood gases are drawn again and the level is reduced from 80 mmHg to 65 mmHg. The nurse should;

choices.A: Have arterial blood gases performed again to check for accuracy.
choices.D: ecrease the tension of oxygen in the plasma.

PNLE4.rationale: This decrease in PaO2 indicates respiratory failure; it warrants immediate medical evaluation.

PNLE4.question: An 18-year-old college student is brought to the emergency department due to serious motor vehicle accident. Right above-knee-amputation is done. Upon awakening from surgery the client tells the nurse, “What happened to me? I cannot remember anything?” Which of the following would be the appropriate initial nursing response?

choices.A: “You sound concerned; You’ll probably remember more as you wake up.”
choices.C: “You were in a car accident this morning.”
choices.D: “An amputation of your right leg was necessary because of an accident.”

PNLE4.rationale: This is truthful and provides basic information that may prompt recollection of what happened; it is a starting point.

PNLE4.question: A 38-year-old client with severe hypertension is hospitalized. The physician prescribed a Captopril (Capoten) and Alprazolam (Xanax) for treatment. The client tells the nurse that there is something wrong with the medication and nursing care. The nurse recognizes this behavior is probably a manifestation of the client’s:
PNLE4.rationale: Clients adapting to illness frequently feel afraid and helpless and strike out at health team members as a way of maintaining control or denying their fear.

PNLE4.question: Before discharge, the nurse scheduled the client who had a colostomy for colorectal cancer for discharge instruction about resuming activities. The nurse should plan to help the client understands that:

choices.A: fter surgery, changes in activities must be made to accommodate for the physiologic changes caused by the operation.
choices.B: Most sports activities, except for swimming, can be resumed based on the client’s overall physical condition.
choices.C: With counseling and medical guidance, a near normal lifestyle, including complete sexual function is possible.
choices.D: ctivities of daily living should be resumed as quickly as possible to avoid depression and further dependency.

PNLE4.rationale: There are few physical restraints on activity postoperatively, but the client may have emotional problems resulting from the body image changes.

PNLE4.question: A client is scheduled for bariatric surgery. Preoperative teaching is done. Which of the following statement would alert the nurse that further teaching to the client is necessary?

choices.A: “I will be limiting my intake to 600 to 800 calories a day once I start eating again.”
choices.B: “I’m going to have a figure like a model in about a year.”
choices.C: “I need to eat more high-protein foods.”
choices.D: “I will be going to be out of bed and sitting in a chair the first day after surgery.”.

PNLE4.rationale: Clients need to be prepared emotionally for the body image changes that occur after bariatric surgery. Clients generally experience excessive abdominal skin folds after weight stabilizes, which may require a panniculectomy. Body image disturbance often occurs in response to incorrectly estimating one’s size; it is not uncommon for the client to still feel fat no matter how much weight is lost.

PNLE4.question: The client who had transverse colostomy asks the nurse about the possible effect of the surgery on future sexual relationship. What would be the best nursing response?

choices.A: The surgery will temporarily decrease the client’s sexual impulses.
choices.B: Sexual relationships must be curtailed for several weeks.
choices.C: The partner should be told about the surgery before any sexual activity.
choices.D: The client will be able to resume normal sexual relationships.

PNLE4.rationale: Surgery on the bowel has no direct anatomic or physiologic effect on sexual performance. However, the nurse should encourage verbalization.

PNLE4.question: A 75-year-old male client tells the nurse that his wife has osteoporosis and asks what chances he had of getting also osteoporosis like his wife. Which of the following is the correct response of the nurse?

choices.A: “This is only a problem for women.”
choices.B: “You are not at risk because of your small frame.”
choices.C: “You might think about having a bone density test,”
choices.D: “Exercise is a good way to prevent this problem.”

PNLE4.rationale: Osteoporosis is not restricted to women; it is a potential major health problem of all older adults; estimates indicate that half of all women have at least one osteoporitic fracture and the risk in men is estimated between 13% and 25%; a bone mineral density measurement assesses the mass of bone per unit volume or how tightly the bone is packed.

PNLE4.question: An older adult client with acute pain is admitted in the hospital. The nurse understands that in managing acute pain of the client during the first 24 hours, the nurse should ensure that:

choices.A: Ordered PRN analgesics are administered on a scheduled basis.
choices.B: Patient controlled analgesia is avoided in this population.
choices.C: Pain medication is ordered via the intramuscular route.
choices.D: n order for meperidine (Demerol) is secured for pain relief.

PNLE4.rationale: Around-the-clock administration of analgesics is recommended for acute pain in the older adult population; this help to maintain a therapeutic blood level of pain medication.

PNLE4.question: A nurse is caring to an older adult with presbycusis. In formulating nursing care plan for this client, the nurse should expect that hearing loss of the client that is caused by aging to have:

choices.A: Overgrowth of the epithelial auditory lining.

PNLE4.rationale: Generally, female voices have a higher pitch than male voices; older adults with presbycusis (hearing loss caused by the aging process) have more difficulty hearing higher-pitched sounds.

PNLE4.question: The nurse is reviewing the client’s chart about the ordered medication. The nurse must observe for signs of hyperkalemia when administering:
PNLE4.rationale: Aldactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic; hyperkalemia is an adverse effect.

PNLE4.question: The physician prescribed Albuterol (Proventil) to the client with severe asthma. After the administration of the medication the nurse should monitor the client for:
PNLE4.rationale: Albuterol’s sympathomimetic effect causes cardiac stimulation that may cause tachycardia and palpitation.

PNLE4.question: A client is receiving diltiazem (Cardizem). What should the nurse include in a teaching plan aimed at reducing the side effects of this medication?

choices.A: Take the drug with an antacid.

PNLE4.rationale: Changing positions slowly will help prevent the side effect of orthostatic hypotension.

PNLE4.question: A client is receiving simvastatin (Zocor). The nurse is aware that this medication is effective when there is decrease in:
PNLE4.rationale: Therapeutic effects of simvastatin include decreased serum triglyceries, LDL and cholesterol.

PNLE4.question: A client is taking nitroglycerine tablets, the nurse should teach the client the importance of:

choices.A: Increasing the number of tablets if dizziness or hypertension occurs.
choices.B: Limiting the number of tablets to 4 per day.
choices.C: Making certain the medication is stored in a dark container.
choices.D: iscontinuing the medication if a headache develops.

PNLE4.rationale: Nitroglycerine is sensitive to light and moisture ad must be stored in a dark, airtight container.

PNLE4.question: The physician prescribes Ibuprofen (Motrin) and hydroxychloroquine sulfate (Plaquenil) for a 58-year-old male client with arthritis. The nurse provides information about toxicity of the hydroxychloroquine. The nurse can determine if the information is clearly understood if the client states:

choices.A: “I will contact the physician immediately if I develop blurred vision.”
choices.B: “I will contact the physician immediately if I develop urinary retention.”
choices.C: “I will contact the physician immediately if I develop swallowing difficulty.”
choices.D: “I will contact the physician immediately if I develop feelings of irritability.”

PNLE4.rationale: Visual disturbance are a sign of toxicity because retinopathy can occur with this drug.

PNLE4.question: The client with an acute myocardial infarction is hospitalized for almost one week. The client experiences nausea and loss of appetite. The nurse caring for the client recognizes that these symptoms may indicate the:
PNLE4.rationale: Toxic levels of Lanoxin stimulate the medullary chemoreceptor trigger zone, resulting in nausea and subsequent anorexia.

PNLE4.question: A client with a partial occlusion of the left common carotid artery is scheduled for discharge. The client is still receiving Coumadin. The nurse provided a discharge instruction to the client regarding adverse effects of Coumadin. The nurse should tell the client to consult with the physician if:
PNLE4.rationale: Warfarin derivatives cause an increase in the prothrombin time and INR, leading to an increased risk for bleeding. Any abnormal or excessive bleeding must be reported, because it may indicate toxic levels of the drug.

PNLE4.question: Levodopa is ordered for a client with Parkinson’s disease. Before starting the medication, the nurse should know that:

choices.A: Levodopa is inadequately absorbed if given with meals.
choices.B: Levodopa may cause the side effects of orthostatic hypotension.
choices.C: Levodopa must be monitored by weekly laboratory tests.
choices.D: Levodopa causes an initial euphoria followed by depression.

PNLE4.rationale: Levodopa is the metabolic precursor of dopamine. It reduces sympathetic outflow by limiting vasoconstriction, which may result in orthostatic hypotension.

PNLE4.question: In making a diagnosis of myasthenia gravis Edrophonium HCI (Tensilon) is used. The nurse knows that this drug will cause a temporary increase in:
PNLE4.rationale: Tensilon, an anticholinesterase drug, causes temporary relief of symptoms of myasthenia gravis in client who have the disease and is therefore an effective diagnostic aid.

PNLE4.question: The nurse can determine the effectiveness of carbamazepine (Tegretol) in the management of trigeminal neuralgia by monitoring the client’s:
PNLE4.rationale: Carbamazepine ( Tegretol) is administered to control pain by reducing the transmission of nerve impulses in clients with trigeminal neuralgia.

PNLE4.question: Administration of potassium iodide solution is ordered to the client who will undergo a subtotal thyroidectomy. The nurse understands that this medication is given to:

choices.A: blate the cells of the thyroid gland that produce T4.
choices.B: ecrease the total basal metabolic rate.
choices.C: ecrease the size and vascularity of the thyroid.
choices.D: Maintain function of the parathyroid gland.

PNLE4.rationale: Potassium iodide, which aids in decreasing the vascularity of the thyroid gland, decreases the risk for hemorrhage.

PNLE4.question: A client with Addison’s disease is scheduled for discharge. Before the discharge, the physician prescribes hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. The nurse expects the hydrocortisone to:

choices.A: Increase amounts of angiotensin II to raise the client’s blood pressure.
choices.B: ontrol excessive loss of potassium salts.
choices.C: Prevent hypoglycemia and permit the client to respond to stress.

PNLE4.rationale: Hydrocortisone is a glucocorticoid that has anti-inflammatory action and aids in metabolism of carbohydrate, fat, and protein, causing elevation of blood glucose. Thus it enables the body to adapt to stress.

PNLE4.question: A client with diabetes insipidus is taking Desmopressin acetate (DDAVP). To determine if the drug is effective, the nurse should monitor the client’s:
PNLE4.rationale: DDAVP replaces the ADH, facilitating reabsorption of water and consequent return of normal urine output and thirst.

PNLE4.question: A client with recurrent urinary tract infections is to be discharged. The client will be taking nitrofurantoin (Macrobid) 50 mg po every evening at home. The nurse provides discharge instructions to the client. Which of the following instructions will be correct?

choices.A: Strain urine for crystals and stones
choices.C: Stop the drug if the urinary output increases
choices.D: Maintain the exact time schedule for drug taking.

PNLE4.rationale: To prevent crystal formation, the client should have sufficient intake to produce 1000 to 1500 mL of urine daily while taking this drug.

PNLE4.question: A client with cancer of the lung is receiving chemotherapy. The physician orders antibiotic therapy for the client. The nurse understands that chemotherapy destroys rapidly growing leukocytes in the:
PNLE4.rationale: Prolonged chemotherapy may slow the production of leukocytes in bone marrow, thus suppressing the activity of the immune system. Antibiotics may be required to help counter infections that the body can no longer handle easily.

PNLE4.question: The physician reduced the client’s Dexamethasone (Decadron) dosage gradually and to continue a lower maintenance dosage. The client asks the nurse about the change of dosage. The nurse explains to the client that the purpose of gradual dosage reduction is to allow:

choices.A: Return of cortisone production by the adrenal glands.
choices.B: Production of antibodies by the immune system
choices.C: uilding of glycogen and protein stores in liver and muscle
choices.D: Time to observe for return of increases intracranial pressure

PNLE4.rationale: Any hormone normally produced by the body must be withdrawn slowly to allow the appropriate organ to adjust and resume production.

PNLE4.question: The nurse is assigned to care for a client with diarrhea. Excessive fluid loss is expected. The nurse is aware that fluid deficit can most accurately be assessed by:
PNLE4.rationale: Dehydration is most readily and accurately measured by serial assessment of body weight; 1 L of fluid weighs 2.2 pounds.

PNLE4.question: Which of the following is the most important electrolyte of intracellular fluid?
PNLE4.rationale: The concentration of potassium is greater inside the cell and is important in establishing a membrane potential, a critical factor in the cell’s ability to function.

PNLE4.question: Which of the following client has a high risk for developing hyperkalemia?
PNLE4.rationale: The kidneys normally eliminate potassium from the body; hyperkalemia may necessitate dialysis.

PNLE4.question: The nurse is reviewing the laboratory result of the client. The client’s serum potassium level is 5.8 mEq/L. Which of the following is the initial nursing action?

choices.A: all the cardiac arrest team to alert them
choices.B: all the laboratory and repeat the test
choices.C: Take the client’s vital signs and notify the physician
choices.D: Obtain an ECG strip and have lidocaine available

PNLE4.rationale: Vital signs monitor cardiorespiratory status; hyperkalemia causes serious cardiac dysrhythmias.

PNLE4.question: Potassium chloride, 20 mEq, is ordered and to be added in the IV solution of a client in a diabetic ketoacidosis. The primary reason for administering this drug is:
PNLE4.rationale: Once treatment with insulin for diabetic ketoacidosis is begun, potassium ions reenter the cell, causing hypokalemia; therefore potassium, along with the replacement fluid, is generally supplied.

PNLE4.question: A female client is brought to the emergency unit. The client is complaining of abdominal cramps. On assessment, client is experiencing anorexia and weight is reduced. The physician’s diagnosis is colitis. Which of the following symptoms of fluid and electrolyte imbalance should the nurse report immediately?

choices.B: evelopment of tetaniy with muscles spasms
choices.D: Nausea, vomiting, and leg and stomach cramps.

PNLE4.rationale: Potassium, the major intracellular cation, functions with sodium and calcium to regulate neuromuscular activity and contraction of muscle fibers, particularly the heart muscle. In hypokalemia these symptoms develop.

PNLE4.question: The client is to receive an IV piggyback medication. When preparing the medication the nurse should be aware that it is very important to:

choices.B: Use exactly 100mL of fluid to mix the medication
choices.C: hange the needle just before adding the medication
choices.D: Rotate the bag after adding the medication

PNLE4.rationale: Because IV solutions enter the body’s internal environment, all solutions and medications utilizing this route must be sterile to prevent the introduction of microbes.

PNLE4.question: The nurse is reviewing the laboratory result of the client. An arterial blood gas report indicates the client’s pH is 7.20, PCO2 35 mmHg and HCO3 is 19 mEq/L. The results are consistent with:
PNLE4.rationale: A low pH and bicarbonate level are consistent with metabolic acidosis.

PNLE5.question: Following spinal injury, the nurse should encourage the client to drink fluids to avoid:
PNLE5.rationale: Clients in the early stage of spinal cord damage experience an atonic bladder, which is characterized by the absence of muscle tone, an enlarged capacity, no feeling of discomfort with distention, and overflow with a large residual. This leads to urinary stasis and infection. High fluid intake limits urinary stasis and infection by diluting the urine and increasing urinary output.

PNLE5.question: The client is transferred from the operating room to recovery room after an open-heart surgery. The nurse assigned is taking the vital signs of the client. The nurse notified the physician when the temperature of the client rises to 38.8 ºC or 102 ºF because elevated temperatures:

choices.A: May be a forerunner of hemorrhage.
choices.B: re related to diaphoresis and possible chilling.

PNLE5.rationale: The temperature of 102 ºF (38.8ºC) or greater lead to an increased metabolism and cardiac workload.

PNLE5.question: After radiation therapy for cancer of the prostate, the client experienced irritation in the bladder. Which of the following sign of bladder irritability is correct?
PNLE5.rationale: Dysuria, nocturia, and urgency are all signs an irritable bladder after radiation therapy.

PNLE5.question: A client is diagnosed with a brain tumor in the occipital lobe. Which of the following will the client most likely experience?
PNLE5.rationale: The occipital lobe is involve with visual interpretation.

PNLE5.question: A client with Addison’s disease has a blood pressure of 65/60. The nurse understands that decreased blood pressure of the client with Addison’s disease involves a disturbance in the production of:
PNLE5.rationale: Mineralocorticoids such as aldosterone cause the kidneys to retain sodium ions. With sodium, water is also retained, elevating blood pressure. Absence of this hormone thus causes hypotension.

PNLE5.question: The nurse is planning to teach the client about a spontaneous pneumothorax. The nurse would base the teaching on the understanding that:

choices.A: Inspired air will move from the lung into the pleural space.
choices.B: There is greater negative pressure within the chest cavity.
choices.C: The heart and great vessels shift to the affected side.
choices.D: The other lung will collapse if not treated immediately.

PNLE5.rationale: As a person with a tear in the lung inhales, air moves through that opening into the intrapleural and causes partial or complete collapse of the lungs.

PNLE5.question: During an assessment, the nurse recognizes that the client has an increased risk for developing cancer of the tongue. Which of the following health history will be a concern?
PNLE5.rationale: Heavy alcohol ingestion predisposes an individual to the development of oral cancer.

PNLE5.question: The client in the orthopedic unit asks the nurse the reason behind why compact bone is stronger than cancellous bone. Which of the following is the correct response of the nurse?

choices.A: ompact bone is stronger than cancellous bone because of its greater size.
choices.B: ompact bone is stronger than cancellous bone because of its greater weight.
choices.C: ompact bone is stronger than cancellous bone because of its greater volume.
choices.D: ompact bone is stronger than cancellous bone because of its greater density.

PNLE5.rationale: The greater the density of compact bone makes it stronger than the cancellous bone. Compact bone forms from cancellous bone by the addition of concentric rings of bones substances to the marrow spaces of cancellous bone. The large marrow spaces are reduced to haversian canals.

choices.A: Ordered PRN analgesics are administered on a scheduled basis.
choices.B: Patient controlled analgesia is avoided in this population.
choices.C: Pain medication is ordered via the intramuscular route.
choices.D: n order for meperidine (Demerol) is secured for pain relief.

PNLE5.rationale: Around-the-clock administration of analgesics is recommended for acute pain in the older adult population; this help to maintain a therapeutic blood level of pain medication.

PNLE5.question: A nurse is caring to an older adult with presbycusis. In formulating nursing care plan for this client, the nurse should expect that hearing loss of the client that is caused by aging to have:

choices.A: Overgrowth of the epithelial auditory lining.

PNLE5.rationale: Generally, female voices have a higher pitch than male voices; older adults with presbycusis (hearing loss caused by the aging process) have more difficulty hearing higher-pitched sounds.

PNLE5.question: The nurse is reviewing the client’s chart about the ordered medication. The nurse must observe for signs of hyperkalemia when administering:
PNLE5.rationale: Aldactone is a potassium-sparing diuretic; hyperkalemia is an adverse effect.

PNLE5.question: The physician prescribed Albuterol (Proventil) to the client with severe asthma. After the administration of the medication the nurse should monitor the client for:
PNLE5.rationale: Albuterol’s sympathomimetic effect causes cardiac stimulation that may cause tachycardia and palpitation.

PNLE5.question: A client is receiving diltiazem (Cardizem). What should the nurse include in a teaching plan aimed at reducing the side effects of this medication?

choices.A: Take the drug with an antacid.

PNLE5.rationale: Changing positions slowly will help prevent the side effect of orthostatic hypotension.

PNLE5.question: A client is receiving simvastatin (Zocor). The nurse is aware that this medication is effective when there is decrease in:
PNLE5.rationale: Therapeutic effects of simvastatin include decreased serum triglyceries, LDL and cholesterol.

PNLE5.question: A client is taking nitroglycerine tablets, the nurse should teach the client the importance of:

choices.A: Increasing the number of tablets if dizziness or hypertension occurs.
choices.B: Limiting the number of tablets to 4 per day.
choices.C: Making certain the medication is stored in a dark container.
choices.D: iscontinuing the medication if a headache develops.

PNLE5.rationale: Nitroglycerine is sensitive to light and moisture ad must be stored in a dark, airtight container.

PNLE5.question: The physician prescribes Ibuprofen (Motrin) and hydroxychloroquine sulfate (Plaquenil) for a 58-year-old male client with arthritis. The nurse provides information about toxicity of the hydroxychloroquine. The nurse can determine if the information is clearly understood if the client states:

choices.A: “I will contact the physician immediately if I develop blurred vision.”
choices.B: “I will contact the physician immediately if I develop urinary retention.”
choices.C: “I will contact the physician immediately if I develop swallowing difficulty.”
choices.D: “I will contact the physician immediately if I develop feelings of irritability.”

PNLE5.rationale: Visual disturbance are a sign of toxicity because retinopathy can occur with this drug.

PNLE5.question: The client with an acute myocardial infarction is hospitalized for almost one week. The client experiences nausea and loss of appetite. The nurse caring for the client recognizes that these symptoms may indicate the:
PNLE5.rationale: Toxic levels of Lanoxin stimulate the medullary chemoreceptor trigger zone, resulting in nausea and subsequent anorexia.

PNLE5.question: A client with a partial occlusion of the left common carotid artery is scheduled for discharge. The client is still receiving Coumadin. The nurse provided a discharge instruction to the client regarding adverse effects of Coumadin. The nurse should tell the client to consult with the physician if:
PNLE5.rationale: Warfarin derivatives cause an increase in the prothrombin time and INR, leading to an increased risk for bleeding. Any abnormal or excessive bleeding must be reported, because it may indicate toxic levels of the drug.

PNLE5.question: Levodopa is ordered for a client with Parkinson’s disease. Before starting the medication, the nurse should know that:

choices.A: Levodopa is inadequately absorbed if given with meals.
choices.B: Levodopa may cause the side effects of orthostatic hypotension.
choices.C: Levodopa must be monitored by weekly laboratory tests.
choices.D: Levodopa causes an initial euphoria followed by depression.

PNLE5.rationale: Levodopa is the metabolic precursor of dopamine. It reduces sympathetic outflow by limiting vasoconstriction, which may result in orthostatic hypotension.

PNLE5.question: In making a diagnosis of myasthenia gravis Edrophonium HCI (Tensilon) is used. The nurse knows that this drug will cause a temporary increase in:
PNLE5.rationale: Tensilon, an anticholinesterase drug, causes temporary relief of symptoms of myasthenia gravis in client who have the disease and is therefore an effective diagnostic aid.

PNLE5.question: The nurse can determine the effectiveness of carbamazepine (Tegretol) in the management of trigeminal neuralgia by monitoring the client’s:
PNLE5.rationale: Carbamazepine ( Tegretol) is administered to control pain by reducing the transmission of nerve impulses in clients with trigeminal neuralgia.

PNLE5.question: Administration of potassium iodide solution is ordered to the client who will undergo a subtotal thyroidectomy. The nurse understands that this medication is given to:

choices.A: blate the cells of the thyroid gland that produce T4.
choices.B: ecrease the total basal metabolic rate.
choices.C: ecrease the size and vascularity of the thyroid.
choices.D: Maintain function of the parathyroid gland.

PNLE5.rationale: Potassium iodide, which aids in decreasing the vascularity of the thyroid gland, decreases the risk for hemorrhage.

PNLE5.question: A client with Addison’s disease is scheduled for discharge. Before the discharge, the physician prescribes hydrocortisone and fludrocortisone. The nurse expects the hydrocortisone to:

choices.A: Increase amounts of angiotensin II to raise the client’s blood pressure.
choices.B: ontrol excessive loss of potassium salts.
choices.C: Prevent hypoglycemia and permit the client to respond to stress.

PNLE5.rationale: Hydrocortisone is a glucocorticoid that has anti-inflammatory action and aids in metabolism of carbohydrate, fat, and protein, causing elevation of blood glucose. Thus it enables the body to adapt to stress.

PNLE5.question: A client with diabetes insipidus is taking Desmopressin acetate (DDAVP). To determine if the drug is effective, the nurse should monitor the client’s:
PNLE5.rationale: DDAVP replaces the ADH, facilitating reabsorption of water and consequent return of normal urine output and thirst.

PNLE5.question: A client with recurrent urinary tract infections is to be discharged. The client will be taking nitrofurantoin (Macrobid) 50 mg po every evening at home. The nurse provides discharge instructions to the client. Which of the following instructions will be correct?

choices.A: Strain urine for crystals and stones
choices.C: Stop the drug if the urinary output increases
choices.D: Maintain the exact time schedule for drug taking.

PNLE5.rationale: To prevent crystal formation, the client should have sufficient intake to produce 1000 to 1500 mL of urine daily while taking this drug.

PNLE5.question: A client with cancer of the lung is receiving chemotherapy. The physician orders antibiotic therapy for the client. The nurse understands that chemotherapy destroys rapidly growing leukocytes in the:
PNLE5.rationale: Prolonged chemotherapy may slow the production of leukocytes in bone marrow, thus suppressing the activity of the immune system. Antibiotics may be required to help counter infections that the body can no longer handle easily.

PNLE5.question: The physician reduced the client’s Dexamethasone (Decadron) dosage gradually and to continue a lower maintenance dosage. The client asks the nurse about the change of dosage. The nurse explains to the client that the purpose of gradual dosage reduction is to allow:

choices.A: Return of cortisone production by the adrenal glands.
choices.B: Production of antibodies by the immune system
choices.C: uilding of glycogen and protein stores in liver and muscle
choices.D: Time to observe for return of increases intracranial pressure

PNLE5.rationale: Any hormone normally produced by the body must be withdrawn slowly to allow the appropriate organ to adjust and resume production.

PNLE5.question: The nurse is assigned to care for a client with diarrhea. Excessive fluid loss is expected. The nurse is aware that fluid deficit can most accurately be assessed by:
PNLE5.rationale: Dehydration is most readily and accurately measured by serial assessment of body weight; 1 L of fluid weighs 2.2 pounds.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following is the most important electrolyte of intracellular fluid?
PNLE5.rationale: The concentration of potassium is greater inside the cell and is important in establishing a membrane potential, a critical factor in the cell’s ability to function.

PNLE5.question: Which of the following client has a high risk for developing hyperkalemia?
PNLE5.rationale: The kidneys normally eliminate potassium from the body; hyperkalemia may necessitate dialysis.

PNLE5.question: The nurse is reviewing the laboratory result of the client. The client’s serum potassium level is 5.8 mEq/L. Which of the following is the initial nursing action?

choices.A: all the cardiac arrest team to alert them
choices.B: all the laboratory and repeat the test
choices.C: Take the client’s vital signs and notify the physician
choices.D: Obtain an ECG strip and have lidocaine available

PNLE5.rationale: Vital signs monitor cardiorespiratory status; hyperkalemia causes serious cardiac dysrhythmias.

PNLE5.question: Potassium chloride, 20 mEq, is ordered and to be added in the IV solution of a client in a diabetic ketoacidosis. The primary reason for administering this drug is:
PNLE5.rationale: Once treatment with insulin for diabetic ketoacidosis is begun, potassium ions reenter the cell, causing hypokalemia; therefore potassium, along with the replacement fluid, is generally supplied.

PNLE5.question: A female client is brought to the emergency unit. The client is complaining of abdominal cramps. On assessment, client is experiencing anorexia and weight is reduced. The physician’s diagnosis is colitis. Which of the following symptoms of fluid and electrolyte imbalance should the nurse report immediately?

choices.B: evelopment of tetaniy with muscles spasms
choices.D: Nausea, vomiting, and leg and stomach cramps.

PNLE5.rationale: Potassium, the major intracellular cation, functions with sodium and calcium to regulate neuromuscular activity and contraction of muscle fibers, particularly the heart muscle. In hypokalemia these symptoms develop.

PNLE5.question: The client is to receive an IV piggyback medication. When preparing the medication the nurse should be aware that it is very important to:

choices.B: Use exactly 100mL of fluid to mix the medication
choices.C: hange the needle just before adding the medication
choices.D: Rotate the bag after adding the medication

PNLE5.rationale: Because IV solutions enter the body’s internal environment, all solutions and medications utilizing this route must be sterile to prevent the introduction of microbes.

PNLE5.question: The nurse is reviewing the laboratory result of the client. An arterial blood gas report indicates the client’s pH is 7.20, PCO2 35 mmHg and HCO3 is 19 mEq/L. The results are consistent with:
PNLE5.rationale: A low pH and bicarbonate level are consistent with metabolic acidosis.

PNLE1.question: Which element in the circular chain of infection can be eliminated by preserving skin integrity?
PNLE1.rationale: In the circular chain of infection, pathogens must be able to leave their reservoir and be transmitted to a susceptible host through a portal of entry, such as broken skin.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following will probably result in a break in sterile technique for respiratory isolation?

choices.A: Opening the patient’s window to the outside environment
choices.B: Turning on the patient’s room ventilator
choices.C: Opening the door of the patient’s room leading into the hospital corridor
choices.D: Failing to wear gloves when administering a bed bath

PNLE1.rationale: Respiratory isolation, like strict isolation, requires that the door to the door patient’s room remain closed. However, the patient’s room should be well ventilated, so opening the window or turning on the ventricular is desirable. The nurse does not need to wear gloves for respiratory isolation, but good hand washing is important for all types of isolation.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following patients is at greater risk for contracting an infection?

choices.C: postoperative patient who has undergone orthopedic surgery

PNLE1.rationale: Leukopenia is a decreased number of leukocytes (white blood cells), which are important in resisting infection. None of the other situations would put the patient at risk for contracting an infection; taking broadspectrum antibiotics might actually reduce the infection risk.

PNLE1.question: Effective hand washing requires the use of:

choices.A: Soap or detergent to promote emulsification

PNLE1.rationale: Soaps and detergents are used to help remove bacteria because of their ability to lower the surface tension of water and act as emulsifying agents. Hot water may lead to skin irritation or burns.

PNLE1.question: After routine patient contact, hand washing should last at least:
PNLE1.rationale: Depending on the degree of exposure to pathogens, hand washing may last from 10 seconds to 4 minutes. After routine patient contact, hand washing for 30 seconds effectively minimizes the risk of pathogen transmission.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following procedures always requires surgical asepsis?
PNLE1.rationale: The urinary system is normally free of microorganisms except at the urinary meatus. Any procedure that involves entering this system must use surgically aseptic measures to maintain a bacteria-free state.

PNLE1.question: Sterile technique is used whenever:
PNLE1.rationale: All invasive procedures, including surgery, catheter insertion, and administration of parenteral therapy, require sterile technique to maintain a sterile environment. All equipment must be sterile, and the nurse and the physician must wear sterile gloves and maintain surgical asepsis. In the operating room, the nurse and physician are required to wear sterile gowns, gloves, masks, hair covers, and shoe covers for all invasive procedures. Strict isolation requires the use of clean gloves, masks, gowns and equipment to prevent the transmission of highly communicable diseases by contact or by airborne routes. Terminal disinfection is the disinfection of all contaminated supplies and equipment after a patient has been discharged to prepare them for reuse by another patient. The purpose of protective (reverse) isolation is to prevent a person with seriously impaired resistance from coming into contact who potentially pathogenic organisms.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following constitutes a break in sterile technique while preparing a sterile field for a dressing change?

choices.A: Using sterile forceps, rather than sterile gloves, to handle a sterile item
choices.B: Touching the outside wrapper of sterilized material without sterile gloves
choices.C: Placing a sterile object on the edge of the sterile field
choices.D: Pouring out a small amount of solution (15 to 30 ml) before pouring the solution into a sterile container

PNLE1.rationale: The edges of a sterile field are considered contaminated. When sterile items are allowed to come in contact with the edges of the field, the sterile items also become contaminated.

PNLE1.question: A natural body defense that plays an active role in preventing infection is:
PNLE1.rationale: Hair on or within body areas, such as the nose, traps and holds particles that contain microorganisms. Yawning and hiccupping do not prevent microorganisms from entering or leaving the body. Rapid eye movement marks the stage of sleep during which dreaming occurs.

PNLE1.question: All of the following statement are true about donning sterile gloves except:

choices.A: The first glove should be picked up by grasping the inside of the cuff.
choices.B: The second glove should be picked up by inserting the gloved fingers under the cuff outside the glove.
choices.C: The gloves should be adjusted by sliding the gloved fingers under the sterile cuff and pulling the glove over the wrist
choices.D: The inside of the glove is considered sterile

PNLE1.rationale: The inside of the glove is always considered to be clean, but not sterile.

PNLE1.question: When removing a contaminated gown, the nurse should be careful that the first thing she touches is the:

choices.A: Waist tie and neck tie at the back of the gown
choices.B: Waist tie in front of the gown

PNLE1.rationale: The back of the gown is considered clean, the front is contaminated. So, after removing gloves and washing hands, the nurse should untie the back of the gown; slowly move backward away from the gown, holding the inside of the gown and keeping the edges off the floor; turn and fold the gown inside out; discard it in a contaminated linen container; then wash her hands again.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following nursing interventions is considered the most effective form or universal precautions?

choices.A: ap all used needles before removing them from their syringes
choices.B: iscard all used uncapped needles and syringes in an impenetrable protective container
choices.C: Wear gloves when administering IM injections

PNLE1.rationale: According to the Centers for Disease Control (CDC), blood-to-blood contact occurs most commonly when a health care worker attempts to cap a used needle. Therefore, used needles should never be recapped; instead they should be inserted in a specially designed puncture resistant, labeled container. Wearing gloves is not always necessary when administering an I.M. injection. Enteric precautions prevent the transfer of pathogens via feces.

PNLE1.question: All of the following measures are recommended to prevent pressure ulcers except:

choices.A: Massaging the reddened are with lotion
choices.B: Using a water or air mattress
choices.C: dhering to a schedule for positioning and turning

PNLE1.rationale: Nurses and other health care professionals previously believed that massaging a reddened area with lotion would promote venous return and reduce edema to the area. However, research has shown that massage only increases the likelihood of cellular ischemia and necrosis to the area.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following blood tests should be performed before a blood transfusion?

choices.D: omplete blood count (CBC) and electrolyte levels.

PNLE1.rationale: Before a blood transfusion is performed, the blood of the donor and recipient must be checked for compatibility. This is done by blood typing (a test that determines a person’s blood type) and cross-matching (a procedure that determines the compatibility of the donor’s and recipient’s blood after the blood types has been matched). If the blood specimens are incompatible, hemolysis and antigen-antibody reactions will occur.

PNLE1.question: The primary purpose of a platelet count is to evaluate the:
PNLE1.rationale: Platelets are disk-shaped cells that are essential for blood coagulation. A platelet count determines the number of thrombocytes in blood available for promoting hemostasis and assisting with blood coagulation after injury. It also is used to evaluate the patient’s potential for bleeding; however, this is not its primary purpose. The normal count ranges from 150,000 to 350,000/mm3. A count of 100,000/mm3 or less indicates a potential for bleeding; count of less than 20,000/mm3 is associated with spontaneous bleeding.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following white blood cell (WBC) counts clearly indicates leukocytosis?
PNLE1.rationale: Leukocytosis is any transient increase in the number of white blood cells (leukocytes) in the blood. Normal WBC counts range from 5,000 to 100,000/mm3. Thus, a count of 25,000/mm3 indicates leukocytosis.

PNLE1.question: After 5 days of diuretic therapy with 20mg of furosemide (Lasix) daily, a patient begins to exhibit fatigue, muscle cramping and muscle weakness. These symptoms probably indicate that the patient is experiencing:
PNLE1.rationale: Fatigue, muscle cramping, and muscle weaknesses are symptoms of hypokalemia (an inadequate potassium level), which is a potential side effect of diuretic therapy. The physician usually orders supplemental potassium to prevent hypokalemia in patients receiving diuretics. Anorexia is another symptom of hypokalemia. Dysphagia means difficulty swallowing.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following statements about chest X-ray is false?

choices.A: No contradictions exist for this test
choices.B: efore the procedure, the patient should remove all jewelry, metallic objects, and buttons above the waist
choices.D: Eating, drinking, and medications are allowed before this test

PNLE1.rationale: Pregnancy or suspected pregnancy is the only contraindication for a chest X-ray. However, if a chest X-ray is necessary, the patient can wear a lead apron to protect the pelvic region from radiation. Jewelry, metallic objects, and buttons would interfere with the X-ray and thus should not be worn above the waist. A signed consent is not required because a chest X-ray is not an invasive examination. Eating, drinking and medications are allowed because the X-ray is of the chest, not the abdominal region.

PNLE1.question: The most appropriate time for the nurse to obtain a sputum specimen for culture is:

choices.B: fter the patient eats a light breakfast

PNLE1.rationale: Obtaining a sputum specimen early in this morning ensures an adequate supply of bacteria for culturing and decreases the risk of contamination from food or medication.

PNLE1.question: A patient with no known allergies is to receive penicillin every 6 hours. When administering the medication, the nurse observes a fine rash on the patient’s skin. The most appropriate nursing action would be to:

choices.A: Withhold the moderation and notify the physician
choices.B: dminister the medication and notify the physician
choices.C: dminister the medication with an antihistamine
choices.D: pply corn starch soaks to the rash

PNLE1.rationale: Initial sensitivity to penicillin is commonly manifested by a skin rash, even in individuals who have not been allergic to it previously. Because of the danger of anaphylactic shock, he nurse should withhold the drug and notify the physician, who may choose to substitute another drug. Administering an antihistamine is a dependent nursing intervention that requires a written physician’s order. Although applying corn starch to the rash may relieve discomfort, it is not the nurse’s top priority in such a potentially life-threatening situation.

PNLE1.question: All of the following nursing interventions are correct when using the Ztrack method of drug injection except:

choices.A: Prepare the injection site with alcohol
choices.B: Use a needle that’s a least 1” long
choices.D: Rub the site vigorously after the injection to promote absorption

PNLE1.rationale: The Z-track method is an I.M. injection technique in which the patient’s skin is pulled in such a way that the needle track is sealed off after the injection. This procedure seals medication deep into the muscle, thereby minimizing skin staining and irritation. Rubbing the injection site is contraindicated because it may cause the medication to extravasate into the skin.

PNLE1.question: The correct method for determining the vastus lateralis site for I.M. injection is to:

choices.A: Locate the upper aspect of the upper outer quadrant of the buttock about 5 to 8 cm below the iliac crest
choices.B: Palpate the lower edge of the acromion process and the midpoint lateral aspect of the arm
choices.C: Palpate a 1” circular area anterior to the umbilicus
choices.D: ivide the area between the greater femoral trochanter and the lateral femoral condyle into thirds, and select the middle third on the anterior of the thigh

PNLE1.rationale: The vastus lateralis, a long, thick muscle that extends the full length of the thigh, is viewed by many clinicians as the site of choice for I.M. injections because it has relatively few major nerves and blood vessels. The middle third of the muscle is recommended as the injection site. The patient can be in a supine or sitting position for an injection into this site.

PNLE1.question: The mid-deltoid injection site is seldom used for I.M. injections because it:

choices.A: an accommodate only 1 ml or less of medication
choices.C: an be used only when the patient is lying down

PNLE1.rationale: The mid-deltoid injection site can accommodate only 1 ml or less of medication because of its size and location (on the deltoid muscle of the arm, close to the brachial artery and radial nerve).

PNLE1.question: The appropriate needle size for insulin injection is:
PNLE1.rationale: A 25G, 5/8” needle is the recommended size for insulin injection because insulin is administered by the subcutaneous route. An 18G, 1 ½” needle is usually used for I.M. injections in children, typically in the vastus lateralis. A 22G, 1 ½” needle is usually used for adult I.M. injections, which are typically administered in the vastus lateralis or ventrogluteal site.

PNLE1.question: The appropriate needle gauge for intradermal injection is:
PNLE1.rationale: Because an intradermal injection does not penetrate deeply into the skin, a small-bore 25G needle is recommended. This type of injection is used primarily to administer antigens to evaluate reactions for allergy or sensitivity studies. A 20G needle is usually used for I.M. injections of oilbased medications; a 22G needle for I.M. injections; and a 25G needle, for I.M. injections; and a 25G needle, for subcutaneous insulin injections.

PNLE1.question: Parenteral penicillin can be administered as an:

choices.A: IM injection or an IV solution

PNLE1.rationale: Parenteral penicillin can be administered I.M. or added to a solution and given I.V. It cannot be administered subcutaneously or intradermally.

PNLE1.question: The physician orders gr 10 of aspirin for a patient. The equivalent dose in milligrams is:
PNLE1.rationale: gr 10 x 60mg/gr 1 = 600 mg

PNLE1.question: 6 mg 10 mg 60 mg 600 mg
PNLE1.rationale: 100ml/60 min X 15 gtt/ 1 ml = 25 gtt/minute

PNLE1.question: The physician orders an IV solution of dextrose 5% in water at 100ml/hour. What would the flow rate be if the drop factor is 15 gtt = 1 ml?
PNLE1.rationale: Hemoglobinuria, the abnormal presence of hemoglobin in the urine, indicates a hemolytic reaction (incompatibility of the donor’s and recipient’s blood). In this reaction, antibodies in the recipient’s plasma combine rapidly with donor RBC’s; the cells are hemolyzed in either circulatory or reticuloendothelial system. Hemolysis occurs more rapidly in ABO incompatibilities than in Rh incompatibilities. Chest pain and urticaria may be symptoms of impending anaphylaxis. Distended neck veins are an indication of hypervolemia.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following is a sign or symptom of a hemolytic reaction to blood transfusion?
PNLE1.rationale: In real failure, the kidney loses their ability to effectively eliminate wastes and fluids. Because of this, limiting the patient’s intake of oral and I.V. fluids may be necessary. Fever, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, and dehydration are conditions for which fluids should be encouraged.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following conditions may require fluid restriction?
PNLE1.rationale: Phlebitis, the inflammation of a vein, can be caused by chemical irritants (I.V. solutions or medications), mechanical irritants (the needle or catheter used during venipuncture or cannulation), or a localized allergic reaction to the needle or catheter. Signs and symptoms of phlebitis include pain or discomfort, edema and heat at the I.V. insertion site, and a red streak going up the arm or leg from the I.V. insertion site.

PNLE1.question: All of the following are common signs and symptoms of phlebitis except:

choices.A: Pain or discomfort at the IV insertion site
choices.B: Edema and warmth at the IV insertion site
choices.C: red streak exiting the IV insertion site
choices.D: Frank bleeding at the insertion site

PNLE1.rationale: Return demonstration provides the most certain evidence for evaluating the effectiveness of patient teaching.

PNLE1.question: The best way of determining whether a patient has learned to instill ear medication properly is for the nurse to:

choices.A: sk the patient if he/she has used ear drops before
choices.B: Have the patient repeat the nurse’s instructions using her own words
choices.C: emonstrate the procedure to the patient and encourage to ask questions
choices.D: sk the patient to demonstrate the procedure

PNLE1.rationale: Capsules, enteric-coated tablets, and most extended duration or sustained release products should not be dissolved for use in a gastrostomy tube. They are pharmaceutically manufactured in these forms for valid reasons, and altering them destroys their purpose. The nurse should seek an alternate physician’s order when an ordered medication is inappropriate for delivery by tube.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following types of medications can be administered via gastrostomy tube?

choices.B: apsules whole contents are dissolve in water
choices.C: Enteric-coated tablets that are thoroughly dissolved in water
choices.D: Most tablets designed for oral use, except for extended-duration compounds

PNLE1.rationale: A drug-allergy is an adverse reaction resulting from an immunologic response following a previous sensitizing exposure to the drug. The reaction can range from a rash or hives to anaphylactic shock. Tolerance to a drug means that the patient experiences a decreasing physiologic response to repeated administration of the drug in the same dosage. Idiosyncrasy is an individual’s unique hypersensitivity to a drug, food, or other substance; it appears to be genetically determined. Synergism, is a drug interaction in which the sum of the drug’s combined effects is greater than that of their separate effects.

PNLE1.question: A patient who develops hives after receiving an antibiotic is exhibiting drug:
PNLE1.rationale: A hemoglobin and hematocrit count would be ordered by the physician if bleeding were suspected. The other answers are appropriate nursing interventions for a patient who has undergone femoral arteriography.

PNLE1.question: A patient has returned to his room after femoral arteriography. All of the following are appropriate nursing interventions except:

choices.A: ssess femoral, popliteal, and pedal pulses every 15 minutes for 2 hours
choices.B: heck the pressure dressing for sanguineous drainage
choices.C: ssess a vital signs every 15 minutes for 2 hours
choices.D: Order a hemoglobin and hematocrit count 1 hour after the arteriography

PNLE1.rationale: Coughing, a protective response that clears the respiratory tract of irritants, usually is involuntary; however it can be voluntary, as when a patient is taught to perform coughing exercises. An antitussive drug inhibits coughing. Splinting the abdomen supports the abdominal muscles when a patient coughs.

PNLE1.question: The nurse explains to a patient that a cough:

choices.A: Is a protective response to clear the respiratory tract of irritants
choices.C: Is induced by the administration of an antitussive drug
choices.D: an be inhibited by “splinting” the abdomen

PNLE1.rationale: In an infected patient, shivering results from the body’s attempt to increase heat production and the production of neutrophils and phagocytotic action through increased skeletal muscle tension and contractions. Initial vasoconstriction may cause skin to feel cold to the touch. Applying additional bed clothes helps to equalize the body temperature and stop the chills. Attempts to cool the body result in further shivering, increased metabloism, and thus increased heat production.

PNLE1.question: An infected patient has chills and begins shivering. The best nursing intervention is to:
PNLE1.rationale: A clinical nurse specialist must have completed a master’s degree in a clinical specialty and be a registered professional nurse. The National League of Nursing accredits educational programs in nursing and provides a testing service to evaluate student nursing competence but it does not certify nurses. The American Nurses Association identifies requirements for certification and offers examinations for certification in many areas of nursing., such as medical surgical nursing. These certification (credentialing) demonstrates that the nurse has the knowledge and the ability to provide high quality nursing care in the area of her certification. A graduate of an associate degree program is not a clinical nurse specialist: however, she is prepared to provide bed side nursing with a high degree of knowledge and skill. She must successfully complete the licensing examination to become a registered professional nurse.

PNLE1.question: A clinical nurse specialist is a nurse who has:

choices.A: een certified by the National League for Nursing
choices.B: Received credentials from the Philippine Nurses’ Association
choices.C: Graduated from an associate degree program and is a registered professional nurse
choices.D: ompleted a master’s degree in the prescribed clinical area and is a registered professional nurse.

PNLE1.rationale: Bile colors the stool brown. Any inflammation or obstruction that impairs bile flow will affect the stool pigment, yielding light, clay-colored stool. Upper GI bleeding results in black or tarry stool. Constipation is characterized by small, hard masses. Many medications and foods will discolor stool – for example, drugs containing iron turn stool black.; beets turn stool red.

PNLE1.question: Clay colored stools indicate:
PNLE1.rationale: In the evaluation step of the nursing process, the nurse must decide whether the patient has achieved the expected outcome that was identified in the planning phase.

PNLE1.question: In which step of the nursing process would the nurse ask a patient if the medication she administered relieved his pain?
PNLE1.rationale: The main sources of vitamin A are yellow and green vegetables (such as carrots, sweet potatoes, squash, spinach, collard greens, broccoli, and cabbage) and yellow fruits (such as apricots, and cantaloupe). Animal sources include liver, kidneys, cream, butter, and egg yolks.

PNLE1.rationale: Maintaing the drainage tubing and collection bag level with the patient’s bladder could result in reflux of urine into the kidney. Irrigating the bladder with Neosporin and clamping the catheter for 1 hour every 4 hours must be prescribed by a physician.

PNLE1.question: Which of the following is a primary nursing intervention necessary for all patients with a Foley Catheter in place?

choices.A: Maintain the drainage tubing and collection bag level with the patient’s bladder
choices.B: Irrigate the patient with 1% Neosporin solution three times a daily
choices.C: lamp the catheter for 1 hour every 4 hours to maintain the bladder’s elasticity
choices.D: Maintain the drainage tubing and collection bag below bladder level to facilitate drainage by gravity

PNLE1.rationale: The ELISA test of venous blood is used to assess blood and potential blood donors to human immunodeficiency virus (HIV). A positive ELISA test combined with various signs and symptoms helps to diagnose acquired immunodeficiency syndrome (AIDS)

PNLE1.question: The ELISA test is used to:

choices.A: Screen blood donors for antibodies to human immunodeficiency virus (HIV)
choices.B: Test blood to be used for transfusion for HIV antibodies
choices.C: id in diagnosing a patient with AIDS

PNLE1.rationale: Tachypnea (an abnormally rapid rate of breathing) would indicate that the patient was still hypoxic (deficient in oxygen).The partial pressures of arterial oxygen and carbon dioxide listed are within the normal range. Eupnea refers to normal respiration.
